articles.title: Perioperative pupillary abnormalities: A systematic review of published cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unexpected perioperative pupillary abnormalities may reflect benign perioperative effects or life-threatening neurologic and ophthalmic emergencies. However, evidence is largely limited to isolated case reports, providing little guidance for perioperative clinicians.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and CNKI were systematically searched for case reports and case series describing perioperative pupillary abnormalities. Clinical characteristics, suspected mechanisms, management strategies and outcomes were summarised. Reporting quality was assessed using adapted Joanna Briggs Institute appraisal items.
RESULTS: Fifty-three articles describing 58 patients were included. Mydriasis and anisocoria were the predominant findings. Position-related, pharmacological and regional anaesthesia-related mechanisms were most frequently reported, although serious neurologic causes also occurred. Most patients recovered completely, although serious pathology occurred in 15.5% of cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative pupillary abnormalities arise from diverse mechanisms ranging from benign transient phenomena to neurologic emergencies. The proposed structured bedside approach may assist perioperative practitioners in timely assessment and management of unexpected pupillary abnormalities.

articles.title: Consent for intensive care research involving adults who lack decision-making capacity: A jurisdictional analysis of Australia's fragmented framework.
articles.abstract: Critically ill adults frequently cannot consent to research because of sedation, delirium, shock or mechanical ventilation, yet safe intensive care depends on evidence generated in this population; several treatments once regarded as standard care proved harmful when finally tested in randomised trials. The ethical framework for enrolling adults who lack decision-making capacity is national-the National Health and Medical Research Council National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research (2025), in effect since 23 June 2026-but legal authority for substitute consent is conferred by eight state and territory statutes that differ in terminology, in decision-maker hierarchies, in whether they address research at all, and whether they permit enrolment in an emergency. Mapping four representative study archetypes across all eight jurisdictions shows that the lawful basis for enrolling the same patient shifts with study design as much as with geography; differing statutory definitions, tribunal involvement and the transition to the 2025 National Statement produce material and avoidable inconsistency. Contemporary Australian intensive care trials show that practice has converged on the National Statement while the underlying legislation has not; the resulting inconsistency risks inequity, underrepresentation of critically ill patients, and bias in the evidence generated. We set out principles for reform (Box 1): nationally consistent framing of substitute consent for research-common terminology and legal principles, an explicit emergency-research pathway in every jurisdiction, and consistent interpretation within each jurisdiction-developed with consumers and with the clinicians and clinical research nurses who obtain consent, and taken forward with formal endorsement from the relevant professional bodies.

articles.title: Impact of ventilation strategy during the transition phase of ARDS: Synchronized vs. non-synchronized pressure-regulated vs. volume-controlled mode - A randomized crossover study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is limited data on the optimal ventilation strategy during the transition phase of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) when spontaneous breathing is resumed and lung recovery is ongoing. Volume assist-control ventilation (ACVVol) is commonly used, but the constant inspiratory flow and the pressurization synchronized to patient effort may have some disadvantages during this phase. Pressure Regulated Volume Control (PRVC) and Pressure-Controlled ventilation with non-synchronized Spontaneous Ventilation (PC-SV) have been proposed to reduce lung stress and increase respiratory variability. This study aimed to compare the physiological effects of ACVVol, PRVC, and PC-SV during the transition phase, focusing on gas exchange, ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) risk, and respiratory variability.
METHODS: In this prospective crossover study, ACVVol, PRVC, and PC-SV were applied for three 45-minute periods in a randomized order once spontaneous ventilation reached 20-30% of minute ventilation in PC-SV. Ventilator settings ensured similar positive end-expiratory pressure, tidal volume (VT), and respiratory rate (RR) across modes. Gas exchange, hemodynamics, airway and esophageal pressures, electrical impedance tomography (EIT) volume distribution, dyspnea (MV-RDOS), pressure-time product (PTP) and VT, RR and PTP variability were measured.
RESULTS: Nineteen patients completed the study. Sedation level, total RR and VT did not differ between ACVVol, PRVC and PC-SV. Gas exchange, MV-RDOS score, PTP and transpulmonary, alveolar and transalveolar pressure showed no significant differences among the three modes. No differences in ventilation distribution or Pendelluft were observed. VT variability was however significantly higher in PC-SV than in ACVVol and PRVC, and PTP variability was higher in PC-SV than in ACVVol. RR variability did not differ among the three modes.
CONCLUSIONS: During the transition phase of ARDS, neither synchronized nor non-synchronized pressure-regulated modes affect gas exchange, dyspnea, or inspiratory effort compared to volume-controlled mode. Similarly, transpulmonary, alveolar, and transalveolar pressures, as well as ventilation distribution, do not differ among the three modes. However, VT and respiratory effort variabilities are higher in the non-synchronized pressure mode.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier: NCT04196738. Registered on June 30, 2020.

articles.title: Determinants of quadriceps responsiveness to neuromuscular electrical stimulation in mechanically ventilated patients at risk of intensive care unit - acquired weakness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) may reduce intensive care unit - acquired weakness (ICU-aw). However, current protocols and patient's responses remain heterogeneous. Identifying the determinants of muscle responsiveness could help optimize NMES strategies in patients at risk of developing ICU-aw.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study is a secondary analysis of DETECT study (NCT04722445). On the first day deemed feasible, each critically ill patient receiving mechanical ventilation underwent quadriceps electrical stimulation aimed at eliciting a knee extension with heel lifted, concomitantly with ultrasound assessment of the quadriceps muscle. US quadriceps images were collected to analyse pennation angle, thickness and echogenicity of the rectus femoris (RF) muscle and skin to RF distance. We also analysed all anthropometric variables and ICU pathway determinants that could impact quadriceps responsiveness.
RESULTS: Among the 75 patients included in the analysis, 29 (39%) were classified as NMES non-responders (maximum stimulation intensity reached without achieving knee extension, with heel lifted: 120 mA). The 46 NMES responders (61%) required a median stimulation intensity of 72.8 [61.5-91] mA. NMES non-responders had greater RF thickness (1.5 (0.6) vs. 1.2 (0.4) cm; p = 0.01), higher BMI (30 [25.5-32.1] vs. 24.8 [21.9-29.5] kg/m2; p = 0.01), higher fluid accumulation (6.5 [2-8] vs. 1 [-1.5-2.5] kg; p < 0.001) and SOFA scores at admission (7 [6-10] vs. 6 [4-7]; p = 0.01). In the NMES non-responders, a larger proportion were diabetic than in the NMES responders (20.7% vs. 4.4%; p = 0.03) and the sepsis rate was also higher (34.5% vs 6.7%; p = 0.002). Aminoglycoside exposure (41.4% vs. 4.4%; p < 0.001) and vasopressor dose (0.2 [0-0.4] vs. 0 [0-0.2] µg/kg/min; p = 0.05) were also higher in non-responders. After multivariable analysis, only fluid accumulation remained associated with NMES non-responsiveness (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.04-1.63; p = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Fluid accumulation could decrease quadriceps excitability during NMES in critically ill patients. RF thickness, BMI, diabetes, illness severity, sepsis, exposure to aminoglycosides, and vasopressor doses could also decrease quadriceps responsiveness but further research is needed to determine the actual impact of these factors.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine as an Adjuvant to Local Anesthetics for Postoperative Analgesia in Breast Cancer Surgery.
articles.abstract: Postoperative pain after breast cancer surgery remains an important clinical issue, particularly after mastectomy and axillary procedures. Dexmedetomidine has been studied as an adjuvant to local anesthetics with the aim of prolonging regional analgesia and reducing rescue opioid requirements. This narrative review summarizes clinical evidence from pectoral, paravertebral, serratus anterior plane, erector spinae plane, thoracic interfascial, and infiltration techniques. Most studies report longer analgesia and lower postoperative analgesic consumption when dexmedetomidine is added to a local anesthetic. However, comparison between studies is limited by differences in block technique, local anesthetic formulation, dexmedetomidine dose, and outcome assessment. Doses of 0.5-1 μg/kg have been most commonly investigated. Although the available evidence supports an adjunctive analgesic benefit, bradycardia and hypotension remain relevant safety concerns. Perineural and interfascial administration as a local anesthetic adjunct remains off-label in settings where dexmedetomidine is licensed for intravenous use. At present, dexmedetomidine appears more appropriate as a selective adjunct than as a routine component of all breast surgery analgesic protocols.

articles.title: Effect of Triamcinolone-Infused Nasal Packing on Postoperative Results in Nasal Surgeries.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The common goal of all rhinology surgeons is to achieve excellent hemostasis and good postoperative healing while avoiding adhesion formation and preventing infection. A well-healed sinus cavity is a known determinant of a successful outcome after sinus surgery. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of triamcinolone acetate-impregnated nasal packing in preventing or reducing postoperative complications in various nasal surgeries.
METHODS: This is a prospective, randomized, double-blinded study conducted on 90 patients who fulfilled the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Triamcinolone-impregnated Merocel packing was placed in one nasal cavity and saline-soaked packing in the other cavity after nasal surgery. Postoperative outcomes were measured using the 22-item Sinonasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) score, Nasal Obstruction Symptom Evaluation (NOSE) score, perioperative sinus endoscopy (POSE) score, and Lund-Kennedy score (LKS) at one, four, eight, and 12 weeks postoperatively. P values were calculated using paired t-tests.
RESULTS: The male-to-female ratio was 1:0.6. We found statistically significant improvements in the SNOT-22 and NOSE scores postoperatively (p < 0.001), which suggested an improved quality of life in our study subjects. A gradual improvement (p < 0.001) was noted in both POSE and LKS scores on the triamcinolone-treated side at all follow-up visits in patients who underwent sinus surgery.
CONCLUSION: Improved postoperative SNOT-22 and NOSE scores underscore the positive impact of triamcinolone on postoperative quality of life after nasal surgery. Objective endoscopic assessment revealed sustained and significant reductions in both POSE and LKS scores, which suggest that triamcinolone-impregnated nasal packing may serve as an effective adjunct in postoperative nasal care after sinus surgery, with the potential to improve both short-term recovery and quality of life in terms of postoperative pain perception.

articles.title: Postoperative acute kidney injury following cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: integration of circadian rhythm and anesthetic factors to develop and validate a predictive model at 7 days.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To predict postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) surgery, we developed and validated a nomogram incorporating circadian rhythms and anesthesia-related variables to assist in predicting AKI occurrence.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included clinical data from 298 patients who underwent cardiac surgery with extracorporeal circulation. All patients were randomly divided into two groups: one for model development (n = 209) and the other for internal validation (n = 89). Candidate variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Independent predictors were identified through multivariable logistic regression, and a predictive nomogram was constructed. The model's discriminatory ability, calibration performance, and clinical utility were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Among the 298 patients, 82 developed postoperative AKI, yielding an overall incidence rate of 27.52%. On multivariate logistic regression analysis, undergoing surgery in the afternoon was a protective factor (odds ratio [OR]: 0.482, P < 0.05), whereas preoperative circadian rhythm disturbance, prolonged CPB duration, and increased propofol infusion rate emerged as independent risk factors for postoperative AKI (OR: 3.081, 1.026, and 2.050, respectively; all P < 0.05). The nomogram showed satisfactory discrimination, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.796 (95% CI: 0.728-0.864) in the training set and 0.776 (95% CI: 0.671-0.881) in the validation set. After bootstrap correction with 1,000 resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.793. At the optimal cutoff point, the sensitivity and specificity for the training cohort were 0.672 and 0.815, respectively, and for the validation cohort, 0.500 and 0.831. Both the training and validation sets showed adequate calibration on the Hosmer-Lemeshow test (P = 0.754 and P = 0.364, respectively). DCA further demonstrated that the nomogram provided a net positive clinical benefit over a wide range of clinically plausible threshold probabilities.
CONCLUSION: The proposed nomogram combines chronobiological factors, anesthesia-related variables, and perfusion time during cardiac surgery. This tool shows potential as a practical means for assessing the risk of acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery, though external validation in independent multicenter cohorts is warranted before widespread clinical implementation. In clinical practice, with appropriate validation, this model may help with early risk stratification and aid in designing targeted perioperative intervention measures to reduce the risk of kidney injury in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Systolic blood pressure-adjusted stroke volume variation for intravascular volume assessment during norepinephrine infusion in elective craniotomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Stroke volume variation (SVV) is widely used in goal-directed fluid therapy but is susceptible to interference from norepinephrine (NE), which biases intravascular volume assessment. This study aimed to characterize NE-induced SVV distortion and establish a corrected SVV parameter to improve volume evaluation during NE infusion.
METHODS: A total of 55 patients undergoing elective craniotomy were divided into a training cohort (n = 35) and a validation cohort (n = 20). Patients received an intraoperative dose of 0.5 g/kg mannitol or normal saline. NE was titrated during hypervolemic and hypovolemic phases differentiated by central venous pressure and urine output. Hemodynamic variables, blood gas parameters and postoperative complications were compared. Multivariate linear regression analysis using SBP, CI, SV, and NE dosage as independent variables was performed to derive the corrected SVV formula (BpSVV).
RESULTS: NE titration induced a stable negative linear correlation between SBP and SVV. The regression slopes of SBP-SVV curves were comparable between groups (P = 0.495), while the intercept significantly increased in the mannitol dehydration phase (P < 0.01). SBP predominantly determined SVV variation. A novel corrected parameter (BpSVV = SVV + 0.101 × ∆SBP) was established. The AUC values of BpSVV and raw SVV were 0.9167 and 0.9531 with favorable diagnostic efficiency. Logistic regression analysis showed that preoperative GCS score was significantly associated with poor postoperative neurological prognosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Conventional SVV is markedly disturbed during titrated NE infusion. BpSVV could serve as a reliable alternative for intravascular volume assessment under such conditions.

articles.title: Association of esketamine anesthetic induction with emergence agitation in children undergoing adenoidectomy: a mediation analysis of early postoperative pain.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between documented induction esketamine use and emergence agitation in children undergoing adenoidectomy, and to quantify the extent to which early postoperative pain statistically mediates this association.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 240 children undergoing adenoidectomy under sevoflurane anesthesia. Children were grouped by documented induction esketamine (0.3 mg/kg) use. Emergence agitation was defined as a Pediatric Anesthesia Emergence Delirium (PAED) score ≥10 within 30 minutes of post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) arrival. The peak Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) score was the prespecified mediator. We performed regression, mediation, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Emergence agitation occurred in 41 (34.2%) children without esketamine and 22/120 (18.3%) with esketamine (χ2 = 7.77, P = 0.005). Esketamine was associated with lower odds of emergence agitation (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.25-0.83, P = 0.011), lower peak PAED (MD -1.88, P<0.001), lower peak FLACC (MD -1.15, P<0.001), and less rescue analgesia (OR 0.48, P = 0.037). Extubation time and PACU stay were similar. Mediation analysis indicated a significant indirect pathway through early pain, accounting for 27.2% of the total association (P = 0.002). Exploratory follow-up showed no significant between-group differences, but validated scales and chronic pain outcomes were unavailable.
CONCLUSIONS: Documented induction esketamine use was associated with less emergence agitation and lower early pain after adenoidectomy. These findings indicate non-causal statistical pathway evidence. They neither verify an N-methyl-D-aspartate-receptor mechanism nor establish an optimal dose. Prospective dose-ranging trials and validated longitudinal assessments are required.

articles.title: Clinical application of homeopathic traction reduction techniques in traumatic fractures of lower extremities.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the clinical efficacy of homeopathic traction reduction techniques in traumatic fractures of the lower extremities (hereafter lower limb fractures).
METHODS: A total of 212 patients with lower limb fractures were enrolled. The control group (n = 100) received reduction using a traction table, and the research group (n = 112) received homeopathic traction reduction. Surgical parameters, perioperative indicators, serum inflammation, oxidative stress (superoxide dismutase (SOD), malondialdehyde (MDA)), complications, function recovery (Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) - Physical Function (PROMIS PF), PROMIS - Mobility (PROMIS MOB)), pain intensity (Visual Analogue Scale (VAS): pain at rest, pain on movement), and quality of life (World Health Organization Quality of Life - BREF (WHOQOL-BREF)) were compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the research group exhibited remarkably better surgical parameters and perioperative indicators, and lower postoperative serum inflammatory markers, MDA, overall complication rates, resting pain, and movement-evoked pain; while postoperative SOD, PROMIS PF scores, PROMIS MOB scores, and WHOQOL-BREF scores were notably higher.
CONCLUSION: The homeopathic traction reduction technique has significant clinical efficacy in lower limb fractures.

articles.title: Antimicrobial stewardship and resistance in intensive care units in the UK: a prospective national audit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Principles of effective antimicrobial stewardship include prescription of empiric therapy based on the most likely causative organism, with medication review within 72 h. Adherence to best practice in UK ICUs is unknown and the aim of this study was to evaluate patient- and unit-level antimicrobial use in UK ICUs.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective national audit of antimicrobial use in adults (aged ≥ 18 y) admitted to ICUs in the UK and Isle of Man with a point-prevalence survey. Subsequently, we collected longitudinal data on review of therapy and antimicrobial resistance in a subset of patients who had commenced therapy within the previous 3 days.
RESULTS: We studied 2626 patients from 154/292 (52.7%) ICUs. Antimicrobial therapy was prescribed in 1592 (60.6%) patients. Of 2116 empiric antimicrobial orders, 1592 (75.2%) were compliant with unit-level guidelines. For non-compliant orders, 253 (12.0% of all empiric orders) were discussed with infection specialists and 69 (3.3%) provided justification for off-guidance therapy, but 202 (9.5%) were prescribed outside guidance without justification or discussion with infection specialists. Guideline-compliant review within 72 h of prescription took place in 1488/1606 (92.7%) eligible medication orders. A pre-specified stop or review date was strongly associated with antimicrobial review within 72 h (adjusted OR 9.3, 95%CI 5.4-16.2).
DISCUSSION: We have benchmarked critical care antimicrobial stewardship and guideline compliance across the UK. We recommend that pre-specified review dates are added to all prescriptions, as the most important determinant of review identified in our audit. Future work should include national stewardship audit cycles to benchmark practice and inform quality improvement initiatives.

articles.title: Patient-reported outcomes, postoperative pain and pain relief after day-case surgery (POPPY): persistent postoperative opioid use prevalence and associations.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: An increasing proportion of complex surgical procedures are being performed in the UK as day-cases, and NHS targets aim for these to encompass ≥ 75% of all surgeries. There has been limited outcome follow-up for this group of patients, particularly considering the prevalence of persistent postoperative opioid use and factors associated with its occurrence.
METHODS: Data from POPPY, a national, prospective, observational study exploring outcomes following day-case surgery in the UK, were used to estimate the prevalence of persistent postoperative opioid use at day 97 following surgery. Patient, anaesthetic and surgical factors associated with increased persistent postoperative opioid use were explored using multivariable analysis.
RESULTS: Of the 7839 initially recruited patients, 3488 (44.5%) provided details of their analgesic medication at day 97 following surgery. The prevalence of daily persistent postoperative opioid use was estimated to be 11.8% (95%CI 11.1-13.2%). Patient factors associated with daily persistent postoperative opioid use were pre-operative opioid use; opioid use at day 7; and composite pain scores (day 1, day 3 and day 7). Compared with general surgery, ENT, breast and orthopaedic surgery carried a higher risk of persistent postoperative opioid use. Patient factors associated with a reduced odds ratio of persistent postoperative opioid use were: female sex; higher composite pain score at baseline; and Index of Multiple Deprivation quintile 4. Daily persistent postoperative opioid use at day 97 following surgery was associated with reduced quality of life scores.
DISCUSSION: Daily persistent postoperative opioid use is common in the UK following day-case surgery. Patient and surgical factors that are associated with an increased risk of this outcome could be used to drive improvement in identification of at-risk patients pre-operatively and optimise postoperative prescribing pathways.

articles.title: Association between glycemic variability and postoperative delirium in elderly cardiac surgery patients: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious complication in elderly patients undergoing cardiac surgery. Glycemic variability (GV) has been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes, but its relationship with POD remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the association between GV and POD in elderly cardiac surgery patients.
METHODS: GV, quantified by the coefficient of variation, was stratified into tertiles. The primary outcome was POD occurrence. Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses evaluated the GV-POD association.
RESULTS: Among 2499 patients (mean age, 74.7 ± 6.5 years; 30.7% female), 322 (12.9%) developed POD. In the fully adjusted model, continuous GV was associated with higher odds of POD. Compared with the low GV group, only the high GV group remained independently associated with POD (OR = 1.39, 95% CI: 1.02-1.90, P = 0.035), whereas the moderate GV group was not significantly associated with POD.
CONCLUSION: High early perioperative GV was independently associated with POD in elderly patients undergoing cardiac surgery. These findings support a potential association between excessive glycemic fluctuations and POD, although further studies are needed to clarify causality and clinical implications.

articles.title: Complications and Management of Thoracic Surgery: Pertinent Information for Intensivists and Hospitalists.
articles.abstract: Thoracic surgery presents unique postoperative challenges that intensivists and hospitalists frequently encounter in both ward and intensive care settings. This review provides a practical overview of common procedures, potential complications, and evidence-based management strategies tailored to intensivists and hospitalists. Topics include the role of imaging, ventilatory support, and pain control, as well as integration with Anesthesiology, Pulmonology, Radiology, and Respiratory Therapy. Major complications and their corresponding management-such as air leaks, atelectasis, pneumonia, atrial fibrillation, bronchopleural fistula, and empyema-are discussed in detail, with emphasis on early recognition and intervention. This paper offers a concise guide for the management of postoperative thoracic surgery patients by outlining key principles most relevant to intensivists and hospitalists in daily practice.

articles.title: Sprint National Anaesthesia Project 3: A survey of perioperative medicine services for older surgical patients in Australia.
articles.abstract: Increasing numbers of older people with age-related conditions such as frailty and multimorbidity are presenting for surgical procedures, which is associated with an increased risk of postoperative complications. This study aimed to assess the provision of perioperative medicine services for older surgical patients across Australian hospitals participating in the third Sprint National Anaesthesia Project. An organisational survey was conducted involving 23 Australian hospitals, collecting data on hospital characteristics, clinical governance, preoperative assessments (including frailty, cognition, and risk of delirium), and postoperative care practices for high-risk older patients. Responses were analysed to evaluate the structure and function of perioperative services for older surgical patients. Twenty-one hospitals completed the survey. Preoperative assessments of older surgical patients were predominantly nurse- or anaesthetist-led, with limited geriatrician involvement. Routine preoperative screening of frailty and cognition was rare, and there was significant variability in approaches to the assessment of postoperative delirium. The survey highlights inconsistencies in perioperative care delivery for older surgical patients, revealing gaps in the implementation of established guidelines and recommendations. There is a need for a structured approach to integrate geriatric services into surgical pathways, with an emphasis on routine screening for frailty, cognitive impairment, multimorbidity, and delirium.

articles.title: 2026 updated recommendations of the Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology for biologic therapy in moderate-to-severe psoriasis: Management of special populations, comorbidities, and treatment-related risks-Part 2.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology regularly updates its recommendations for the management of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. The expanding availability of biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments, together with emerging evidence on their efficacy and safety, requires updated guidance for special populations, patients with comorbidities, and treatment-related risk management. This document provides evidence-informed recommendations to support individualized therapeutic decision-making.
METHODS: Recommendations were developed using the nominal group technique, supported by a scoping review of the literature. Two coordinators appointed a panel of GPS experts and defined the clinical questions and topics requiring revision. With the assistance of an information specialist, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through October 2025. Evidence was selected from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and high-quality real-world studies. Relevant national and international clinical practice guidelines and consensus documents were also reviewed. Previous recommendations were revised, and new recommendations were developed, evaluated by the expert panel, and refined through successive review rounds.
RESULTS: Updated recommendations address biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments for moderate-to-severe psoriasis. Management considerations include older adults, pediatric patients, pregnancy, breastfeeding, conception planning, poor treatment adherence, multiple treatment failures, and psoriasis affecting special anatomical sites. Recommendations also address treatment selection in patients with obesity, metabolic syndrome, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, depression, malignancy, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, neurologic disorders, lupus, and other autoimmune diseases. Treatment-related risk management encompasses pretreatment assessment, laboratory and clinical monitoring, vaccination, infection and latent tuberculosis screening, neurotoxicity, perioperative management, adverse events, and treatment discontinuation. Multidisciplinary care is emphasized throughout.
CONCLUSIONS: These updated recommendations provide an evidence-informed framework for individualized systemic treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis in special populations and patients with comorbidities. Treatment selection should integrate disease characteristics, comorbidities, patient preferences, available evidence, and treatment-specific safety considerations. Ongoing risk assessment, appropriate monitoring, and multidisciplinary collaboration are essential components of long-term psoriasis management.

articles.title: Outcomes After Fetoscopic Myelomeningocele Repair With Preoperative BMI ≥ 35.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 is associated with preterm birth and adverse maternal outcomes following fetoscopic myelomeningocele (MMC) repair.
METHOD: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing fetoscopic MMC repair from 2014 to 2026. Patients with preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 were compared with BMI < 35 kg/m2. The primary outcome was preterm birth before 37 weeks' gestation. Secondary outcomes included gestational age at delivery, maternal complications, and procedure-related risks. Comparisons were performed using bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 209 patients, 21 (10%) had preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2. Rates of preterm birth before 37 weeks were similar in patients with BMI ≥ 35 versus < 35 kg/m2 (52% vs. 49%, p = 0.80), as was gestational age at delivery (35.9 vs. 37.0 weeks, p = 0.70). BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 was not associated with preterm birth after multivariable adjustment (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.37-2.62). Skin-to-skin operative time, CO2 insufflation time, and total fetoscopic time were comparable between the groups. No differences were observed in the rates of PPROM, placental abruption, intraamniotic infection, or maternal perioperative complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Pre-operative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 was not associated with differences in preterm birth, gestational age at delivery, operative characteristics, or maternal perioperative morbidity following fetoscopic MMC repair.

articles.title: Bilateral Petit's-Triangle Transversus Abdominis Plane Block and Postoperative Opioid Consumption After Minimally Invasive Primary Bariatric Surgery: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tra​nsversus abdominis plane (TAP) blocks are a common modality of opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia in bariatric surgery; however, the effectiveness of a particular injection site is unknown. We compared bilateral Petit's-triangle (posterior landmark) TAP blocks with TAP blocks placed at other abdominal sites, with respect to early postoperative opioid consumption.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort of adults undergoing minimally invasive (laparoscopic or robotic) primary bariatric surgery-sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass-who received a TAP block and no intraperitoneal local-anesthetic instillation. The exposure was bilateral Petit's-triangle block versus block at other sites. The primary outcome was cumulative inpatient opioid consumption at 24 h, expressed in morphine milligram equivalents (MME). Because opioid use was zero-inflated and right-skewed, the adjusted difference was estimated by ordinary-least-squares (OLS) regression with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC3) standard errors and corroborated with median (quantile) regression and a two-part (hurdle) model; multivariable models additionally adjusted for scheduled acetaminophen, NSAID use, procedure, approach, and surgeon. Groups were compared with Wilcoxon rank-sum and χ²/Fisher tests.
RESULTS: Of 266 patients, 144 received Petit's-triangle blocks and 122 received blocks at other sites. Median 24-hour opioid consumption was 0.0 MME (IQR 0.0-6.6) in the​ Petit's group versus 5.0 MME (2.0-11.8) in the other-site group (P < 0.001; Hedges g = - 0.49); 12- and 48-hour results were concordant (both P < 0.001). Fewer Petit's-group patients required any opioid in the first 24 h (49% vs. 75%; adjusted odds ratio 0.26, 95% CI 0.14-0.50; number needed to treat 4). The adjusted difference was - 4.36 MME after surgeon fixed effects and - 4.65 MME (95% CI - 7.13 to - 2.17) after additionally adjusting for acetaminophen an​d NSAID use; median regression (- 5.01 MME, 95% CI - 6.80 to - 3.22) and a within-surgeon analysis restricted to the two surgeons who used both sites (- 5.20 MME, 95% CI - 7.86 to - 2.55) were concordant. A head-to-head comparison against bilateral multiple-site blocks (the predominant comparator) gave the same result (P < 0.001). Pain scores did not differ at 24 h (4.0 vs. 4.0, P = 0.87); average pain was slightly higher in the Petit's group but not significantly so (4.0 vs. 3.3, P = 0.09). CONCL​USIONS: In minimally invasive primary bariatric surgery, bilateral Petit's-triangle TAP blocks were associated with approximately half the early opioid requirement of blocks placed at other sites, with no penalty in reported pain and with an effect robust to adjustment for patient, procedural, and surgeon factors. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that the block site may be a modifiable determinant of TAP-block effectiveness and warrants prospective, randomized evaluation.

articles.title: Who is the patient with metabolic acidosis? What six bicarbonate trials mean for critical care practice.
Radiofrequency Ablation versus Lateralization for Bilateral Inferior Turbinate Hypertrophy: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Radiofrequency ablation (RFIT) and lateralization are both established, office-based, local-anaesthesia treatments for bilateral inferior turbinate hypertrophy (BITH), but have not previously been compared head-to-head as stand-alone procedures. This trial compared the two in patients who declined turbinate surgery under general anaesthesia.
METHODS: Prospective, randomised, comparative trial with 6-month follow-up at a single tertiary otolaryngology clinic in Malaysia. 54 adults with BITH refractory to medical therapy were randomised to RFIT (n=26) or lateralization (n=28). Outcomes were Nasal Obstruction Symptom Evaluation (NOSE) score, endoscopic turbinate grade, procedural pain/anxiety (visual analogue scale), and complications, assessed at baseline and 1 week, 1, 3 and 6 months.
RESULTS: 53 patients completed follow-up. Baseline NOSE scores were similar between groups (RFIT 62.1, 95% CI 56.6-67.6; lateralization 64.6, 95% CI 59.1-70.2; both in the severe category). Both groups improved significantly from baseline through 6 months (RFIT: F(4,100)=56.3, p<0.001, ηp²=0.69; lateralization: F(4,104)=20.4, p<0.001, ηp²=0.44; Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons all p<0.001). RFIT improved further between 1 week and 1 month (p<0.001) before plateauing. Lateralization plateaued immediately after 1 week without losing ground. Turbinate grade improved significantly within each group (RFIT: F(4,68.4)=14.2, p<0.001, ηp²=0.197; lateralization: F(4,71.1)=10.9, p<0.001, ηp²=0.162). RFIT maintained its reduction at all follow-up points, while in the lateralization group the grade improvement was no longer statistically significant versus baseline at 6 months (Bonferroni-adjusted p=0.431). Groups differed significantly at 3 months (p=0.029) and 6 months (p=0.002). The Group×Time interaction was significant (F(4,204)=4.78, p=0.001). Pain and anxiety scores were comparable between groups (p=0.986, p=0.580).
CONCLUSIONS: Both procedures produce durable, statistically significant improvement in BITH under local anaesthesia. RFIT achieves greater, still-improving relief through 1 month before plateauing. Lateralization plateaus earlier at a more modest but still durable level. The choice may reasonably depend on the priority given to magnitude of relief versus procedural simplicity and resource availability.

articles.title: Effects of propofol in addition to isoflurane anesthesia on the immune response within the microcirculation: An intravital microscopy study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundGeneral volatile anesthesia is widely used in human medicine and the standard approach in many experimental animal procedures. In certain clinical situations, intravenous propofol may be added to inhalational anesthesia. Both types of anesthetics are known to have immunomodulatory effects, however, the effects of combining them on the immune response remain insufficiently understood.MethodsTwenty male C57BL/6J mice received either isoflurane alone or a combination of isoflurane and propofol. The mice were challenged with either endotoxin or placebo. Intravital fluorescence microscopy of the intestinal submucosa was performed to quantify leukocyte rolling flux and adhesion in collecting (V1) and post-capillary (V3) venules. Additionally, functional capillary density (FCD) was measured in the mucosa and muscularis layers to evaluate microvascular perfusion.ResultsThe addition of propofol to isoflurane anesthesia attenuated the inflammatory response to endotoxin, as shown by reduced leukocyte adhesion and preservation of rolling flux in the intestinal microcirculation. Intestinal FCD remained unchanged across both mucosal and muscular layers in both anesthetic regimens under baseline and inflammatory conditions.ConclusionsPropofol appears to have anti-inflammatory effects. The consequences of these effects should be considered in the clinical context of pre-existing inflammation (protective) or physiological response to surgical trauma (potentially detrimental).

articles.title: Reducing General Anesthesia Use in Pediatric Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) program at our institution has relied solely on general anesthesia for patients who are unable to lie still or adequately breath-hold. The goal of the project was to decrease the percentage of patients who require general anesthesia for CMR from 34% per month to 20% per month while maintaining high-quality imaging.
METHODS: This is an ongoing quality improvement project that began in January 2024 at our free-standing children's hospital. We included all patients scheduled for a CMR, including some adults cared for by our adult congenital cardiology colleagues at a partnering institution. The outcome measure was the percentage of patients who required general anesthesia for CMR.
RESULTS: After 21 months, we shifted our mean from 34% to 6.5% per month and sustained that for 15 months by the time of this article submission.
CONCLUSIONS: By implementing a quality improvement project that follows the Institute for Healthcare Improvement model, we significantly decreased the percentage of patients who require general anesthesia to achieve CMR and sustained this reduction. Our experience at a free-standing pediatric children's hospital with a small but growing CMR program can inform improvements in MRI centers of all sizes but could particularly benefit programs of similar size that lack a dedicated cardiac anesthesia program.

articles.title: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Protocols in Laparoscopic GI Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Protocols known as enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) have transformed perioperative care by integrating multidisciplinary, evidence-based measures that aim to reduce surgical stress and promote faster recovery.
OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the influence of ERAS pathways on perioperative outcomes among patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrointestinal operations.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 170 adult patients (18-80 years) who underwent laparoscopic procedures between February 2023 and August 2025. Patients treated according to ERAS principles were compared with those receiving conventional perioperative care. Outcomes of interest included opioid consumption, readmission rates, complication profiles, hospitalization duration, and overall costs.
RESULTS: Among 170 patients (mean age 42.0 ± 15.9 years; 59.4% female), cholecystectomy was the most common procedure (64.1%). ERAS implementation was associated with a shorter duration of opioid therapy (median 3 days, discontinued by day 5), low readmission frequency (3.5%), and brief hospitalization (median 27 hours). Postoperative complications occurred in 5.3% of patients, most often wound seroma (2.4%). Multivariable analysis showed younger age predicted earlier recovery, while sex, nationality, comorbidities, and procedure type had no significant effect.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective single-center cohort of 170 patients undergoing a range of laparoscopic gastrointestinal procedures, ERAS-based perioperative care was associated with favorable recovery outcomes. Because procedure complexity and expected recovery varied across the cohort, these findings should be interpreted as associative and should not be taken to imply an identical ERAS effect across all procedure types.
articles.journal_full: JSLS : Journal of the Society of Laparoendoscopic Surgeons

articles.title: Association between early sensory level following spinal anesthesia and intraoperative pain during cesarean delivery: a retrospective cohort study (2019-2020).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal anesthesia is widely used for cesarean delivery; however, some patients experience intraoperative pain or discomfort. This study investigated the association between early onset with rapid cephalad spread of spinal anesthesia and intraoperative pain during cesarean delivery.
METHODS: In this retrospective study conducted at Seoul National University Bundang Hospital, a total of 427 cesarean deliveries were evaluated. Data on sensory block levels at 5 and 10 min after intrathecal injection were extracted from anesthesia records. Intraoperative pain was defined as a distressing sensation managed with supplemental analgesia. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated associations of sensory block levels at 5 and 10 min with intraoperative pain.
RESULTS: Pain occurred in 56 patients (13.1%). Among patients experiencing intraoperative pain, the mean sensory level was lower compared with patients without pain at 5 min (8.1 ± 1.8 vs 6.8 ± 1.9; mean difference, 1.3 dermatomes; P < 0.001) and at 10 min (5.8 ± 1.6 vs 4.7 ± 1.2, mean difference, 1.1 dermatomes; P < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression models, each 1-dermatome lower sensory level at 5 min was associated with 16% higher adjusted odds of intraoperative pain (aOR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.01-1.33; P = 0.035), while at 10 min, it was associated with 43% higher odds (aOR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.18-1.74; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Lower sensory levels during the first 10 min after intrathecal injection were associated with pain, despite an apparently adequate T4 sensory block at skin incision, suggesting that slower onset might predict intraoperative pain during cesarean delivery.

articles.title: Cost and Environmental Protection Related to Procedure Room Surgery Versus Operating Room Surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Climate change poses a significant public health threat, and the health care sector could contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Operating rooms (ORs) are highly energy-intensive and produce substantial waste, including disposable products and anesthesia services. This study compares the environmental impact and cost-effectiveness of simple operative procedures like carpal tunnel release, ganglion excision, and trigger finger release performed in outpatient procedure rooms (PRs) versus ORs, hypothesizing that PRs are more sustainable and cost-effective.
METHODS: This observational study was conducted at a level 2 trauma center in Saskatchewan, Canada. Institutional Research Ethics Board approval was obtained. A total of three OR and six PR surgeries performed by a single surgeon were observed. Data on procedural duration, resource utilization, waste generation, and associated direct costs were systematically collected. Carbon emissions in kilograms of CO2 equivalents (kgCO2e) were estimated using standardized emission factors based on the processing of surgical waste and linens, as well as energy consumption from room lights, surgical lights, and central processing. Statistical analysis was conducted using the statistical software SAS 9.4 (SAS Institute Inc).
RESULTS: A single PR procedure produced 1.05 kgCO2e, whereas an OR procedure produced 4.36 kgCO2e. OR procedures generated 18 times more surgical waste and used twice as many linens. Financially, a PR procedure costs $376.78, whereas an OR procedure costs $1,004.28.
CONCLUSIONS: Shifting simple operative procedures from ORs to PRs can significantly reduce environmental impact and costs. PR surgeries generated 76% less carbon emissions and 94.5% less surgical waste and were 62.5% less expensive. These findings suggest that outpatient PR settings offer a more sustainable and cost-effective alternative for many simple procedures, contributing to a greener and more economically efficient health care system.
TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Economic/decision analysis IIb.
articles.journal_full: Journal of hand surgery global online

articles.title: Effects of propofol- or sevoflurane-containing anaesthesia on auditory brainstem responses in children: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Auditory brainstem response (ABR) provides objective hearing assessment in children who cannot undergo reliable behavioural audiometry. Sedation or general anaesthesia may facilitate recording but can alter electrophysiological measurements and potentially influence diagnostic interpretation. The primary aim of this systematic review was to explore electrophysiological and diagnostic outcomes of paediatric ABR testing when at least one study condition included propofol or sevoflurane.
METHODS: This Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 systematic review was prospectively registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261324873). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception, with searches updated on 17 August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened the original search; one reviewer screened the later update. Because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively.
RESULTS: The database searches identified 2386 records and yielded six eligible studies. Citation checking identified one additional study, giving seven in total. Four studies reported longer wave V latency under anaesthesia than under their respective comparators, but co-administered agents and differing populations preclude drug-specific attribution. In a within-participant comparison, hearing-loss classification differed between sevoflurane and propofol; a later observational cohort found no significant adjusted association for its distinct exposure groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Four of seven studies reported longer ABR electrophysiological wave V latency under anaesthesia, but five studies had a high risk of bias. A single study with within-participant comparison found different diagnostic classifications under sevoflurane and propofol. Heterogeneous designs and exposures do not establish which anaesthesia technique best preserves paediatric ABR findings.

articles.title: Daily debriefings, burnout, and impostor phenomenon in anaesthesiology trainees and supervisors: a controlled feasibility study.
Advances in appendectomy for uncomplicated appendicitis.
articles.abstract: Appendicitis is the most common surgical emergency in children and a leading cause of hospitalization among pediatric patients. Over recent decades, considerable advances have transformed both operative and perioperative management of acute uncomplicated appendicitis. This chapter highlights historical and contemporary literature describing the evolution of acute appendicitis management, with an emphasis on surgical innovation and perioperative care in pediatric patients. Surgical management of appendicitis has evolved dramatically from open procedures performed without anesthesia to the current standard of minimally invasive laparoscopic approaches. Laparoscopic appendectomy has largely replaced open appendectomy and become the standard of care due to reduced postoperative pain, shorter hospital stays, faster recovery, and lower surgical site infection rates. Emerging modifications - including single-incision laparoscopic surgery (SILS), endoscopic, and robotic approaches - further minimize invasiveness and improve cosmetic outcomes, though cost and resource availability remain limiting factors. Parallel to these surgical advances, perioperative care has shifted substantially. Appendicitis, once treated as a surgical emergency, is now commonly managed with antibiotics initially and a less urgent surgical approach. Evidence supports the safety of delayed appendectomy up to 24 h after diagnosis following antibiotic initiation. Preoperative antibiotics have remained standard, whereas postoperative antibiotic use in uncomplicated cases is no longer recommended. Enhanced recovery protocols and outpatient pathways have enabled safe same-day discharge following appendectomy, further reducing healthcare utilization and cost.

articles.title: Perioperative esketamine is associated with attenuated sleep deprivation-related cognitive dysfunction: a retrospective biomarker cohort study of the ferroptosis-neuroinflammation axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep deprivation is common in older surgical patients and may increase vulnerability to postoperative neurocognitive dysfunction through oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and regulated cell-death pathways. Experimental studies increasingly implicate hippocampal ferroptosis, particularly disruption of the SLC7A11-GSH-GPX4 defense axis, in sleep-deprivation-related cognitive injury. Esketamine has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but whether its perioperative neurocognitive benefit is associated with a ferroptosis-related molecular phenotype in clinical patients remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective biomarker cohort study of 398 adults aged 60-80 years who underwent elective major non-cardiac surgery between January 2022 and December 2025. Patients were classified according to preoperative sleep deprivation (total sleep time <4 h and sleep efficiency <70% during the night before surgery) and perioperative esketamine exposure, generating four groups: NSD-C, NSD-E, SD-C, and SD-E. The primary outcome was early postoperative cognitive decline on postoperative day (POD) 7, defined by a ≥1-SD deterioration in a composite neuropsychological Z score. In a biomarker subcohort, plasma 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (4-HNE), malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione (GSH), glutathione peroxidase activity, inflammatory cytokines, neuronal injury markers, and PBMC expression of GPX4, SLC7A11, and ACSL4 were analyzed. Confounding was addressed using multivariable models and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting. Bootstrap mediation models examined a ferroptosis-related redox score and IL-6 as candidate mediators.
RESULTS: In the cohort, cognitive decline occurred in 32.5% of sleep-deprived patients without esketamine and 17.7% of sleep-deprived patients exposed to esketamine. After adjustment, esketamine exposure in the sleep-deprivation subgroup was associated with lower odds of cognitive decline (adjusted OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.92). Sleep deprivation was associated with higher 4-HNE, MDA, ACSL4, IL-6, TNF-α, and NSE and lower GSH, GPX activity, GPX4, and SLC7A11; these abnormalities were attenuated in the esketamine-exposed group. The exploratory ferroptosis-related redox score was independently associated with cognitive decline. Under the specified exploratory mediation model, the estimated total mediated proportion was 54%; this model-based decomposition does not establish causal biological mediation.
CONCLUSION: Perioperative esketamine was associated with less pronounced early postoperative cognitive decline in sleep-deprived patients and a less pronounced peripheral ferroptosis-related/inflammatory phenotype.

articles.title: Comparison of the efficacy and safety of intra-aortic balloon occlusion and uterine artery embolization in types IIb-III cesarean scar pregnancy: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Managing cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is clinically challenging because of the substantial risk of hemorrhage, which necessitates appropriate preoperative strategies. Uterine artery embolization (UAE) is widely used to reduce perioperative bleeding, whereas intra-aortic balloon occlusion (IABO) offers temporary vascular control without permanent embolization. This retrospective cohort study compared perioperative, economic, menstrual, and subsequent reproductive outcomes between IABO and UAE in patients with types IIb-III CSP.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 73 patients with types IIb-III CSP admitted to Jiangxi Provincial Maternal and Child Health Hospital between June 2020 and June 2025. Patients were managed with IABO-assisted surgery (n = 40) or UAE-assisted surgery (n = 33) according to the pretreatment strategy used in routine clinical practice. Baseline characteristics, perioperative outcomes, hospitalization indicators, menstrual recovery, and subsequent reproductive outcomes were compared between groups. Because treatment allocation was nonrandomized, between-group findings were interpreted as observational associations.
RESULTS: The groups differed in baseline fetal cardiac activity and ultrasonographic hypervascularity. Intraoperative blood loss, operative time, treatment conversion, treatment success, and readmission did not differ significantly between groups. Massive hemorrhage, defined as intraoperative blood loss ≥500 mL, occurred in 3 of 40 patients (7.5%) in the IABO group and 3 of 33 patients (9.1%) in the UAE group. The IABO group had a shorter hospital stay and lower hospitalization costs. Postoperative hypomenorrhea within 1 year was less frequent in the IABO group than in the UAE group. Subsequent pregnancy outcomes were described descriptively because of the small number of patients with follow-up pregnancies.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, IABO and UAE showed broadly comparable perioperative hemostatic outcomes, while IABO was associated with shorter hospitalization, lower costs, and a lower frequency of postoperative hypomenorrhea. However, treatment allocation was nonrandomized and baseline differences indicated potential confounding by indication. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory associations rather than evidence of comparative superiority.

articles.title: Targeting MicroRNAs in the perioperative window to prevent surgery-induced metastasis and postoperative cancer recurrence.
articles.abstract: Surgery remains a central curative treatment for many solid tumors; however, postoperative recurrence and distant metastasis continue to limit long-term survival. The perioperative period is increasingly recognised as a biologically active window during which surgical trauma, inflammation, wound repair, hypoxia, platelet activation, immunosuppression, anaesthetic exposure, and extracellular vesicle signalling may influence the survival and outgrowth of residual tumour cells, circulating tumour cells, and dormant micrometastases. MicroRNAs are particularly relevant in this context because they regulate coordinated gene networks involved in tumor survival, epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, angiogenesis, immune escape, and metastatic niche formation. OncomiRs such as miR-21, miR-10b, miR-155, miR-210, and miR-221/222 may promote recurrence-associated signaling, whereas tumor-suppressive miRNAs including miR-34a, the miR-200 family, let-7, miR-126, miR-143/145, and miR-29 may restrict metastatic progression. This review provides a translational framework linking surgery-induced host responses with miRNA-mediated metastatic regulation. It discusses perioperative immune and stromal remodeling, anesthetic and analgesic influences, exosomal miRNAs, biomarker-guided monitoring, therapeutic delivery systems, safety concerns, and clinical trial design. Although perioperative miRNA therapy is not yet a validated clinical intervention, serial miRNA profiling combined with ctDNA, circulating tumor cells, cytokines, and clinicopathological variables may support future precision strategies to identify high-risk patients and guide recurrence-prevention studies. The key challenge is to suppress pro-metastatic signaling without impairing wound healing, infection control, or postoperative recovery.

articles.title: Anatomical Basis for Advancing the Transesophageal Echocardiography Probe Through the Esophageal Hiatus: Insights from Computed Tomography.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Advancement of a transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) probe through the esophageal hiatus can be hindered by resistance, yet the mechanism is poorly understood. We investigated the esophageal trajectory and surrounding structures to provide an anatomical basis for transgastric probe advancement.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
SETTING: Single-center cardiovascular surgery program.
PARTICIPANTS: Eighteen of 191 consecutive patients undergoing cardiovascular surgery in whom postoperative computed tomography (CT) was obtained with a nasogastric tube in place.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Postoperative CT images were used to analyze the esophageal trajectory and its spatial relationship with the descending thoracic aorta. Preoperative CT images were used to assess esophageal dimensions and surrounding structures immediately above the hiatus. The esophagus followed a posteriorly curved trajectory. Its median diameters immediately above the hiatus were 16.2 × 13.0 mm, similar to those of the distal portion of the TEE probe. The esophagus was bordered predominantly by the heart anteriorly and aorta posteriorly, whereas loose connective tissue or lung predominated laterally. The aorta progressively approached the esophagus and was mostly within 10 mm at the hiatus, predominantly posterior or slightly right-posterior in the TEE operator's orientation.
CONCLUSION: The posterior esophageal course and loose lateral tissues provide a plausible anatomical explanation for resistance caused by probe misalignment near the hiatus. The close relationship between the esophagus and aorta provides a rationale for using the aorta as a visual landmark during probe advancement. These findings may facilitate a more structured and anatomically informed approach to TEE education.

articles.title: Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy During Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation as a Marker of Persistent Organ Support Burden and Post-Decannulation Mortality in Adult Cardiovascular Critical Care: A 9-Year Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) use during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) serves as a clinical marker of persistent organ support burden and is associated with survival to hospital discharge and post-decannulation mortality among patients successfully separated from ECMO.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Tertiary cardiovascular center, 2017-2025.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults (n = 1,224) supported with ECMO, of whom 918 (75.0%) had cardiac failure, 245 (20.0%) underwent extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and 1,164 (95.1%) initially received veno‑arterial (V‑A) ECMO.
INTERVENTIONS: CRRT use at any point during the ECMO course; patients without CRRT served as the comparator.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge; secondary analysis examined post‑decannulation death in patients successfully separated from ECMO. Primary severity‑adjusted models included age, sex, ECMO indication, intra‑aortic balloon pump use, pre‑ECMO lactate, and log‑transformed vasoactive‑inotropic score. CRRT was used in 519 (42.4%) patients. Survival to discharge was significantly lower with CRRT than without (149/513 [29.0%] v 380/700 [54.3%]; unadjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.34; 95% CI, 0.27-0.44), and the association remained after severity adjustment (adjusted OR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.28-0.48). Additional sensitivity models adjusting for pre-ECMO Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score (n = 1,056; adjusted OR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.29-0.50) and pre-ECMO Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO score in V-A ECMO (n = 1,052; adjusted OR, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.27-0.47) confirmed the consistency of this association. Among 676 patients successfully separated from ECMO, post-decannulation death occurred in 80 of 230 (34.8%) with CRRT and 66 of 446 (14.8%) without CRRT (adjusted OR, 2.69; 95% CI, 1.81-3.99).
CONCLUSIONS: CRRT use during ECMO marked a high-risk cardiovascular critical care phenotype with greater persistent organ support burden, lower discharge survival, and higher post-decannulation mortality. These associations should be interpreted as prognostic rather than causal; CRRT status may provide pragmatic information for risk stratification after ECMO separation.

articles.title: Revisiting Perioperative Tacrolimus Concentration Changes After Kidney Transplantation Through Detailed Clinical Observation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although much is known about tacrolimus (Tac) after kidney transplantation, understanding fluctuations in Tac concentrations observed in clinical practice remains challenging. We aimed to characterize perioperative Tac concentration fluctuations through detailed clinical observation.
METHODS: This was a single-center, retrospective, descriptive study of kidney transplant recipients. In 158 patients, day-to-day percentage changes and directional distributions of Tac concentrations from postoperative day (POD) 1 to POD4 were evaluated, with additional analyses according to dose modification and CYP3A5 genotype. Individual patient trajectories were examined. In a subsequent cohort of 59 patients, perioperative changes in interleukin-6 (IL-6), hematocrit (Ht), albumin (Alb), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were analyzed in relation to changes in Tac concentrations.
RESULTS: Changes in Tac concentrations showed substantial interindividual variability, but at the population level, a common trend in the direction of change was observed across PODs. Similar trends were seen in analyses according to dose modification and CYP3A5 genotype, although the magnitude of changes differed. Individual patient trajectories were diverse; however, the four most frequent patterns based on direction alone accounted for 64.4% of patients, and all included an increase on POD2 and a decrease on POD4. Changes in IL-6, Ht, and Alb also showed substantial interindividual variability.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative Tac concentration changes showed features suggesting a temporally continuous process. These findings suggest the possible involvement of underlying factors contributing to similar fluctuations. Considering how concentrations may change subsequently and the effects of interventions from this perspective may help us better understand perioperative Tac concentration fluctuations.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Functional Outcomes After Surgery for Spinal Dysraphism: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Introduction Spinal dysraphism includes heterogeneous congenital lesions that may affect motor, bladder, and bowel function. This study described the clinical spectrum, perioperative events, and functional outcomes after surgery. Methods We retrospectively studied 276 patients who underwent surgery for spinal dysraphism. Neurological function was recorded using the modified McCormick grade. Preoperative and postoperative grades were compared with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Simple group comparisons explored factors associated with improvement. Categorical variables were compared with the chi-square or Fisher's exact test, and continuous variables with the Mann-Whitney U test. Results The median age was 2.3 years (interquartile range, 0.73-5.0), and 148 patients (53.6%) were male. Motor weakness was present in 212 (76.8%), bladder involvement in 146 (52.9%), and bowel involvement in 62 (22.5%). The median modified McCormick grade was 4 before surgery and 3 after surgery (P < 0.001). Functional grade improved in 108 patients (39.1%), remained unchanged in 162 (58.7%), and worsened in six (2.2%). Immediate postoperative complications occurred in 29 patients (10.5%). Improvement was associated with lower preoperative motor power, greater preoperative functional disability, selected caudal dysraphic phenotypes, sac repair, and detethering in unadjusted comparisons. Bladder involvement did not change significantly after surgery (P = 0.625). Conclusion Most patients had stable or improved postoperative functional grades. Because the cohort was retrospective and anatomically heterogeneous, the observed associations should be considered descriptive rather than predictive across diverse lesions and operative approaches. Standardized long-term neurological and urological follow-up is needed.

articles.title: Incidence, Etiologies, and Predictors of Seven-Day Graft Loss in Adult Lung Transplantation: A National Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Seven-day graft loss, defined as graft failure or recipient death within 7 days posttransplant, remains poorly characterized in adult lung transplantation. We evaluated national incidence, etiologies, and predictors of 7-day graft loss and 7-day posttransplant death.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data to retrospectively analyze 25 593 adult deceased donor lung transplant recipients transplanted from 2015 to 2024. We compared recipients with 7-day graft loss or 7-day posttransplant death with recipients who had ≥1-year graft or patient survival, respectively.
RESULTS: Seven-day graft loss occurred in 526 recipients (2.1% ). Primary nonfunction was the leading etiology (63.5%), followed by etiologies coded as "other/unknown" (35.4% ). Cardiovascular failure was the leading cause of 7-day posttransplant death (24.1% ), and 72-hour extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was the strongest independent predictor of 7-day graft loss (odds ratio 9.04, P < .001). Other predictors were retransplant (odds ratio 1.80, P = .01), elevated serum bilirubin at transplant (odds ratio 1.16, P < .001), and higher physiologic severity score (odds ratio 1.02, P < .001), whereas extracorporeal membrane oxygenation at listing carried lower odds (odds ratio 0.61, P = .04). Predictors of 7-day posttransplant death included 72-hour extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (odds ratio 21.97, P < .001), elevated physiologic severity score (odds ratio 1.02, P < .001), and bilateral lung transplant (odds ratio 2.09, P = .04). Male sex (odds ratio 0.64, P = .045) and higher match-time lung allocation score (odds ratio 0.98, P = .005) carried lower odds. Donor characteristics were assessed only in unadjusted comparisons.
CONCLUSIONS: Seven-day outcomes were associated with recipient physiologic reserve and early post-operative instability. Frequent other/unknown etiologic coding underscores the need for improved reporting and event-level granularity. Despite registry limitations, this risk profile may inform risk stratification, postoperative surveillance, donor-recipient matching, and perioperative optimization.

articles.title: Magnetic Ureteric Stents After Kidney Transplantation: A Systematic Review of Retrieval Success, Cystoscopy Avoidance, Safety, and Resource Utilization.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Ureteric stents are routinely used after kidney transplant to prevent urological complications; however, cystoscopic removal can be associated with discomfort and high costs, particularly in the pediatric population where general anesthesia is often required. Magnetic stents offer a novel method of bypassing cystoscopic retrieval. Here, we synthesized evidence on feasibility, safety, and service delivery of magnetic stents after kidney transplant.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This systematic review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA, evaluated magnetic ureteric stents in kidney transplant recipients. The primary outcome was successful non-cystoscopic stent retrieval. Secondary outcomes included failed retrieval, removal time, pain, quality of life, urinary tract infection, urological and transplant-specific complications, cost, and service delivery measures.
RESULTS: Our study included 9 studies: 2 randomized controlled trials, 2 prospective nonrandomized comparative studies or abstracts, 1 audit abstract, and 4 noncomparative cohort or feasibility studies. Seven studies involving 251 recipients reported extractable retrieval outcomes, with successful non-cystoscopic retrieval achieved in 244 cases, corresponding to a crude success rate of 97.2%. Need for cystoscopic rescue occurred in 7 of 251 cases. Removal times were short, and magnetic retrieval was well-tolerated. Comparative studies did not show clear superiority for pain, quality of life, or stent-related symptoms. No clear signal of increased urinary tract infections or urological complications was identified. Cost and service delivery outcomes generally favored magnetic stents when the full removal pathway was considered.
CONCLUSIONS: Magnetic ureteric stents after kidney transplant appear feasible, well-tolerated, and associated with high rates of successful non-cystoscopic retrieval. Main benefits appear to be cystoscopy avoidance, pathway simplification, and potential cost savings, rather than clear improvements in pain or quality-of-life. Current evidence is limited by small study sizes, heterogeneous designs, and incomplete reporting, thus remaining underpowered for transplant-specific outcomes. Magnetic stents may be useful in selected transplant pathways, provided that cystoscopic backup is available.
articles.journal_full: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation

articles.title: Evaluation of Kidney Graft Survival and Associated Risk Factors Using Cox Regression and Kaplan-Meier Survival Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Kidney transplantation is the preferred treatment for end-stage kidney disease; however, long-term graft survival is affected by multiple recipient-, donor-, and posttransplant-related factors. In this study, we evaluated kidney graft survival and identified factors associated with graft outcomes using integrated survival analysis methods.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 700 adult kidney transplant recipients who underwent transplant at Farhikhtegan Hospital, Tehran, Iran, between 2020 and 2025. We extracted demographic, clinical, transplant-related, and follow-up data from medical records and the hospital information system. We estimated graft survival using the Kaplan-Meier method. We assessed differences between groups with the log-rank test and identified independent predictors of graft failure using the Cox proportional hazards model. We analyzed the following subgroups: recipient and donor age, sex, and body mass index.
RESULTS: Estimated kidney graft survival at 1, 2, 3, and 4 years after transplant was 94.71%, 86.4%, 81.1%, and 77.0%, respectively. Recipient age and donor age were significantly associated with graft survival (P < .001), with younger recipients and younger donors demonstrating better long-term outcomes. Recipient sex and donor sex showed no significant association with graft survival. Higher body mass index in both recipients and donors was associated with reduced graft survival. Cox regression analysis identified prolonged pretransplant dialysis duration, elevated serum creatinine levels, posttransplant infection, increased body mass index, and rejection episodes as significant predictors of graft failure.
CONCLUSIONS: Kidney graft survival is influenced by the combined effects of demographic, metabolic, and clinical factors rather than a single determinant. The integrated use of Kaplan-Meier survival estimation and Cox proportional hazards modeling provides comprehensive assessment of survival patterns and risk factors. Optimizing donor selection, metabolic status, perioperative management, and long-term follow-up may improve graft survival and clinical outcomes.
