articles.title: Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Children Undergoing Major Non-Cardiac Surgery: Protocol for a Multicentre Study (POAKIDS).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with increased mortality and adverse long-term outcomes. Postoperative AKI is a common and recognised complication after surgery in adults. In children, AKI following paediatric cardiac surgery has been extensively studied. However, the incidence and characteristics of postoperative AKI after non-cardiac surgery in children remain poorly defined, with existing evidence largely derived from retrospective and single-centre studies.
METHODS: POAKIDS is an international, multicentre, prospective observational study including hospitalised children aged 0-16 years undergoing major non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. Postoperative AKI will be defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO). The primary outcome is the incidence of postoperative AKI. Secondary objectives include evaluation of established and novel urinary biomarkers as predictors of postoperative AKI and exploration of perioperative potential predictors of renal injury. The maximal follow-up is seven postoperative days. Sample size is based on the incidence estimate, with a planned inclusion of 2000 patients. Data will be analysed using descriptive statistics, agreement analyses, and exploratory regression models.
DISCUSSION: This study aims to provide robust prospective data on the incidence of postoperative AKI in children undergoing major non-cardiac surgery and to improve understanding of perioperative renal injury in this population. By combining standardised AKI definitions with systematic biomarker assessment, the results are expected to inform future preventive strategies and guide the design of interventional studies targeting postoperative renal injury in paediatric perioperative care.

articles.title: Paediatric Sedation With Intranasal Dexmedetomidine for Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paediatric sedation for magnetic resonance imaging presents significant challenges. To facilitate this, our department decided to implement paediatric sedation with intranasal dexmedetomidine for children requiring a scan. We aim to summarise lessons learnt from implementation of intranasal dexmedetomidine, comparing time consumption and effectiveness.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study. Data from children sedated with intranasal dexmedetomidine 4 μg/kg (n = 51) were collected prospectively and compared with historical controls (n = 100) collected from children previously anaesthetized with either sevoflurane or propofol.
RESULTS: Sedation with intranasal dexmedetomidine resulted in a longer hospital stay (214 min vs. 133 min [67.94-94.74]), longer time to sufficient sedation (60 min vs. 26 min [29.31, 38.68]) and longer time in the post-operative unit (112 min vs. 64, 48 min [36.11, 60, 80]). Of children sedated with dexmedetomidine, 75% were cooperative with the intranasal administration of the medicine and 37% were successfully sedated with dexmedetomidine as the sole sedative. In the historical controls, 43% of patients required airway management compared to 1.9% in the dexmedetomidine group [0.00, 0.19]. In the control group, 20% had post-sedation agitation compared to none in the dexmedetomidine group. No serious bradycardia or desaturation was registered in either group.
CONCLUSION: Paediatric sedation with intranasal dexmedetomidine as the sole medicament for magnetic resonance imaging is more time-consuming compared to sevoflurane and propofol. Sedation with intranasal dexmedetomidine has a relatively low success rate but is without serious adverse events.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This single center case-control study with prospective datacollection for the case group, intranasal dexmedetomidine and comparison with a historical non-dexmedetomidine sedation group described multiple possible clinical advantages with intranasal dexmedetomidine administration as it was done here.

articles.title: Update in alternative donor strategies in heart and lung transplantation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Alternative donor strategies in cardiothoracic transplantation are becoming routine. This review covers recent developments and their implications for the anesthesiologist.
RECENT FINDINGS: Donor scarcity is a principal constraint on heart and lung transplantation. Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and the adoption of machine preservation have reshaped the donor pool. This review covers literature comparing thoracoabdominal normothermic regional perfusion with direct procurement and preservation, warm ischemic thresholds and their relationship to primary graft dysfunction, normothermic and hypothermic ex-situ perfusion, 10 °C static cold storage, and ex-vivo lung perfusion, and discusses the ethics of DCD. Extended-criteria and hepatitis C virus-viremic donors are now used routinely, and cardiac xenotransplantation is entering clinical study. Each advance alters graft physiology at reperfusion and the timing of perioperative services. Research into cardiac xenotransplantation is ongoing.
SUMMARY: These strategies enlarge the donor pool and introduce novel graft physiological concerns, as well as ethical concerns, for the anesthesiologist.

articles.title: A pilot randomized feasibility trial of perioperative melatonin for cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, sedative and analgesic medication use, and mechanical ventilation following CABG.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative complications remain common following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Although melatonin may have cardioprotective and sedative-sparing effects, its feasibility and potential effects on early postoperative cardiac rhythm and recovery in patients undergoing CABG remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility of a future definitive randomized controlled trial (RCT) of perioperative melatonin in patients undergoing on-pump CABG and to obtain preliminary estimates of its effects on cardiac arrhythmias during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use.
METHODS: In this pilot randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled feasibility trial, 22 adults undergoing elective on-pump CABG were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral melatonin (3 mg) or placebo nightly, from three nights before to three nights after surgery. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, completeness of outcome assessment, and intervention safety. Exploratory clinical outcomes included cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use.
RESULTS: Twenty-two participants were randomized. The recruitment rate was 68.75%, while retention, protocol adherence, and completeness of outcome assessment were all 100%; no treatment-related adverse events were observed. Arrhythmias during CPB weaning occurred in 2 of 11 participants (18.2%) in each group (OR, 1.00; 95% CI: 0.11-8.73). The median duration of mechanical ventilation was 9.5 hours with melatonin and 15.0 hours with placebo (Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the between-group location shift, -3.30 hours; 95% CI: -6.90 to 1.05). Postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use was generally comparable between groups, although the corresponding effect estimates were imprecise.
CONCLUSION: Melatonin was feasible and well tolerated in this pilot cohort, with no treatment-related adverse events observed. The exploratory estimates were imprecise and do not provide evidence of efficacy, supporting a larger, adequately powered randomized trial to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of melatonin.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: IRCT20250206064666N1, date of registration: 2025-02-24.

articles.title: Extravascular Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillators in Children: Real World Evidence.
articles.abstract: The extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (EV-ICD) is a novel substernal ICD with limited reports in children and adolescents. Single-centre review of EV-ICDs in children <18-years. Clinical, peri-procedural, and electrocardiographic data reviewed, including device performance in routine exercise stress testing. Median follow-up 10.9 (IQR 7.5 - 12.5) months. Between April 2025-April 2026, 15 EV-ICDs were successfully implanted by a single cardiothoracic surgeon: median age 13.8-years, IQR 10.2-16.4; 11 (73%) male; weight 52 kg, IQR 38.2-64.1; BSA 1.6 m2, IQR 1.2-1.8. Smallest child was 4-years, 17.3 kg (BSA 0.7 m2). Indications were primary (n = 10) and secondary (n = 5) prevention. Underlying diagnoses included cardiomyopathy (n = 9), channelopathy (n = 3). One child had a previous sternotomy and another severe chest-wall deformity. Median anaesthetic time was 148 min (IQR 130-161), surgical time 68 min (59-88), fluoroscopy time 2.6 min (2.2-3.8). Median 3 (IQR 2-4) day hospitalisation. Two children experienced early complications. In one child, defibrillator threshold testing terminated ventricular fibrillation (VF) into ventricular tachycardia (VT) requiring CPR and a decision to use external cardioversion. The child fully recovered. One adolescent experienced profound bradycardia and syncope early post anaesthesia. R-wave amplitude at implant (5mV, IQR 4.2 - 6.7), discharge (5, IQR 2.8 - 8.1) and latest follow-up (5.8, IQR 3.2 - 13.7) was stable. Device sensing during routine exercise stress testing has been appropriate. There has been one successful appropriate high voltage therapy and no inappropriate high voltage therapy. This is the largest single-centre series internationally, demonstrating reliable paediatric EV-ICD implantation and short-term device performance. Ongoing paediatric surveillance is necessary.

articles.title: Short-term postoperative outcomes of endoscopic treatment versus robot-assisted pyeloplasty for ureteropelvic junction obstruction.
articles.abstract: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction may cause hydronephrosis, infection, and renal dysfunction. Pyeloplasty remains the reconstructive standard, whereas endoscopic treatment is a less invasive alternative. Long-term outcomes of endoscopic treatment and pyeloplasty for ureteropelvic junction obstruction have already been addressed. However, contemporary multi-institutional comparisons of their short-term perioperative outcomes remain limited. This retrospective study compares 30-day postoperative outcomes between endoscopic ureteropelvic junction treatment and robot-assisted pyeloplasty in adults using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database. Adults undergoing endoscopic ureteropelvic junction treatment or robot-assisted pyeloplasty were identifed from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database (2022-2024). The prinicipal CPT code 52,345 identified endoscopic treatment cases, while robot-assisted pyeloplasty cases were sampled from the minimally invasive pyeloplasty cohort under CPT code 50,544, using the robotic variable. The primary endpoint was a composite of any 30-day non-wound postoperative complication. Secondary endpoints included the broader postoperative complication composite, readmission, reoperation, operative time, and length of stay. Multivariable regression models evaluated associations between surgical approach and outcomes after adjustment for relevant covariates. The cohort included 1,133 patients (93 endoscopic treatment; 1,040 robot-assisted pyeloplasty). Overall, 79 patients (7%) experienced at least one non-wound postoperative complication with similar rates between endoscopic treatment and robot-assisted pyeloplasty (4.3% vs. 7.2%, p = 0.291). After adjustment, procedure group was not significantly associated with non-wound complications (aOR 0.491, 95% CI 0.173-1.393; p = 0.181). The same applied for readmission (7.5% vs. 5.1%, p = 0.329) and unplanned reoperation (1.1% vs. 2.0%; p = 1.000). The endoscopic-treatment group had lower odds of hospitalization beyond the day of surgery (aOR 0.043, 95% CI 0.025-0.075; p < 0.001) and a shorter adjusted median operative time (difference - 127.1 min, 95% CI - 143.3 to - 110.8; p < 0.001). In this multi-institutional ACS NSQIP cohort, the endoscopic treatment of UPJO was associated with shorter operative time and hospital stay. No significant differences in 30-day postoperative complications, readmission, reoperation and mortality rates were detected between endoscopic UPJ treatment and robotic pyeloplasty. However, the small cohort and limited events preclude conclusions regarding equivalent safety. NSQIP does not capture long-term functional outcomes or treatment durability.

articles.title: Opioid-free vs. opioid-inclusive anaesthesia in laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the most common abdominal operation worldwide, yet whether opioid-free anaesthesia improves the overall analgesic benefit remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this multicentre randomised controlled trial, adults undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy were randomised 1:1 to receive opioid-free anaesthesia (dexmedetomidine, esketamine and sevoflurane) or opioid-inclusive anaesthesia (sufentanil and sevoflurane). Patients received prophylactic anti-emetics and multimodal analgesia with flurbiprofen axetil and ropivacaine wound infiltration. The primary outcome was the overall benefit of analgesia score (0-28, lower scores indicate greater benefit) at 24 h postoperatively; a 3-point difference was considered clinically relevant. Secondary outcomes included pain on movement at 24 h and chronic postsurgical pain at 90 days.
RESULTS: Between March and September 2025, 315 patients completed this trial (158 opioid-free, 157 opioid-inclusive). The mean (SD) 24-h overall benefit of analgesia score was 2.2 (2.4) after opioid-free anaesthesia vs 3.4 (3.1) after opioid-inclusive anaesthesia (adjusted mean difference -1.3; 95%CI -1.8 to -0.8, p < 0.001), without reaching the threshold for clinical importance. Incidence of pain on movement (adjusted mean difference -0.2; 95%CI -0.4-0) and chronic postsurgical pain (16.1% vs 15.5%; adjusted relative risk 1.03; 95%CI 0.55-1.91) did not differ between groups. Opioid-free anaesthesia was associated with reduced intra-operative hypotension (19.6% vs 35.7%; relative risk 0.55; 95%CI 0.37-0.80) and lower incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (23.4% vs 33.8%; relative risk 0.69; 95%CI 0.48-0.98).
DISCUSSION: Opioid-free anaesthesia did not achieve a clinically meaningful improvement in overall benefit of analgesia. These findings do not support its routine adoption in laparoscopic cholecystectomy. However, the observed reductions in intra-operative hypotension and postoperative nausea and vomiting suggest that this regimen may warrant consideration in selected patients, pending validation in future trials.

articles.title: Incidence of pain, supplemental analgesia and conversion to general anaesthesia during intrapartum caesarean delivery using converted epidural anaesthesia: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: It is common practice to convert an existing labour epidural into surgical anaesthesia for intrapartum caesarean delivery. However, this approach does not always provide adequate anaesthesia. This meta-analysis aimed to determine the incidence of inadequate anaesthesia during epidural conversion for intrapartum caesarean delivery.
METHODS: Databases were searched for observational studies and randomised controlled trials evaluating epidural conversion for intrapartum caesarean delivery. Using a random-effects model and the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation, we calculated the respective incidences of intra-operative patient-reported pain; use of supplemental analgesia; and conversion to general anaesthesia.
RESULTS: A total of 43 studies, involving 11,904 patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Pooled incidences of intra-operative pain (eight studies), supplemental analgesia (34 studies) and conversion to general anaesthesia (33 studies) were 20.2% (95%CI 12.2-29.5%, I2 = 93.1%), 17.7% (95%CI 13.3-22.7%, I2 = 96.3%) and 1.3% (95%CI 0.7-2.1%, I2 = 81.7%), respectively. These results were consistent in sensitivity analyses and appeared unaffected by publication year, study design, country type, local anaesthetic used or use of epidural fentanyl. However, substantial heterogeneity was observed due to variability in study methodologies, measurement methods, definitions, thresholds and local clinical practices.
DISCUSSION: This meta-analysis highlights the risk of inadequate anaesthesia and emphasises the importance of thorough pre-operative informed consent when converting labour epidurals to surgical anaesthesia for intrapartum caesarean delivery. However, the considerable heterogeneity in the pooled estimates indicates that these incidences vary significantly across different settings, suggesting that local audit data would be more informative for individual practices.

articles.title: Patient-reported experiences of malignant hyperthermia susceptibility investigation: a survey of waiting time, perioperative care and recovery after muscle biopsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malignant hyperthermia susceptibility investigation in Sweden includes muscle biopsy and in vitro contracture testing and is centralized to a single national unit, resulting in prolonged waiting times. Although the diagnostic pathway is well established, patients' experiences of referral, investigation, and recovery have rarely been studied. Therefore, this study aimed to explore patient-reported experiences of malignant hyperthermia investigation, with particular focus on waiting time, perioperative care, and recovery after muscle biopsy.
METHODS: An exploratory cross-sectional survey was conducted using a modified version of the Swedish National Patient Survey. Questionnaires were distributed to 172 adults who underwent malignant hyperthermia investigation between 2018 and 2024 at the Swedish Malignant Hyperthermia Unit. Descriptive statistics and group comparisons were performed.
RESULTS: Seventy participants responded (response rate 41%). Prolonged waiting time negatively affected 24.3% of participants and was associated with stress, uncertainty, and restricted access to surgical care. Most participants reported receiving clear information (95.7%) and being treated with compassion and respect (97.2-98.6%). Immediate postoperative discomfort was reported by 35 participants (50.0%), while 37 participants (52.9%) reported pain lasting one week or longer after the biopsy procedure. No statistically significant differences were detected according to age, sex, or diagnostic outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, among survey respondents, patients generally reported positive experiences of perioperative care during malignant hyperthermia susceptibility investigation. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously due to potential recall bias and the use of a non-validated questionnaire. However, postoperative pain was common, and prolonged waiting times had clinically relevant consequences for some patients. Improved pre-procedural information regarding postoperative recovery and better management of patient expectations during the waiting period may improve the overall patient experience.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Postoperative delirium is associated with accelerated brain ageing: an exploratory cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced age is a major risk factor for both delirium and dementia. A potential early biomarker for dementia is the brain-predicted age difference (brainPAD). We hypothesised that brain ageing accelerates after postoperative delirium (POD), and that increased brainPAD is associated with cognitive decline.
METHODS: Brain MRI scans were obtained in 287 older patients before and 3 months after major elective surgery, and two MRI scans at similar time intervals were obtained in 46 nonsurgical control participants. We computed grey matter brainPAD in patients with POD (POD+), patients without POD (POD-), and nonsurgical controls. The Trail Making Test (TMT) was administered at both time points to examine associations between changes in brainPAD and changes in attention/processing speed (TMT-A) and executive task switching (TMT-B and TMT B-A).
RESULTS: Compared with the POD- group, brainPAD increased by an additional 6 (sd=3) months over time in the POD+ group (P=0.002). For each 1 year-over-year increase in brain age gap, patients took 2.3 s longer to complete the TMT-A (P=0.016), whereas no association was observed with TMT-B (P=0.254) or TMT B-A (P=0.91).
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperativ edelirium is associated with accelerated brain ageing, which in turn is associated with decline in attention and processing speed. These findings help to understand the complex relationship between ageing, delirium, and dementia.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT02265263.

articles.title: Association of preoperative vaping-related disorder versus cigarette nicotine dependence with postoperative respiratory complications: a multicentre matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electronic cigarette aerosols may promote airway inflammation, bronchial hyperreactivity, and impaired mucociliary defence, but their perioperative respiratory safety remains uncertain. We examined whether preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide matched cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network database, comparing surgical patients with documented preoperative vaping-related disorder and cigarette nicotine dependence. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative respiratory complications, including pneumonia, respiratory failure, bronchospasm, noninvasive ventilation, and mechanical ventilation.
RESULTS: Among 3817 matched pairs, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of 30-day respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence (10.7% vs 5.1%, relative risk [RR] 2.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.79-2.49). Vaping-related disorder was also associated with increased risks of pneumonia (RR 3.20, 95% CI 2.40-4.28), respiratory failure (RR 2.48, 95% CI 1.98-3.10), bronchospasm (RR 1.92, 95% CI, 1.38-2.68), and noninvasive ventilation (RR 2.56, 95% CI 1.64-3.98). Vaping-related disorder combined with cigarette nicotine dependence was associated with a higher risk of respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence alone (RR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53), whereas vaping-related disorder alone showed a larger RR increase than neither diagnosis (RR 3.11, 95% CI 2.56-3.76).
CONCLUSIONS: Among surgical patients, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence. These findings suggest that vaping history should be specifically assessed during preoperative evaluation and considered in perioperative respiratory risk stratification.

articles.title: Preoperative roxadustat in major elective noncardiac surgery: a phase 2a randomised clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative complications remain a leading cause of mortality. Experimental data indicate that roxadustat, a first-in-class prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, reduces ischaemia-reperfusion injury, accelerates wound healing, and enhances survival in sepsis. Therefore, preoperative administration of roxadustat might reduce perioperative organ injury. We examined the perioperative tolerability and the potential for adverse surgical interactions with roxadustat.
METHODS: In this phase 2a, single-centre, double-blind, randomised-controlled pilot trial, 150 patients undergoing major elective noncardiac surgery were allocated to preoperative roxadustat 100 mg or placebo for three alternate-day doses, with the last dose on the operative morning. The co-primary outcomes were preoperative adverse events and postoperative complications meeting standardised endpoint definitions within 30 days.
RESULTS: Among 148 participants (52 [35.1%] females; median age 65 [range 24-84] yr) receiving at least one drug dose, at least one preoperative adverse event occurred in 21 of 75 (28%) in the roxadustat group and 20 of 73 (27%) in the placebo group (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.50-2.12). No serious adverse reactions occurred. Among 143 participants who proceeded to surgery (52 [36.4%] females; median age 65 [range 26-84] yr), ≥1 complication occurred in 23 of 74 participants (31%) who received roxadustat compared with 21 of 69 participants (30%) who received placebo (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.51-2.10). Days alive out of hospital within 30 days was similar between the groups. The annualised enrolment rate was 90 per year, with high levels of drug compliance.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative roxadustat was feasible in patients having major surgery. Uncertainty remains regarding the safety and efficacy of this intervention.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.anzctr.org.au; ACTRN12624000188538.

articles.title: Intraoperative peripheral perfusion index and mortality after noncardiac surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative haemodynamic monitoring primarily targets arterial pressure and flow but might not adequately reflect tissue perfusion. The peripheral perfusion index provides a continuous, noninvasive, and readily available indicator of peripheral perfusion, but its prognostic significance across surgical populations remains uncertain. We hypothesised that greater intraoperative exposure to low perfusion index would be associated with postoperative complications and mortality.
METHODS: In this prespecified multicentre cohort study using electronic health record data, we included adults (≥18 yr) undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery. The primary exposure was cumulative intraoperative area under a perfusion index of 1.5 expressed in PI⋅min. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. The secondary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative intensive care unit admission, reoperation, acute kidney injury, or prolonged hospital stay.
RESULTS: Among 399 842 patients undergoing 540 101 procedures, a total of 7066 (1.3%) deaths occurred within 30 days: 654 (0.5%) among procedures with no exposure, 1185 (0.6%) in the lower half of exposed procedures, and 5227 (2.6%) in the upper half (split at 3.8 PI⋅min). Compared with no exposure, the adjusted odds ratio for 30-day mortality was 2.18 (95% CI 1.98-2.40, overall association P<0.001) at the 95th percentile of exposure (42.5 PI⋅min), with similar patterns observed across the major surgical specialties. For the composite outcome, the corresponding odds ratio was 1.16 (95% CI 1.14-1.18; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Greater intraoperative exposure to low perfusion index was associated with higher postoperative mortality and complications in adult patients undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT07164339.

articles.title: Anesthesia Care-Team Staffing Ratios in the United States: Anesthesia Time and Billing Units: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs) in medically directed anesthesia care teams has expanded, but the implications for anesthesia time and billing units remain uncertain, especially in relation to staffing supervision ratios (number of CRNAs to anesthesiologist).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective fixed-panel observational study of unique surgical encounters spanning January 2018 through December 2024 using billing records from a large revenue cycle management company. The sample included encounters involving anesthesiologists, CRNAs, surgeons, and facilities across 47 states. We compared physician-alone cases with medically directed care-team cases using fixed-effects regression models. Outcomes included anesthesia minutes and anesthesia billing units (base, time, modifier, conditional, and total units). A Medicare subsample was analyzed for realized gross payments. Secondary analyses examined each encounter by the number of CRNAs the anesthesiologist medically directed simultaneously, that is, staffing ratios, to assess whether outcomes varied by level. Models adjusted for patient-, procedure-, surgeon-, facility-, and time-level factors.
RESULTS: Care-team cases were associated with longer anesthesia time (adjusted difference +1.67 minutes; 95% CI, 1.11-2.23; P < .001) and higher total billing units (adjusted difference +0.11 units; 95% CI, 0.04-0.18; P = .003) than cases performed by an anesthesiologist alone. Both differences increased with the staffing ratio. Relative to physician-alone cases, anesthesia time was shorter with 1 CRNA directed (-2.52 minutes; 95% CI, -3.22 to -1.83), similar with 2 CRNAs (-0.13 minutes; 95% CI, -0.69 to 0.43), and longer with 3 CRNAs (+3.03 minutes; 95% CI, 2.40-3.66) and 4 CRNAs (+6.99 minutes; 95% CI, 6.18-7.80); total billing units followed the same pattern (1 CRNA, -0.23; 2 CRNAs, -0.02 [not significant]; 3 CRNAs, +0.21; 4 CRNAs, +0.50). In a Medicare subsample, gross payments differed little overall (-$3.53; 95% CI, -$5.13 to -$1.92) and followed the same staffing-ratio gradient (1 CRNA, -$10.44; 4 CRNAs, +$3.74).
CONCLUSIONS: Medically directed CRNA care teams were associated with modestly longer anesthesia time and slightly greater billing-unit intensity than physician-alone care. These differences were small overall but increased with rising staffing ratios, indicating that the number of CRNAs directed concurrently is associated with measurable differences in anesthesia time and billing intensity.

articles.title: Etomidate vs Propofol for Anesthetic Induction: Association With 30-Day Mortality and Postoperative Complications in a Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Etomidate is commonly used for induction in hemodynamically unstable patients to preserve cardiovascular stability. However, concerns persist regarding potential adverse outcomes, including adrenal suppression and increased mortality. We evaluated whether intravenous anesthetic induction with etomidate was independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes as compared to propofol induction.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 155,667 adult surgical patients undergoing induction with etomidate or propofol at our academic health system. Patients younger than 18 years of age, those receiving preoperative mechanical ventilation, and those with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status VI were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes included sepsis, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), cardiogenic shock, and acute kidney injury (AKI). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, comorbidity, physiologic, and surgical factors. Given substantial baseline imbalance between induction groups, propensity score matching (1:1) using the same covariates was performed. Sensitivity analyses included adjustment for neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, complete-case analyses, and interaction testing.
RESULTS: A total of 155,667 patients met inclusion criteria, including 3846 (2.5%) who received etomidate and 151,821 (97.5%) who received propofol. Thirty-day mortality occurred in 1151 patients (0.74%). Unadjusted mortality was higher in the etomidate group (227/3846 [5.9%]) than in the propofol group (924/151,821 [0.61%]). After multivariable adjustment, etomidate use remained independently associated with increased 30-day mortality (aOR 1.44; 95% CI, 1.21-1.72; P < 0.001). Propensity score matching (n = 3832 per group) reduced the average standardized mean difference from 0.398 before matching to 0.023 after matching. The association persisted in the matched cohort (aOR 1.43; 95% CI, 1.14-1.78; P = 0.002), with observed mortality of 225/3832 (5.9%) among etomidate recipients and 157/3832 (4.1%) among propofol recipients, corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 1.8% and a number needed to harm of 56. In the matched cohort, etomidate was also associated with higher odds of sepsis (aOR 1.28; 95% CI, 1.08-1.52), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 1.24; 95% CI, 1.09-1.41), cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.56; 95% CI, 1.21-2.01), and acute kidney injury (aOR 1.27; 95% CI, 1.11-1.45). Post-induction hypotension was lower in the etomidate group (aOR 0.40, 95% CI 0.32-0.49; P < 0.001). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Etomidate induction was associated with increased 30-day mortality and major postoperative complications. Given the observational design, results should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Accelerated Biological Aging and Postoperative Complications After Major Orthopedic Surgery: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
Anticoagulation strategies for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: agents, intensity, and monitoring.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Anticoagulation is among the most challenging aspects of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), during which patients remain at risk of both bleeding and thrombosis. This review synthesizes current evidence across the three interconnected domains of anticoagulation: agent, intensity, and monitoring.
RECENT FINDINGS: Unfractionated heparin remains the first-line anticoagulant, although evidence supporting its superiority over alternative agents is limited. Direct thrombin inhibitors and, more recently, therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin have emerged as alternatives. Anticoagulation intensity has historically lacked standardized definitions, while observational data linking higher activated partial thromboplastin time values to bleeding have contributed to a shift toward lower anticoagulation targets. Available assays provide complementary rather than interchangeable information, and no single test reliably reflects anticoagulant effect or predicts outcomes, although anti-Xa is emerging as the most informative single assay for unfractionated heparin.
SUMMARY: Recent evidence supports reduced-intensity anticoagulation during contemporary ECMO, although the lower limit of safe anticoagulation remains undefined and no single agent, target, or assay is optimal for every patient. Anticoagulation should therefore be individualized by integrating agent, intensity, and monitoring according to patient characteristics, circuit performance, and the evolving balance between thrombosis and bleeding.

articles.title: Palmitoylethanolamide versus ibuprofen for acute postoperative pain after extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy: a randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), an endogenous lipid mediator, exhibits anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties, its efficacy as a stand-alone treatment for acute postoperative pain remains uncertain. This study compared oral micronized PEA with ibuprofen in managing pain following extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL).
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, double-blind investigation, 120 patients classified as ASA I-II undergoing elective ESWL were evaluated. They were randomly divided to take either 600 mg of oral micronized PEA or 600 mg of ibuprofen two hours prior to the procedure, continuing every 12 h for 72 h. The primary endpoint was postoperative pain intensity quantified by visual analogue scale (VAS) 2 h post-ESWL. Secondary endpoints included VAS scores at predefined intervals, rescue analgesia, adverse events, and patient satisfaction.
RESULTS: VAS scores were comparable between groups during the early postoperative period, including at 2 h (PEA: 1 [0-2] vs. ibuprofen: 1 [0-2], P = 0.091). However, pain was significantly higher with PEA at 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h (P < 0.001). Rescue analgesia was required more frequently with PEA (76.7% vs. 58.3%, P = 0.032), with greater cumulative opioid consumption (10.7 ± 2.2 vs. 9.4 ± 1.8 mg, P = 0.003). Gastrointestinal discomfort was more frequent with ibuprofen (21.7% vs. 1.7%, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this active-comparator trial, oral micronized PEA was inferior to ibuprofen at 12-48 h after ESWL, with more rescue analgesia, but early pain scores were similar. The analgesic effect of PEA itself cannot be established. Fewer gastrointestinal adverse events warrant further study.

articles.title: Clinical implementation of official ASA physical status examples: a questionnaire survey and multifaceted educational pre-post intervention study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS) classification is widely used, but subjective interpretations cause evaluation variability. Although specific clinical examples were added in 2014 and 2020 to reduce ambiguity, their clinical adoption remains unclear. We evaluated awareness of these examples and whether a multifaceted educational intervention was associated with scoring consistency.
METHODS: This two-phase study evaluated ASA-PS scoring consistency. In Study 1, 45 anesthesiologists at two institutions evaluated 20 simulated adult, pediatric, and obstetric cases to assess understanding of official ASA-PS examples. In Study 2, a pre- and post-intervention study in clinical practice included 414 cases. The intervention included survey feedback, re-dissemination of official examples, and implementation of a reference system in the electronic medical record. The primary outcome was the exact agreement rate between clinician-assigned and consensus scores based on official examples.
RESULTS: In Study 1, the overall correct rate with the official reference classifications was 47.6% (Cohen's kappa = 0.321). Correct rate was particularly low in pediatric cases (kappa = 0.243). Highly experienced anesthesiologists demonstrated lower correct rates and a tendency toward underestimation. In Study 2, the exact agreement rate increased from 73.5% before the intervention to 82.4% (OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.01-2.78) after the intervention. Cohen's kappa improved from 0.553 to 0.712, and underestimation decreased from 21.1% - 14.8%.
CONCLUSION: Publishing clinical examples alone may be insufficient to standardize ASA-PS classification. A multifaceted intervention incorporating educational feedback and an electronic reference system was associated with improved scoring consistency.

articles.title: Successful use of ultrasound-guided quadroiliac plane block for postoperative analgesia in a child undergoing percutaneous nephrolithotomy.
Volatile-free total intravenous anesthesia for elective circumcision in two school-age survivors of Crisponi/cold-induced sweating syndrome type 1.
Effect of fascial plane blocks providing postoperative analgesia on mechanical ventilation duration in the ıntensive care unit and early oxygenation after cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The primary objective of this study was to examine whether a combined pecto-intercostal fascial plane block (PIFB) and serratus anterior plane block (SAPB) influences the duration of mechanical ventilation in patients who underwent open cardiac surgery via median sternotomy with cardiopulmonary bypass. Secondary objectives included evaluating the effects of this analgesic approach on early postoperative oxygenation parameters, pain intensity scores, and overall opioid consumption.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study enrolled 206 adult patients who underwent open cardiac surgery through median sternotomy between January and July 2025. Participants were allocated into two groups based on the postoperative analgesic strategy employed: the Block group (G1, N.=107), which received combined PIFB and SAPB, and the Control group (G0, N.=99), which was managed with conventional multimodal analgesia. To minimize selection bias, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied using seven clinical covariates. Mechanical ventilation duration was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves, Cox proportional hazards regression, and the restricted mean survival time (RMST) method.
RESULTS: Patients in the Block group demonstrated a significantly shorter median duration of mechanical ventilation compared to controls (300 vs. 420 min; RMST difference: -65.8 min; 95% CI: -94.2 to -41.6; P<0.001). The incidence of prolonged intubation, defined as mechanical ventilation exceeding 480 minutes, was markedly lower in the Block group (G1=6.5% vs. G0=20.2%; Firth OR: 0.29; 95% CI: 0.11-0.75; P=0.011). Postoperative pain scores were significantly reduced across all assessment time points in the Block group (Benjamini-Hochberg corrected q<0.001), and total opioid requirements declined by approximately 28% (IRR: 0.719; P<0.001). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected with respect to the PaO<inf>2</inf>/FiO<inf>2</inf> ratio or the length of intensive care unit stay. CONCLUSİONS: The combined application of PIFB and SAPB was associated with a shorter duration of mechanical ventilation and lower opioid consumption following cardiac surgery. Incorporating fascial plane blocks into multimodal analgesia protocols may confer meaningful clinical benefits, particularly in patients considered to be at elevated perioperative risk.

articles.title: Association between serial perioperative oxygen reserve index measurements and postoperative pulmonary complications in patients at increased pulmonary risk undergoing non-thoracic surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We examined whether the previously observed association between preoxygenation (preoxy) oxygen reserve index (ORi) and postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) could be reproduced in an independent non-thoracic surgical cohort and whether later intraoperative ORi measurements provided additional information.
METHODS: We prospectively studied 155 patients aged ≥ 51 years undergoing elective non-thoracic surgery. ORi was measured at 1, 2, and 3 min of preoxy and at four intraoperative time points. The primary outcome was at least one PPC by postoperative day 30. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed associations and discrimination, respectively.
RESULTS: PPCs occurred in 57 patients (37%). ORi was lower at 2 and 3 min of preoxy in patients who developed PPCs, with no significant intraoperative differences. After adjustment for Assess Respiratory Risk in Surgical Patients in Catalonia (ARISCAT) score and other clinical covariates, 3-min ORi was inversely associated with PPCs (odds ratio, 0.06; 95%CI, 0.01-0.28; P < 0.001). The within-patient ORi-arterial partial pressure of oxygen correlation was 0.38 (95% CI, 0.27-0.47; P < 0.001). Area under the curve (AUCs) were 0.645 for ORi, 0.711 for ARISCAT, and 0.760 for the combined model. Adding ORi improved model fit (χ² = 10.82, P = 0.001), with ΔAUC 0.049 (95% bootstrap CI, -0.002 to 0.100).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoxy ORi, particularly at 3 min, was associated with PPCs. Although adding ORi to ARISCAT improved model fit, the gain in discrimination was modest and imprecisely estimated, supporting ORi as a complementary physiological marker rather than an alternative to established risk assessment.

articles.title: Low-dose carbon monoxide in cardiovascular surgery: mechanisms, monitoring, and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Carbon monoxide has been regarded as a toxic gas for a long time, however, recent studies have demonstrated that carbon monoxide, as an endogenous gaseous signaling molecule generated via the heme oxygenase system, plays an important regulatory role in various physiological and pathological processes. Physiologically, endogenous carbon monoxide production is approximately 400-500 μmol per day, whereas freely diffusible carbon monoxide remains very low, at about 0.002 μM, or approximately 2.5 ppm as an equivalent gas-phase concentration. At low concentrations, carbon monoxide exerts diverse biological effects, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, vasoregulatory, mitochondrial-modulating, and anti-remodeling actions. These properties are particularly relevant to cardiovascular surgery, especially procedures involving cardiopulmonary bypass, where systemic inflammation, ischemia-reperfusion injury, hemolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and microcirculatory disturbance contribute substantially to perioperative morbidity. During cardiopulmonary bypass, endogenous carbon monoxide production may increase and can be indirectly assessed by carboxyhemoglobin and exhaled carbon monoxide, suggesting a potential role for carbon monoxide-related measurements as dynamic biomarkers of hemolysis, inflammation, and surgical stress. In parallel, preclinical studies have shown that low-dose inhaled carbon monoxide and carbon monoxide-releasing molecules may alleviate inflammatory responses, preserve mitochondrial function, protect the vascular endothelium, and reduce cardiovascular surgery-related organ injury under controlled experimental conditions. Nevertheless, the translational application of carbon monoxide remains limited by its narrow therapeutic window, dose- and time-dependent biological effects, interindividual variability, and the need for rigorous perioperative monitoring. This review summarizes the sources, metabolism, molecular targets, and cardiovascular effects of carbon monoxide, with a focus on its monitoring value and therapeutic potential in cardiovascular surgery. We further discuss current evidence, safety considerations, and future directions for translating low-dose carbon monoxide and carbon monoxide-releasing strategies into perioperative cardiovascular care.

articles.title: Comparison of Single-Port and Two-Port Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery for Thymoma Resection.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the clinical efficacy and safety of single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (SP-VATS) versus two-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (TP-VATS) in patients undergoing thymoma resection.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data from 162 consecutive patients who underwent VATS thymoma resection at the Department of Thoracic Surgery, Beijing Chest Hospital, between August 2009 and March 2024. Patients were categorized according to the surgical approach into the TP-VATS group (n = 115) and the SP-VATS group (n = 47). Baseline clinical characteristics, perioperative safety outcomes, and surgical efficacy were systematically compared between the two groups. In addition, potential factors contributing to intraoperative conversion to thoracotomy were evaluated.
RESULTS: All patients successfully completed the planned surgical procedures and were discharged without perioperative mortality. In the TP-VATS group, one patient required intraoperative conversion to thoracotomy. Compared with the TP-VATS group, patients in the SP-VATS group experienced a significantly shorter operative time (median: 110 vs. 80 min, P = 0.013), lower intraoperative blood loss (median: 50 vs. 20 mL, P < 0.001), and a shorter postoperative hospital stay (median: 8 vs. 7 days, P = 0.029). Multiple linear regression analysis demonstrated that, in the clinical baseline model evaluating operative time (Model 1), SP-VATS was independently associated with a reduced operative duration, with unstandardized coefficient (B) of 19.99 (95% CI: 0.87-39.11, P = 0.041). Consistently, in the preoperative clinical assessment model (Model 2), SP-VATS remained significantly associated with operative time reduction B = 19.00, 95% CI: -0.44-38.45, P = 0.045).
CONCLUSION: Multiple linear regression modeling indicates that the choice of surgical approach influences perioperative risk profiles in patients undergoing thymectomy for thymoma. Compared with TP-VATS, SP-VATS was associated with a statistically significant but clinically modest reduction in operative time and estimated blood loss, while maintaining procedural safety. These findings suggest that SP-VATS represents an effective and favorable surgical option that thoracic surgeons may consider for thymoma resection; however, the clinical relevance of the observed reductions should be interpreted with caution. Further studies incorporating patient-centered outcomes and cost-effectiveness analyses are needed to determine the clinical importance of these perioperative differences.

articles.title: Lung ultrasound in congenital heart disease: from physiology to precision medicine.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Congenital heart disease (CHD) affects approximately 8 per 1000 births worldwide. Approximately 25% are classified as critical congenital heart disease (CCHD), requiring early diagnosis and neonatal intervention. Management of these patients is complex, dynamic and multiparametric. Respiratory complications are common during the hospitalization of patients with CHD. Lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a valuable bedside tool to accurately assess lung aeration, particularly in critically ill patients in whom conventional imaging techniques may be difficult to obtain, impractical, or challenging to interpret. Although growing evidence supports the use of LUS throughout the perioperative and postoperative period, its application remains insufficiently characterized. LUS is evolving beyond its traditional role as a diagnostic imaging modality toward a dynamic bedside monitoring tool, with the potential to guide and optimize respiratory management before, during, and after cardiac surgery.
CONCLUSION: This review aims to summarize the current evidence regarding the use of LUS in this population and to highlight its potential role in the assessment and management of preoperative and postoperative respiratory complications.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Lung ultrasound (LUS) is a bedside, radiation-free imaging technique that provides real-time information on pulmonary aeration, interstitial edema, pleural effusion, atelectasis, and pneumothorax in children with congenital heart disease (CHD). • Pulmonary abnormalities in CHD are closely related to the underlying hemodynamic physiology and may change dynamically throughout the preoperative, perioperative, and postoperative periods. However, the clinical application of LUS in this population remains heterogeneous and is not yet routinely integrated into CHD management.
WHAT IS NEW: • This review summarizes the current evidence on LUS in CHD from a pathophysiological perspective, linking ultrasound findings to the underlying cardiac physiology and highlighting potential pitfalls in their interpretation. • LUS may contribute to a precision-medicine approach in children with CHD by integrating bedside pulmonary phenotyping with clinical and echocardiographic assessment, while identifying key areas where prospective studies are needed to establish standardized protocols and determine whether LUS-guided management improves clinically relevant outcomes.

articles.title: The effects of perioperative intravenous balanced crystalloids versus normal saline on outcomes in patients undergoing craniotomy: A meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative fluid therapy in craniotomy requires balancing intracranial and systemic physiology. Normal saline (NS) is associated with hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis. While balanced crystalloids (BC) provide physiological buffering, their effects on cerebral relaxation remain unclear. This meta-analysis compares the effects of BC versus NS on metabolic parameters, intraoperative brain relaxation, and neurological outcomes in patients undergoing craniotomy.
METHODS: Medline, Embase, Scopus and Cochrane databases were searched up to 20 August 2026. Outcomes were meta-analysed with random-effects inverse-variance models, reporting mean differences (MD) or risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The GRADE framework was used to assess the certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: Twelve RCTs (n = 803) were analysed. BC and NS had no statistically significant differences in intraoperative brain relaxation (RR 0.94 95% CI: 0.83 to 1.08) (GRADE: +++), good neurological outcome at discharge (RR 1.08 95% CI 0.92 to 1.25) (GRADE: +), or mortality (RR 0.60 95% CI: 0.20 to 1.78) (GRADE + ). BC was associated with a reduced incidence of hyperchloremic acidosis (RR 0.15 95% CI 0.03 to 0.78) (GRADE: +++). At 24 h postoperatively, BC patients had higher arterial pH (MD 0.03 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.05) (GRADE: +) and increased bicarbonate (MD 2.24 mEq/L 95% CI: 0.54 to 3.93 mEq/L) (GRADE: +).
CONCLUSIONS: Balanced crystalloids improved acid-base and electrolyte profiles without significant differences in brain relaxation, neurological outcomes, or mortality. However, the certainty and clinical significance of these findings remain uncertain, highlighting the need for further adequately powered trials.

articles.title: Does the morphology of the mandibular lingula affect the location of the mandibular foramen?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate localization of the mandibular foramen (MF) is essential for successful inferior alveolar nerve block. The mandibular lingula (ML), a bony projection partially overlying the MF, is commonly used as an anatomical landmark; however, its morphology exhibits considerable variation. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between ML morphology and the spatial position of the MF using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT).
METHODS: This retrospective CBCT-based study analyzed 288 scans (144 females; mean age 51.0 ± 19.4 years) acquired between March 2023 and March 2025. ML morphology was classified into truncated, nodular, assimilated, and other types. Vertical and horizontal relationships between the ML, MF, mandibular borders, and oblique ridges were measured using multiplanar reconstruction. MF dimensions and the presence of accessory mandibular canals were also assessed. Inter- and intra-examiner reliability were evaluated. Statistical analysis included one-way ANOVA and independent t-tests, with significance set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: The nodular ML was the most prevalent morphology (60.76%). ML type did not significantly influence the vertical position or dimensions of the MF (P > 0.05). However, significant differences were observed in horizontal localization, particularly relative to the internal oblique ridge, with the assimilated ML type demonstrating a more posteriorly positioned MF (P < 0.05). Accessory mandibular canals, present in 5.56% of cases, were associated with significantly reduced horizontal distances to the MF.
CONCLUSION: ML morphology significantly influences its horizontal localization. Assimilated lingula and accessory mandibular canals may compromise the reliability of conventional landmarks.

articles.title: Attrition in neurosurgery residency: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Resident attrition creates a significant burden for trainees, residency programs, and the healthcare system. The global trends in attrition from neurosurgical residency have not been previously synthesized. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the global rate of attrition in neurosurgery residents and compare attrition in male and female trainees.
METHODS: We systematically searched Medline, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar for studies reporting on attrition in neurosurgical trainees. Results were pooled, analyzed using random-effects models, and are presented as Forest plots, pooled proportions, and relative risk. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used for risk of bias assessment, and the GRADE Working Group criteria was used for quality of evidence assessment.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included in systematic review, and four studies met the inclusion criteria for meta-analysis. The pooled estimated rate of attrition from neurosurgical residency was 0.13 (95% CI: 0.09-0.17), with significant between-study variation (I2 = 95.9%, p < 0.001). Attrition was higher among female compared with male residents (0.19 vs 0.11; p = 0.001), and females had nearly twice the probability of leaving neurosurgery compared to males (RR 1.92, 95% CI:1.35-2.73). Residents leaving neurosurgery most commonly transferred to radiology, anesthesiology, or emergency medicine, and most frequently left during the first two years of clinical training.
CONCLUSION: Neurosurgery residency has a high attrition rate, with an estimated 13% of residents leaving their program throughout residency training. The rate of attrition in female residents is nearly double the rate of attrition in male residents. Further research is warranted to understand factors which contribute most to attrition, particularly in females.

articles.title: Surgical and Cosmetic Outcomes After Fronto-Orbital Advancement With Hybrid Fixation for Unilateral Coronal Craniosynostosis: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fronto-orbital advancement (FOA) remains the standard surgical treatment for unilateral coronal craniosynostosis, particularly in patients presenting beyond the age window for endoscopic treatment and in those with significant frontal and orbital deformity. However, postoperative relapse, residual asymmetry, and fixation-related limitations remain important clinical concerns. Fixation strategies aim to provide immediate structural stability while minimizing potential interference with subsequent cranial growth.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate surgical, morphometric, cosmetic, and perioperative outcomes after FOA using a hybrid fixation strategy in patients with nonsyndromic unilateral coronal craniosynostosis.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 14 patients treated between January 2023 and December 2024 at the JSC National Center for Neurosurgery, Astana, Kazakhstan. All patients had CT-confirmed unilateral nonsyndromic coronal craniosynostosis and underwent primary FOA with combined fixation using biodegradable plates in key structural regions and absorbable sutures between individual remodeled bone fragments. Cosmetic outcomes were assessed using the Whitaker classification and clinician-rated Visual Analog Cosmetic Score (VACS), with each patient's VACS calculated as the mean of independent ratings from 10 assessors. Morphometric evaluation combined cephalic index (CI), as a measure of overall cranial width-to-length proportions, with frontal asymmetry index (FAI), orbital assessment, and nasal deviation angle (NDA). Perioperative safety outcomes and follow-up data were also analyzed.
RESULTS: The mean age at surgery was 16.7±12.9 months, and mean follow-up was 16 months (range 12-24). Favorable cosmetic outcomes were achieved in all patients: 92.9% were classified as Whitaker class I and 7.1% as class II, with no class III or IV outcomes or revision surgeries. Median postoperative VACS was 9.5 (range 6-10). FAI categories decreased in 10 of 14 patients (exact sign test, P=0.002; Holm-adjusted P=0.006). CI categories decreased in 6 patients (P=0.031; Holm-adjusted P=0.063), without establishing normalization of cranial shape. NDA categories showed no evidence of a directional change (P=0.625). All 14 patients received intraoperative autologous blood reinfusion and additional allogeneic blood transfusion. Mean total hospital stay was 18.9±3.5 days, including both preoperative and postoperative inpatient care. No major postoperative complications, cerebrospinal fluid leakage, surgical-site infection, relapse, or reoperation were observed.
CONCLUSION: Extended FOA with hybrid fixation was associated with favorable early cosmetic outcomes in this retrospective cohort. These findings describe the combined reconstructive procedure and do not establish the independent contribution of fixation, preservation of physiological cranial growth, or superiority over alternative fixation methods. Larger comparative studies with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: A Phase IB Study to Evaluate the Safety and Feasibility of Nivolumab or Nivolumab With Azacitidine in Patients With Recurrent, Resectable Osteosarcoma: A Report From the National Pediatric Cancer Foundation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Relapse rates following complete surgical resection (CSR) of pulmonary osteosarcoma recurrence remain high. We hypothesized that PD-1 inhibition with nivolumab (Nivo) combined with epigenetic priming using azacitidine (5-Aza) would be safe and augment systemic immune activation in patients with resectable pulmonary osteosarcoma relapse.
METHODS: This Phase I trial sought to establish the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D) of perioperative Nivo/5-Aza in patients ≤39 years old with isolated, resectable pulmonary osteosarcoma relapse. Three dose levels (DLs) were studied using a modified 3 + 3 design with dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) assessed from Day 1 of therapy to CSR. Patients received biweekly Nivo 3 mg/kg alone (DL1) or with 5-Aza at 60 or 75 mg/m2/day (DL2 and DL3) in 28-day cycles.
RESULTS: Twenty patients received therapy; 18 were evaluable for DLTs. DL3 exceeded the maximum tolerated dose (Grade 3 vomiting, prolonged Grade 4 neutropenia). Common adverse events included anemia, neutropenia, and nausea. Seventeen patients (85%) reached CSR after neoadjuvant therapy. Median event-free survival (EFS) was 3.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.7-7.7 months), and median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% CI: 10.1-42.6 months). Combination therapy was associated with evidence of systemic immune activation, including increases in IFN-γ, IL-1α, IL-1β, and CCL5.
CONCLUSION: The RP2D was Nivo 3 mg/kg and 5-Aza 60 mg/m2/day on Days 1-5 and 8-9. The combination was feasible and tolerable. EFS was limited in the context of a Phase I trial. These findings provide safety, feasibility, and exploratory immunologic data to inform future immunotherapy trials in osteosarcoma.

articles.title: Relationship between baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels and the incidence of maternal fever after epidural labor analgesia: A cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels and the incidence of maternal fever after epidural labor analgesia. Blood samples were collected from the median cubital vein, and serum IL-6 concentrations were measured using up-converting phosphor technology. Based on the IL-6 concentration results, parturients were categorized into 2 groups: the normal baseline IL-6 group and the elevated baseline IL-6 group. Demographic and clinical data including maternal age, gestational week, height, weight, body mass index, basal body temperature, intra-labor temperature, number of cervical examinations, duration of the first and second stages of labor, neonatal 1-minute and 5-minute Apgar scores, cesarean section rate, instrumental delivery rate, neonatal transfer, and mechanical ventilation were recorded. The overall incidence of intrapartum fever was higher in the elevated IL-6 group, and mean maternal temperature was also higher at 3 and 9 hours after analgesia (P < .05). No significant differences were observed in other indices (P > .05). Elevated baseline IL-6 was associated with a higher unadjusted incidence of intrapartum fever among women receiving epidural labor analgesia.

articles.title: Comparison of claims-defined postpartum depression after cesarean delivery under spinal versus epidural anesthesia: A nationwide propensity score-matched cohort study in Korea.
articles.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common and serious mental health disorder that adversely affects maternal well-being and early parenting. Although spinal and epidural anesthesia are widely used during cesarean section, their differential associations with PPD remain unclear. This nationwide retrospective cohort study used data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service between 2013 and 2022. Women who underwent cesarean section with either spinal or epidural anesthesia were included. Propensity score matching (1:1 nearest-neighbor without replacement) was applied to control for baseline differences. The primary outcome was claims-defined PPD within 1 year postpartum, identified by diagnostic codes or antidepressant prescriptions. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between the anesthesia type and PPD. The absolute difference in PPD proportions between the spinal and epidural anesthesia groups was approximately 0.69 percentage points (3.03% vs 2.33%, respectively). Epidural anesthesia was associated with significantly lower odds of PPD than spinal anesthesia (adjusted odds ratio, 0.833; 95% confidence interval, 0.740-0.938; P = .003), even after adjusting for clinical and sociodemographic confounders. Among women undergoing cesarean delivery, epidural anesthesia was associated with lower odds of PPD than spinal anesthesia. Further studies are needed to confirm this association and determine its clinical relevance.

articles.title: Feasibility of a two-point erector spinae plane block in standing mares.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thoracolumbar pain in horses involves multiple contiguous vertebrae. The erector spinae plane (ESP) block may provide multi-metameric desensitisation. A two-point technique could enhance cranio-caudal spread, but its feasibility and effects in horses are insufficiently characterised.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility, desensitisation, and motor impairment of a lidocaine two-point ESP block at Th15 and L1 in horses.
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective, randomised, blinded, controlled experimental study.
METHODS: Eight healthy unsedated mares received four ESP injections: 0.1 mL/kg lidocaine 2% at Th15 and L1 on one assigned side (LID group) and an equal volume of saline 0.9% contralaterally (SAL group). Feasibility was evaluated through ultrasound image quality and injection time. Desensitisation was assessed using noxious mechanical stimulation test from metamers Th14-L5 at four dorsoventral points (2 and 10 cm from the midline, coxal tuberosity, stifle) over 300 min. Motor impairment was scored at each time point using a 4-point ordinal scale. Data were summarised as mean ± SD or median (25th-75th percentiles) and compared using Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney U, and independent-samples t-tests (p < 0.05).
RESULTS: All injections were feasible with good-excellent image quality and no significant differences between Th15 and L1. Median injection times (minutes) were 3 (1-4.75) at Th15 and 2 (2.5-3.75) at L1. Lidocaine produced consistent multi-metameric desensitisation, whereas no desensitisation was observed in SAL group: the number of desensitised metamers was 3 (0-5) and 0 (0-0) (p = 0.001; 95% CI: 2-3) for LID and SAL groups, respectively. Lidocaine effects peaked at 30 min and lasted 270 min. Mild-moderate motor impairment occurred in 2/8 horses, resolving within 120 min.
MAIN LIMITATIONS: Small sample size and animal age may not be representative. Noxious mechanical stimulation testing may not reflect deep nociception.
CONCLUSIONS: The two-point ESP block was feasible, produced consistent multi-metameric somatic desensitisation and induced mild, transient motor impairment. Clinical evaluation is warranted.

articles.title: Misdiagnosis of Trigeminal Neuralgia and Inappropriate Prescribing of Carbamazepine and Its Derivatives in Headache Disorders.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to determine the rate of facial pain misdiagnosis leading to the use of CBZ, OXC or eslicarbazepine (ESL), along with the associated clinical features.
METHODS: We conducted a service evaluation of patients seen in a single tertiary-care headache centre to identify patients with any exposure to CBZ, OXC, or ESL from June 2014 to April 2024. Final diagnoses were reviewed and patients with inappropriate usage or previous misdiagnosis of trigeminal neuralgia were characterized.
RESULTS: Of the 226 patients prescribed CBZ/OXC/ESL, 190 had headache or neuralgia indications. Crucially, only 65 patients (34%) were appropriately prescribed for trigeminal neuralgia, SUNHA or other neuralgias. Eight patients misdiagnosed with trigeminal neuralgia and not exposed to CBZ/OXC/ESL were identified. Of those either inappropriately treated with CBZ/OXC/ESL or potentially-misdiagnosed-as-trigeminal neuralgia (n=133), migraine was among the most common (79%; 44% migraine only) final diagnosis. The main clinical features in those misdiagnosed were facial involvement of pain (75%), unilateral pain (69%), throbbing (55%), stabbing (34%), sharp pain (33%) and allodynia (66%). Adverse effects were seen in 59% on carbamazepine and 55% on oxcarbazepine.
DISCUSSION: In patients referred to a tertiary headache clinic, trigeminal neuralgia is over diagnosed and inappropriately treated with CBZ and its derivatives resulting in no useful clinical outcome and substantial side effects. Migraine with lateralised facial involvement is a common presentation resulting in this misdiagnosis.

articles.title: Characterizing relatives who provide surrogate consent for clinical research in the ICU: a multicenter sociodemographic profiling study (PICTURE-ICU).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surrogate consent for clinical research in the intensive care unit (ICU) is a complex process often influenced by psychological distress and the quality of communication. While some barriers are known, there is sparse quantitative data on how sociodemographic profiles relate to a consenting relative's perception of the decision-making process. This study aimed to characterize the distinct sociodemographic profiles among consenting relatives and to describe their perceptions regarding the surrogate consent process.
METHODS: We conducted an exploratory, observational, prospective, multicenter study across 14 French ICUs. A 30-item questionnaire (including an 18-item Likert-scale assessment and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale [HADS]) was administered to 125 relatives who had provided surrogate consent for a patient's inclusion in a research protocol. Data were analyzed using multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) followed by hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) to identify homogeneous respondent profiles.
RESULTS: Our analysis identified three distinct clusters of relatives. Cluster 1 (n = 4, 3.2% of the sample) comprised non-professionally active or unemployed individuals who reported lower levels of knowledge and ambivalence regarding their legitimacy to consent. Cluster 2 (n = 59) consisted of older spouses and retirees (aged 51-75 years) characterized by high trust in the healthcare team and a strong sense of legitimacy, despite reporting significant stress during the decision-making process. Cluster 3 (n = 62) was composed of younger, professionally active children of the patient (aged < 50 years) who reported higher healthcare knowledge, felt competent to judge risks and benefits, and prioritized the clarity of information received. Overall, HADS scores indicated moderate to high anxiety and depression across all clusters, though this was not directly attributed to the research participation itself.
CONCLUSIONS: This study offers a robust typology of consenting relatives in the ICU. It reveals three distinct sociodemographic profiles with specific communication needs, levels of trust, and decision-related stress. The findings can inform future research aimed at developing innovative pedagogical tools to tailor and personalize information as effectively as possible.

articles.title: Relative presence during brain death evaluation: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Bereavement following brain death declaration can be profoundly traumatic for relatives, and the outcomes associated with their presence during brain death evaluation warrant careful evaluation. Brain death can be declared while cardiopulmonary function is still mechanically maintained, a dissociation that can be difficult for families to reconcile with what they are told. This review aimed to assess whether relative presence during brain death evaluation affects family comprehension, psychological and grief-related outcomes, and organ donation consent. We conducted a systematic search across PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Nine studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising one randomized controlled trial, one prospective multicenter trial, one retrospective cohort study, two survey studies, three qualitative studies, and one case series. Across studies, family presence was consistently associated with better comprehension that death had occurred. The only randomized trial found no increase in psychological distress, measured with the Impact of Event Scale and General Health Questionnaire-12, among family members who were present compared with those who were absent. Most data on how often presence is offered predate current international guidance, and evidence on whether presence affects organ donation consent was inconclusive. The evidence base is small, methodologically heterogeneous, and concentrated in a few countries, resting on a single randomized trial. Where offered, family presence is consistently facilitated through a structured, staff-supported model rather than unstructured bedside access. Since 2014, only 22 patients' families have been studied at the bedside, although international guidance now encourages their presence. Larger, prospectively registered, multicenter trials reporting outcomes from relatives are needed to test these recommendations.

articles.title: Implementing model-informed precision dosing of antibiotics in critically ill patients: a case-study with electronic health record interfacing and comparative evaluation of the Tucuxi software for cefepime therapeutic drug monitoring.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) of antibiotics are recommended to optimize care, especially in critically ill patients. There is a need to develop and evaluate MIPD tools. The aim of this feasibility study was to describe the implementation of the Tucuxi software for MIPD of cefepime in intensive care units (ICU).
METHODS: An interface was created between the ICU electronic health record (ICCA, Philips) and the MIPD software Tucuxi. Cefepime concentrations from ICU patients were retrospectively analyzed with Tucuxi and BestDose. Bias, imprecision and agreement of estimated past concentration, future concentration to be observed on subsequent TDM occasions, and predicted dosages for achieving a target exposure were compared.
RESULTS: The interface was successful for importation of TDM data from ICCA into Tucuxi. The comparative evaluation was performed with data from 34 patients (89 cefepime concentrations). Upon the first TDM occasion, the median cefepime trough concentration was 19.2 mg/L, with 46% of values above 20 mg/L. The rate of overexposure decreased to 29% after the first MIPD round. In the estimation of all observed concentration, the fits of the two programs were comparable with mean prediction error of -0.7 ± 2.6 and - 1.2 ± 3.1 mg/L for BestDose and Tucuxi, respectively. Forecasting results were also similar (-2.2 ± 16.1 and - 4.2 ± 13.3 mg/L for BestDose and Tucuxi, respectively). Dosage requirements were also in agreement, except for two cases.
CONCLUSION: The Tucuxi software has been interfaced with ICCA and showed promising performance for cefepime MIPD in ICU.

articles.title: Updates on management of pretransplant and peritransplant infections: Guidance from the American Society of Transplantation Infectious Diseases Community of Practice.
articles.abstract: An expert panel of the American Society of Transplantation Infectious Diseases Community of Practice reviewed and updated guidance highlighting developments since the prior version published in 2019. A 5-article series provides guidance on screening, diagnosis, and treatment of infections in transplantation. This section focuses on donor and recipient screening and assessment of donor-derived infections, pretransplant ventricular assist device infections, and perioperative prophylaxis. The assessment and management of posttransplant infectious syndromes, including intra-abdominal infection, pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and diarrhea are presented. Recommendations are made based on the modified Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach.
