articles.title: Prevalence and prognosis of gait dysfunction in patients operated on for cervical spondylotic myelopathy: a Spine CORe™ analysis of QOD data.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Among patients undergoing surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM), the prevalence of gait disturbance and the likelihood of gait improvement remain unclear. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence and prognosis of gait disturbance in CSM and identify factors associated with gait improvement postoperatively.
METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of the CSM cohort of the prospectively collected 14-site Spine CORe™ Study Group Quality Outcomes Database (QOD) registry. Outcomes of interest included postoperative ambulatory function at 24 months defined by lower extremity score on the modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scale and predictors of improved ambulation. The p values for descriptive statistics were obtained using paired and unpaired t-tests and chi-square tests as appropriate. For multivariable analysis, a logistic regression model was fit for improvement in gait in the subset of patients with baseline gait impairment.
RESULTS: Of the 1141 patients meeting prespecified inclusion criteria, 1135 had baseline gait data; of these, 877 (77.3%) had baseline gait dysfunction and 258 (22.7%) did not. At baseline, patients with gait dysfunction were older (61.5 ± 11.6 vs 57.2 ± 11.7 years, p < 0.001), had higher BMI (30.4 ± 6.6 vs 29.3 ± 6.0 kg/m2, p = 0.008), were less likely to have private insurance (46.0% vs 67.4%, p < 0.001), and had more comorbidities. Preoperatively, patients with gait dysfunction had worse neck disability (Neck Disability Index [NDI], 41.0 ± 20.8 vs 30.2 ± 18.4, p < 0.001) and quality of life (EQ-VAS, 56.2 ± 21.4 vs 70.0 ± 18.9, p < 0.001; and EQ-5D, 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 0.7 ± 0.2, p < 0.001). Patients with impaired ambulation at baseline were less satisfied with surgery at 24 months (North American Spine Society satisfaction questionnaire [NASS] score 1, 51.4% vs 60.9%, p = 0.004). Among 596 patients with gait dysfunction who received follow-up postoperatively at 24 months, 304 (51.0%) showed improvement and 292 (49.0%) did not. Patients who improved also demonstrated greater improvement in visual analog scale (VAS) neck pain (-3.3 ± 3.2 vs -2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) and arm pain (-3.2 ± 3.9 vs -2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) scores, as well as better NDI (16.5 ± 17.4 vs 26.8 ± 20.9, p < 0.001), EQ-VAS (74.1 ± 20.0 vs 60.2 ± 23.2, p < 0.001), EQ-5D (0.8 ± 0.2 vs 0.6 ± 0.2, p < 0.001), and NASS (score 1, 74.0% vs 53.8%, p < 0.001) scores. Multivariable analyses revealed that lower BMI (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02, p = 0.01) and lower American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class (for ASA class I or II, OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.04-2.80, p = 0.04) were associated with gait improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, 77.3% of patients who underwent surgery for CSM demonstrated gait dysfunction preoperatively. Of these patients, 51% had gait improvement after cervical spine surgery. Lower BMI and ASA class were associated with improved gait postoperatively. Patients who improved reported superior quality of life, satisfaction with surgery, and decreased pain and disability.

articles.title: Monoportal endoscopic intrapelvic versus conventional anterior intrapelvic approach for acetabular fractures: a retrospective comparative study of early postoperative and radiographic outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The monoportal endoscopic intrapelvic (MEI) approach has recently been introduced as a minimally invasive alternative to the conventional anterior intrapelvic (AIP) approach for acetabular fractures. This study compared perioperative, radiographic, and early clinical outcomes between the MEI and AIP approaches.
METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study included 48 patients undergoing acetabular fracture fixation through an isolated intrapelvic approach (28 historical AIP and 20 MEI). Perioperative outcomes, radiographic reduction quality, postoperative pain, opioid consumption, mobilization, length of stay, and complications were compared. Multivariable regression analyses were adjusted for age, ASA score, polytrauma, both-column fracture pattern, and marginal impaction.
RESULTS: Compared with isolated AIP, MEI was associated with lower postoperative pain on day 1 (adjusted mean difference - 2.07, 95% CI - 2.90 to - 1.25; p < 0.001), lower transformed cumulative opioid consumption (adjusted ratio 0.15, 95% CI 0.06-0.42; p < 0.001), earlier mobilization (adjusted ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.39-0.89; p = 0.012), and shorter hospital stay (adjusted ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.40-0.75; p < 0.001). Estimated blood loss was numerically lower with MEI but did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (adjusted ratio 0.71, 95% CI 0.48-1.05; p = 0.087). No statistically significant difference was detected in postoperative radiographic reduction quality.
CONCLUSIONS: The MEI approach was associated with improved early postoperative recovery compared with conventional AIP, with no statistically significant difference detected in radiographic reduction quality. Larger prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings and further define the role of endoscopic intrapelvic fixation in acetabular fracture surgery.
articles.journal_full: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie

articles.title: Outcomes of a Multidisciplinary Lower Limb Fracture Care Pathway in a Tertiary Hospital: A 3-Year Experience of 1073 Geriatric Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Geriatric lower limb fractures place a significant burden on tertiary healthcare systems. This study evaluates the outcomes of a fast-track, multidisciplinary lower limb fracture care pathway implemented at a tertiary hospital in Singapore. This study aims to describe and compare the functional outcomes, mortality, and the comparative impact of time to surgery (TTS) across different geriatric lower limb fractures (knee, femur shaft, and ankle) within the pathway, using hip fractures as a benchmark.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of patients ≥ 65 years old with non-pathological, surgically-treated lower limb fractures admitted to a tertiary institution between December 2020 and April 2024. Primary outcomes included postoperative functional status assessed via Modified Barthel Index (MBI) scores and perioperative complications, while the secondary outcome was 12-month mortality. Multivariate regression analyses evaluated predictors influencing these outcomes.
RESULTS: The cohort predominantly consisted of hip fracture patients (82.2%), with knee (7.3%), ankle (5.4%), and femur shaft (5.1%) fractures comprising smaller groups. At 12 months, there were no significant differences in mortality across fracture types (overall mortality: 7.2%). Functional outcomes, measured by MBI scores, showed significant improvement over 12 months, with no significant difference between fracture types (p = 0.32). Multivariate analysis identified younger age, female gender, higher pre-fracture MBI scores, and lower clinical frailty scores as positive predictors of 12-month functional outcomes. Early surgery (< 48 h) was significantly associated with better 12-month functional outcomes in knee fracture patients. TTS (< 48 h) significantly influenced mortality outcomes in hip fractures only.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings describe comparable functional outcomes and mortality across fracture types and outcomes observed for a broader range of lower limb injuries beyond hip fractures are favorable under a coordinated multidisciplinary care pathway.

articles.title: Preoperative depressive symptoms predict long-term mortality and early functional recovery after osteoporotic hip fracture: a 3-year cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Depressive symptoms are common in older adults with osteoporotic hip fracture, but their impact on long-term outcomes remains unclear. In this cohort study, preoperative depressive symptoms were associated with increased 3-year mortality and poorer early functional recovery. These findings highlight the importance of psychological assessment in the management of fragility fractures.
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between preoperative depressive symptoms and postoperative mortality and functional recovery in older adults with hip fracture.
METHODS: This secondary analysis was based on a prospective cohort of patients aged ≥65 years undergoing surgical treatment for hip fracture. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) within 24 hours of admission, with a cutoff score of ≥5. Mortality and functional recovery were evaluated at 30-day, 120-day, 1-year, and 3-year follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models and multinomial logistic regression were used after adjustment for potential confounders.
RESULTS: Among 1092 patients, 93 (8.5%) had PHQ-9 ≥ 5. Preoperative depressive symptoms were not associated with short-term mortality but were independently associated with increased 3-year mortality (HR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.05-2.36). Patients with PHQ-9 ≥ 5 had significantly poorer functional recovery at 30-day, 120-day, and 1-year follow-up, whereas no independent association was observed at 3 years.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative depressive symptoms were associated with increased long-term mortality and poorer early functional recovery. These findings support the role of early psychological assessment in perioperative risk stratification.

articles.title: Analysis of factors hindering the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: A qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) have a high incidence of perioperative hypothermia due to anesthetic suppression of thermoregulation, prolonged surgical duration, and diminished endogenous thermoregulatory function, which can lead to poor outcomes. Effective prevention of hypothermia is a critical clinical issue; however, previous studies have lacked in-depth analysis of comprehensive continuous management and practical barriers.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify barriers to the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly THA patients.
METHODS: A qualitative study design was employed, conducted from January to February 2026 at a Grade III Level A hospital in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Using purposive sampling, anesthesiologists (n = 5), anesthesia nurses (n = 5), and operating room nurses (n = 5) were recruited as participants. Semi-structured face-to-face interviews were conducted, and data were analyzed using content analysis with the assistance of NVivo 12.0 software.
RESULTS: A total of 3 themes and 5 subthemes were identified: (1) System and process level: The warm chain management process requires improvement, and the allocation of key warming resources needs to be strengthened; (2) Human resources and team atmosphere level: Nursing staffing needs to be reinforced, and a positive organizational culture requires cultivation; (3) Multidisciplinary collaboration and continuous improvement level: The multidisciplinary collaboration platform and continuous improvement system remain inadequate.
CONCLUSION: Diverse factors hinder the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly THA patients. Managers should implement improvements across three dimensions-system processes, human resources and team atmosphere, and multidisciplinary collaboration-to explore perioperative temperature management strategies and promote quality improvements in hypothermia prevention and control.

articles.title: Advances in obstetric anesthesia care in patients with severe cardiac comorbidities.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to update the reader about recent clinical practice recommendations in caring for the cardio-obstetric patient.
RECENT FINDINGS: The emergence of pregnancy heart teams has facilitated multidisciplinary communication for caring for a pregnant patient with cardiac disease. The utilization of noninvasive diagnostic modalities such as brain natriuretic peptide and bedside transthoracic echocardiography can yield quick actionable results regarding therapeutic options. Vaginal delivery remains the preferred mode of delivery for the vast majority of pregnant patients with cardiovascular disease. Timely and effective use of mechanical circulatory support in pregnancy can be beneficial for patients in cardiogenic shock or decompensated heart failure.
SUMMARY: Anesthesiologists are essential team members within the pregnancy heart team and should familiarize themselves with the evidence-based guidelines for caring for pregnant patients with cardiac disease.

articles.title: State of the art in analgesia techniques for lung transplantation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Pain associated with lung transplantation (LTx) is complex and can adversely affect patient recovery, satisfaction, and outcomes. Despite advances in surgical technique and perioperative care, management of LTx-related pain remains challenging. This review highlights contemporary analgesia techniques in LTx and discusses chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) after LTx.
RECENT FINDINGS: Fascial plane blocks are viable options to aid with pain control for LTx. The use of liposomal bupivacaine for intercostal blocks may not be inferior to thoracic epidural analgesia. Cryoablation of intercostal nerves may reduce early opioid requirements and pain, but long-term safety and efficacy are not known. Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols for LTx have been reported, but there is still significant variability in pain management strategies.
SUMMARY: Perioperative analgesia for LTx is anchored on optimizing multimodal, opioid-sparing approaches. There is more diversity in regional anesthetic techniques and nonopioid medications for this purpose. ERAS for LTx is evolving but has not been widely adopted. Significant knowledge gaps remain, and focused research is needed to better understand the impact of current techniques, identify ways to improve them, and develop alternative strategies to optimize individualized care.

articles.title: The right heart matters: contemporary right ventricular monitoring during thoracic surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Right ventricular dysfunction contributes to perioperative cardiovascular instability during thoracic surgery. General anesthesia, positive-pressure ventilation, one-lung ventilation, and pulmonary vascular manipulation or resection can rapidly alter right ventricular loading. This review examines contemporary strategies to identify right ventricular vulnerability, assess reserve, and monitor perioperative adaptation.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recent literature emphasizes right ventricular adaptation to load rather than resting function or pulmonary artery pressure alone. Multiparametric echocardiography integrates chamber size, systolic performance, septal geometry, tricuspid regurgitation, and right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling. Functional capacity and clinical findings provide complementary preoperative risk information. Stress echocardiography interrogates reserve, while advanced imaging and congestion measures characterize function and systemic consequences. Intraoperatively, pressure, cardiac output, imaging, congestion, and tissue perfusion should be reassessed across key physiologic transitions.
SUMMARY: Perioperative assessment should determine whether the right ventricular can tolerate the additional load imposed by anesthesia and surgery. Integrated monitoring may identify maladaptation and guide escalation of support. Proposed assessment during a clinically indicated preceding procedure requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Emergence agitation in children undergoing general anaesthesia: Clinical risk factors and perioperative management.
articles.abstract: Emergence agitation is a psychiatric disturbance that occurs during recovery from general anaesthesia. In paediatric populations, reported incidence ranges from 20% to 80%. Inadequate management of emergence agitation not only poses risks of injury to the child but also reduces parental satisfaction. This article synthesises current evidence on the diagnosis, underlying mechanisms, risk factors, and preventive and therapeutic strategies for paediatric emergence agitation, with the aim of improving postoperative recovery and providing a practical reference for reducing its incidence in clinical practice.

articles.title: Centralized Pain Phenotyping Before Spinal Cord Stimulation: Outcome Definition and Predictive Uncertainty.
Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Agonists or Tezepelumab for Obesity-Associated Asthma: A Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Obesity is associated with poor asthma outcomes. GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists induce weight loss and dampen airway inflammation independent of pathways currently targeted by biologics.
OBJECTIVE: To compare differences in respiratory outcomes and weight loss between GLP-1-based medications and tezepelumab in asthma patients without diabetes.
METHODS: A retrospective study was performed in a multi-institutional electronic health record database. Patients with specialist-treated, obesity-associated, moderate-to-severe asthma with at least one severe exacerbation in the prior year who initiated liraglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide, or tezepelumab between January 1, 2022 and December 31, 2025 were identified. Prevalent diabetes was excluded. Patients were followed for subsequent exacerbations, rescue inhaler prescriptions, respiratory-related healthcare encounters, and time to greater than 10% loss in body mass index. Overlap weighting accounted for imbalance in baseline asthma and obesity characteristics.
RESULTS: 2779 patients were identified, of whom 133 initiated liraglutide, 1770 semaglutide, 472 tirzepatide, and 404 tezepelumab. In weighted estimates, patients starting tirzepatide experienced a lower hazard of severe exacerbation compared to tezepelumab (weighted hazard ratio [wHR] 0.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.24-0.70); those starting semaglutide had a similar hazard (wHR 0.99; 95% CI 0.70-1.39). Tirzepatide and semaglutide initiators attained >10% reduction in BMI sooner, had less need for rescue inhalers, and had fewer subsequent respiratory-related encounters compared to tezepelumab.
CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1-based medications, and in particular dual-incretin GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, may have comparable effectiveness to biologic therapy among patients with associated obesity without diabetes. Clinical trials are necessary to validate findings in this observational study.

articles.title: Robotic Versus Endoscopic Approach in Single-port Nipple-sparing Mastectomy With Direct-to-implant Prepectoral Breast Reconstruction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compares surgical and implant-related outcomes between robotic and endoscopic approaches in single-port nipple-sparing mastectomy with direct-to-implant prepectoral breast reconstruction.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 54 patients undergoing nipple-sparing mastectomy with prepectoral reconstruction were divided into a robotic group (n = 21) and an endoscopic group (n = 33). Perioperative variables, including operative time, blood loss, drainage duration, hospital stay, and costs, as well as postoperative complications, were analyzed and compared between the 2 groups.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 4.45 months for the robotic group and 8.73 months for the endoscopic group. The robotic approach required significantly longer operative time (244.32 ± 43.10 versus 178.72 ± 47.53 min, P < 0.001) and incurred substantially higher cost (US $14,464.77 ± $503.38 versus $10,303.79 ± $1017.26, P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in intraoperative blood loss, length of hospital stay, drainage duration, or postoperative complication rates between the 2 groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted nipple-sparing mastectomy with direct-to-implant prepectoral reconstruction is currently associated with longer operative time and higher cost compared with the endoscopic approach. Larger prospective studies with extended follow-up are needed to assess its oncological safety and aesthetic outcomes.

articles.title: Balancing Feasibility and Validity: A Delphi Consensus on Frailty Assessment Tools in Perioperative Care.
Interpretable Machine Learning for Predicting Risk Factors for Chronic Postsurgical Pain After Cesarean Delivery: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) after cesarean delivery can severely impair the mother's quality of life and her ability to care for the infant. The aim of this study was to develop and validate a high-performance, interpretable, machine learning-based prediction model to identify high-risk factors for chronic incisional pain at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively and chronic non-incisional pain at 12 months postoperatively. A total of 678 patients who underwent elective cesarean delivery at our hospital were included in the prospective study. A total of 38 preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative variables, including demographic characteristics, psychological scale scores, and anesthesia/analgesia regimens, were collected. We combined the Boruta algorithm, recursive feature elimination, and the Mantel test for feature selection and constructed a high-performance machine learning-based prediction model (MLPM-CPSP-CD). The incidence of chronic incisional pain at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively was 12.39%, 9.73%, and 7.96%, respectively, whereas the incidence of chronic non-incisional pain was 24.04%. The MLPM-CPSP-CD model demonstrated excellent predictive performance. The core high-risk factors for postoperative chronic incisional pain were SQ-6 (history of dysmenorrhea), SH-5 (patient-controlled analgesia [PCA] pump pressing frequency), and SH-6 (PCA opioid consumption). This study provides an important foundation for developing and optimizing perioperative pain management strategies.

articles.title: Bedside electromagnetic neuronavigation for cranial access procedures in neurotrauma and neurocritical care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bedside cranial access devices (external ventricular drain (EVD), subdural evacuation port system (SEPS), parenchymal intracranial pressure (ICP) monitor) are foundational to neurotrauma and neurocritical care. Craniometric-based techniques are limited by aberrant anatomy, clot-filled ventricles, and complex extra-axial collections. Bedside electromagnetic (EM) neuronavigation registered to computed tomography (CT) imaging may enable precise targeting without requiring transport to the operating room, general anesthesia, or rigid cranial fixation.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients undergoing bedside cranial procedures with EM-neuronavigation (Medtronic StealthStation) from November 1, 2025 to July 21, 2026 at our Level I trauma center neurocritical care unit for distorted anatomy, atypical targets, and/or high consequences of imprecision. Outcomes included device function, post-procedure neuroimaging confirmation of device placement, and navigation-related complications.
RESULTS: Ten patients underwent 15 EM-navigated bedside procedures (11 EVDs, 2 SEPS, 2 parenchymal ICP monitors). Clinical indications included aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, traumatic brain injury, loculated subdural hematoma, ventriculitis, ventricular trapping, obstructive hydrocephalus, and intracerebral hemorrhage. Notably, EM-navigation enabled dual-catheter placement to access non-communicating ventricular compartments and optimized SEPS placements at maximal extra-axial collection thickness while avoiding vascular membranes. All procedures achieved intended device function and intended positioning on post-procedure imaging. There were no complications or revision procedures related to EM-navigation.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center proof-of-principle series, bedside EM-navigation was feasible, safe, and readily integrated into high-risk patient care workflows in neurocritical care. Whether bedside neuronavigation improves procedural precision, supports clinician education, or reduces operative and transport needs was beyond the scope of the current study and requires well-designed prospective evaluation.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level V, Therapeutic/Care Management.

articles.title: A Machine Learning-Based Early Warning System for Renal Replacement Therapy in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal replacement therapy (RRT) is a life-saving intervention for acute kidney injury in the intensive care unit (ICU). The decision to initiate RRT remains highly complex and subjective. Accurate and timely predictions for the need of RRT initiation are crucial components of personalized care. Using time series patient data (vital signs, laboratory findings, medications, ventilator settings, intake/output, risk scores), we aimed to develop machine learning (ML) models for predicting future initiation of RRT.
METHODS: Using data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-III, MIMIC-IV, and Electronic ICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU), we trained and internally validated models using dataset-specific training, validation, and test splits. We externally validated model performance using held-out eICU hospitals excluded from model development and a temporally distinct cohort of ICU patients admitted during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic period (2020-2022). Models were developed for: (1) screening patients for prediction of the need for RRT after their first 12 hours in the ICU; and (2) real-time dynamic prediction of the likelihood of documented RRT initiation within the next 24 hours.
RESULTS: Here, we summarize the results of the ML model aimed at screening patients for early prediction of RRT. In internal validation, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.90 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.886-0.906) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.53 (95% CI, 0.496-0.564) in MIMIC-III. Results were similar in MIMIC-IV and eICU. External validation on ICU patients admitted during the coronavirus disease (COVID) period yielded an AUROC of 0.90 (95% CI, 0.894-0.913) and an AUPRC of 0.57 (95% CI, 0.534-0.602). Additional hospital-level external validation across eight individual eICU hospitals showed AUROCs ranging from 0.86 to 0.91 and AUPRCs ranging from 0.35 to 0.52. Accuracy ranged from 0.78 to 0.84 across validation experiments.
CONCLUSION: By accurately identifying patients at high risk for RRT initiation, the early prediction ML model could serve as a triage tool to prompt closer nephrology evaluation or optimization of fluid and hemodynamic management before overt renal failure develops.

articles.title: Peripheral Warming Versus Earlobe Measurement for Pulse Oximetry in Critically Ill Patients With Impaired Peripheral Perfusion.
Left Paratracheal Pressure versus Cricoid Pressure During Airway Management: A Focused Synthesis of Randomized Evidence.

Disparities in Regional Analgesia Utilization for Rib Fractures: Hospital-Level Variation, Trends, and Clinical Outcomes in a Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study 2016 to 2022.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Regional analgesia is recommended for rib fractures, but utilization remains low. The extent to which hospital-level factors drive utilization and influence patient outcomes is unclear. This study's objective was to evaluate associations between hospital characteristics and regional analgesia receipt and outcomes.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS) of adult hospitalizations (>18 years) between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2022 with rib fractures. Exposures included hospital bed-size, ownership, teaching status and geographic region. Primary outcome was regional analgesia receipt. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and tracheostomy.
RESULTS: 250,630 hospitalizations met inclusion criteria, of which 7,179 (2.9%) received regional analgesia. After adjustment, 23.9% of variation in utilization was attributable to between-hospital differences. Greater utilization was associated with large hospital bed-size (odds ratio [OR] 2.08; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.80-2.39), urban teaching-status (OR 1.39; 95% CI, 1.19-1.62), higher income-quartile (OR 1.21; 95% CI, 1.10-1.33), and private insurance (OR 1.24; 95% CI, 1.14-1.35). Lower odds were observed in private nonprofit (OR 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65-0.86) and for-profit hospitals (OR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.34-0.53) compared with government hospitals. Regional analgesia utilization varied geographically, with the highest utilization in New England. Private insurance, White race, highest income quartile, government ownership and urban teaching status were also associated with earlier receipt of regional anesthesia. Disparities by insurance and hospital characteristics either persisted or widened from 2016 to 2022.Regional analgesia was associated with lower mortality (OR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.42-0.64) and tracheostomy (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.36-0.63) in multivariable analysis. In instrumental variable analysis with leave-one-out hospital-year regional analgesia rate as the instrument, these associations were attenuated.
CONCLUSIONS: Regional analgesia remains infrequently utilized for rib fractures, with marked variation across hospitals. Access and outcomes appear to depend substantially on where patients receive care. Understanding the institutional and provider-level factors underlying this variation represents an important target for future quality-improvement and implementation efforts.

articles.title: Management of unintended dural puncture and postdural puncture headache in obstetrics: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Unintended dural puncture during epidural catheter placement for labor analgesia is uncommon but may result in postdural puncture headache, neurologic complications, psychological morbidity, and chronic head and back pain. This narrative review translates recent multisociety and intrathecal catheter guidelines, supplemented by contemporary observational and meta-analytic evidence, into practical point-of-care decision support for anesthesia clinicians. No procedural technique has been shown to reliably prevent unintended dural puncture. When it occurs, either performing a repeat epidural procedure or threading an intrathecal catheter may be appropriate; neither approach is clearly superior or reliably prevents postdural puncture headache. Safe management requires individualized pathway selection, cautious incremental neuraxial dosing, clear intrathecal or epidural catheter labeling, close hemodynamic monitoring, structured handover, and readiness to treat high or total spinal anesthesia. Current evidence does not support routine prophylactic epidural blood patch, prolonged intrathecal catheterization, or pharmacologic prophylaxis. Evaluation of postpartum headache should begin with screening for warning features and alternative diagnoses before postdural puncture headache is assumed. Conservative measures remain first-line treatment, whereas epidural blood patch is appropriate for moderate-to-severe or refractory symptoms, symptoms that limit daily activities, or when neurologic features are present. Because postdural puncture headache is associated with serious neurologic and psychological morbidity and chronic pain, care should include written discharge instructions, defined follow-up until symptom resolution, communication with primary care clinicians, and prompt imaging or specialist referral when symptoms are atypical, progressive, or refractory.

The Development and Implementation of an Academic Mentorship Program.
Incidence and Risk Factors of Postoperative Delirium in Patients with Lung Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent neurological complication after lung cancer surgery and is associated with delayed recovery, cognitive decline, prolonged hospitalization, and increased mortality. However, its incidence and risk factors remain inconsistent across studies. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled cumulative incidence of POD and identify associated risk factors in patients undergoing lung cancer surgery. Nine databases were searched from inception to August 12, 2025, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) checklist. Eleven studies involving 5,575 patients were included. The pooled cumulative incidence of POD was 12% (95% confidence interval (CI): [0.08, 0.16]), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 96.3%, P < 0.001). Subgroup analyses identified significant variation in cumulative incidence across countries, whereas differences by diagnostic tool and surgical type were less conclusive. The incidence was higher in studies from China than in those from Japan, and heterogeneity disappeared in the thoracoscopic radical-resection subgroup. Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis showed that the pooled cumulative incidence remained stable, ranging from 10% to 13%. Significant risk factors included thoracotomy, age ≥75 years, higher American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) classification, prolonged one-lung ventilation, history of coronary heart disease, and history of sedative medication use. Compared with PaO₂ ≤ 60 mmHg, PaO₂ levels of 60 < PaO₂ ≤ 80 mmHg and 80 < PaO₂ ≤ 100 mmHg were associated with lower odds of POD. POD occurs in approximately one in ten patients after lung cancer surgery, highlighting the need for early identification and targeted perioperative prevention.

articles.title: Practice patterns of midazolam administration in patients undergoing cardiac-related non-operating room procedures: analysis of a US anaesthesia database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Midazolam can be administered as an anxiolytic, a cardio-stable sedative, or an anaesthetic agent during non-operating room anaesthesia (NORA) procedures. Guidelines suggest avoidance in older or frail patients, and current practices are unknown. We hypothesised that there would be significant variation in midazolam administration for cardiac-related NORA procedures by attending and institutional characteristics, in addition to patient characteristics.
METHODS: This is a retrospective observational analysis of a multi-institution US-centric electronic health record dataset including all adult patients undergoing cardiac-related NORA procedures in the Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group database from 2015 to 2022. The primary aim of the study was to identify the proportion of total variance in midazolam administration attributable to patient-, attending-, and institutional-level factors. The secondary aim was to identify practice pattern variations in the dosage and timing of midazolam administration. The primary outcome was any midazolam administration ≤1 h before anaesthesia start to 1 h after anaesthesia end. Secondary outcomes included total dose and timing of midazolam administration. Variance in midazolam administration attributable to patient, attending, and institutional factors was calculated with intraclass correlation coefficients following multilevel mixed-effects generalised linear models, in which a three-level nesting structure was assumed: patients nested within attendings and attendings nested within institutions. For the primary outcome, a binomial distribution and logit link function was specified. For the secondary outcome of total midazolam, the same three-level nesting structure was used, and covariates were modelled using a multilevel mixed-effects model specifying a Gaussian distribution and identity link function.
RESULTS: A total of 246 918 cardiac-related NORA procedures with care provided by 5212 unique anaesthesia attendings across 63 institutions with a median case volume of 9 (inter-quartile range [IQR] 2-37) were included in the analysis. Midazolam was administered in 33.0% of patients (n=81 602), including 25.5% of patients aged ≥65 yr (n=40 469). Midazolam administration declined from 50.7% of patients in 2015 to 29.0% in 2022 (P<0.001). The median dose was 2 mg (IQR 2-2), with 89.9% administered before procedure start. For transoesophageal echocardiography procedures, it was estimated that 37.0% of midazolam administration (30.4-44.3) was attributable to attending variation and 26.4% (19.2-35.2) to the institution, assuming that 36.6% of the variation was attributable to known patient factors. For transcatheter/endovascular procedures, attending, institution, and patient factors accounted for 45.7% (39.0-52.6), 27.7% (19.7-37.4), and 26.6%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Although patient-level factors accounted for a meaningful proportion of variability, substantial variation in midazolam administration was also attributable to attending- and institution-level factors. Further studies on clinical outcomes and patient experience associated with this type of midazolam administration have the potential to inform future practice.

articles.title: Predictive performance of bedside physiological parameters for the failure of prophylactic non-invasive ventilation after extubation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extubation failure is associated with increased mortality. Whether bedside physiological variables can identify patients at risk of reintubation during prophylactic NIV after extubation is unknown.
METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of a multicenter physiological study, 60 hypoxemic adults at high risk of extubation failure underwent two 1-hour NIV sessions after planned extubation, with oronasal and full-face masks in randomized crossover order. We assessed the magnitude of airway occlusion pressure (Pocc), the esophageal pressure swing (ΔPes), SpO₂/FiO₂, respiratory rate, tidal volume, dynamic lung elastance (EL,dyn), ROX index [(SpO₂/FiO₂)/respiratory rate] and the pressure-oxygenation index (POX, SpO₂/FiO₂ divided by Pocc). Prophylactic NIV failure was reintubation for respiratory failure within 7 days. Discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis.
RESULTS: Fourteen patients (23%) experienced NIV failure. Pocc yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.83 (95% CI, 0.71-0.95) with the oronasal mask and 0.83 (95% CI, 0.72-0.95) with the full-face mask, showing greater discriminative performance than tidal volume (AUCs, 0.55 and 0.53), respiratory rate (0.54 and 0.38), SpO₂/FiO₂ (0.51 and 0.50), and the ROX index (0.54 and 0.38; all p < 0.05). By contrast, the discriminative performance of Pocc did not differ from that of EL,dyn (AUCs, 0.72 and 0.73; p = 0.08 and 0.11), POX (AUCs, 0.82 and 0.81; p = 0.68 and 0.29), or |ΔPes| (AUCs, 0.83 and 0.82; p = 1.00 and 0.64).
CONCLUSIONS: During prophylactic NIV, Pocc discriminated NIV failure better than conventional bedside variables, with no detectable difference from directly measured inspiratory effort. External validation is required.

articles.title: Infection Rates Following Ultrasound-Guided Microinvasive Carpal Tunnel Release: A Single-Practice Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative infection following carpal tunnel release (CTR) is uncommon, although reported rates vary because of differences in outcome definitions and follow-up methodology. As ultrasound-guided and microinvasive CTR techniques continue to emerge, infection-specific outcomes remain inconsistently reported. The purpose of this study was to determine the rate of clinically significant postoperative infection following ultrasound-guided microinvasive CTR (Micro-CTR) and to contextualize this rate against published benchmarks.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed of consecutive adults undergoing office-based ultrasound-guided Micro-CTR in a single practice. All procedures were performed under local anesthesia using a standardized ultrasound-guided technique with percutaneous access and real-time visualization of the transverse carpal ligament and surrounding neurovascular structures. The primary outcome was clinically significant infection, defined as infection involving the palmar compartment requiring medical or surgical intervention. Secondary outcomes included localized superficial infection at the puncture site. Infection rates were calculated with 95% confidence intervals and compared descriptively with published data across CTR techniques.
RESULTS: A total of 476 patients contributed 533 procedures. Clinically significant infection occurred in one case (0.19%; 95% CI, 0.005-1.04). No localized superficial infections were identified. No cases required hospital admission or additional operative management. The observed rate was interpreted descriptively alongside published infection benchmarks across CTR techniques.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinically significant infection following ultrasound-guided Micro-CTR was rare in this single-practice cohort. The observed rate was interpreted descriptively alongside published benchmarks across established CTR techniques. Standardized, clinically meaningful outcome definitions may improve comparison of infection risk as less invasive approaches continue to emerge.
TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic IV.
articles.journal_full: Journal of hand surgery global online

articles.title: Trends in Medications for Opioid Use Disorder Before Surgery Among Medicaid Beneficiaries.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Opioid overdose is a leading cause of preventable death in the US, yet there is widespread underuse of medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD), including buprenorphine, methadone, and extended-release naltrexone. Surgical care is a frequent health care encounter where continuity of MOUD use can influence perioperative safety and long-term outcomes. National data assessing trends in preoperative MOUD use are unavailable among Medicaid patients, who account for a disproportionate share of patients with opioid use disorder.
OBJECTIVE: To assess national trends in the prevalence of preoperative MOUD use among Medicaid patients undergoing surgery, overall and across subgroups by MOUD type, demographics, and surgical procedure categories.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the Transformed Medicaid Statistical Information System Analytic Files for surgical procedures performed between July 1, 2016, and December 31, 2021. Patients aged 12 to 64 years with continuous Medicaid enrollment for 180 days before surgery were included. Data were analyzed from December 11, 2024, to June 29, 2025.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was preoperative MOUD use, defined as any claim for buprenorphine, methadone, or naltrexone use within 180 days before surgery. Unadjusted and adjusted annual prevalence estimates were calculated using logistic regression models with demographic and clinical covariates. Secondary outcomes included prevalence by medication type and by surgical procedure category.
RESULTS: The study cohort included 7 967 328 Medicaid beneficiaries undergoing 13 115 728 procedures during the study period (mean [SD] age, 40.7 [15.0] years; 8 551 437 [65.2%] female, 4 564 291 [34.8%] male). The overall prevalence of preoperative MOUD use increased from 1440.0 to 2278.3 per 100 000 procedures; after adjusting for demographic, insurance, and clinical factors, the prevalence increased from 185.8 to 337.1 per 100 000 procedures. Buprenorphine use accounted for most of the increase, rising from 808.8 to 1453.5 per 100 000 procedures, while smaller gains were observed for methadone use (589.6 to 756.5 per 100 000 procedures) and naltrexone use (69.9 to 129.2 per 100 000 procedures). Prevalence was highest among tricuspid or mitral valve repair procedures (11 393.8 per 100 000 procedures). Sensitivity analyses excluding states and years with lower data quality yielded similar results.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cohort study found that among Medicaid beneficiaries undergoing surgery, preoperative MOUD use increased substantially during the study period, with growth across all major medication types. These findings highlight the need for evidence-based strategies to optimize the perioperative care of patients using MOUD.

articles.title: Endoscope-assisted vs. conventional anterior cervical discectomy and fusion for single-level degenerative cervical disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscope-assisted anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (EA-ACDF) has been introduced as a modified technique for the treatment of degenerative cervical disease, but its comparative efficacy and safety relative to conventional ACDF (CA-ACDF) remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare EA-ACDF with CA-ACDF for single-level degenerative cervical disease.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, WanFang, VIP, and SinoMed were searched from inception through September 7, 2026. Comparative studies of EA-ACDF vs. CA-ACDF were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Eleven retrospective comparative studies involving 755 patients were included. Compared with CA-ACDF, EA-ACDF was associated with longer operative time (MD = 17.31 min, 95% CI 11.38-23.23), but lower intraoperative blood loss (MD = -17.31 mL, 95% CI -24.38 to -10.25), postoperative drainage volume (MD = -10.97 mL, 95% CI -16.98 to -4.96), length of hospital stay (MD = -0.67 days, 95% CI -1.16 to -0.17), and overall complication rate (RR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.25-0.78). No significant between-group differences were observed in final Japanese Orthopaedic Association score, Neck Disability Index, visual analogue scale score, cervical lordosis, or fusion rate. The certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low.
CONCLUSION: EA-ACDF may offer modest perioperative advantages at the cost of longer operative time, while short- to mid-term clinical, radiographic, and fusion outcomes appear broadly similar. Current evidence does not establish clinical superiority.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251123475, identifier CRD420251123475.

articles.title: CPB-REPORT: An automated perioperative data integration platform in cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery under cardiopulmonary bypass generates large volumes of perioperative data fragmented across multiple clinical information systems, limiting their integration for quality improvement and research. Cardiac surgery registries still rely predominantly on manual data entry, which is time-consuming, error-prone, and often incomplete.
OBJECTIVE: To report the real-world implementation of an automated perioperative data integration platform and evaluate its performance in terms of data completeness, accuracy, clinical workflow, and patient safety.
METHODS: We developed CPB-REPORT, a secure web-based platform using an Extract-Transform-Load architecture, integrating data from electronic health records, anaesthesia, and critical care systems into a unified database aligned with the national cardiac surgery registry. The platform was deployed in a high-volume cardiac surgery centre and initially combined automated extraction of registry variables and structured manual entry. A concordance study was performed to evaluate the robustness of automatically integrated data.
RESULTS: Between May 2022 and May 2026, CPB-REPORT prospectively captured all cardiac surgery procedures performed at the institution: 2,915 patients underwent 2,927 procedures, each documented across 174 fields and transmitted to the national registry. Compared with the previous fully manual process, the platform reduced data entry time by 20 min per patient. Dataset completeness improved from 68 % at platform deployment to 90 % in 2025. The concordance study showed an overall concordance of 97.8 % between automatically extracted and source-record values (95 % CI: 94.7-99.4 %), with excellent intraclass correlation coefficients for continuous variables. Real-time outcome monitoring enabled early detection of a surgical site infection cluster in 2022. No cybersecurity incident occurred.
CONCLUSION: The present work demonstrates that Extract-Transform-Load-based perioperative data integration is achievable in routine cardiac surgery practice using standard hospital infrastructure. The platform offers a transferable methodological model for integrating clinical information systems with international registries in line with European data-protection and interoperability frameworks.

articles.title: International expert consensus on radical resection combined with intestinal autotransplantation for locally advanced pancreatic cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radical resection combined with intestinal autotransplantation (RRCIA) has emerged as a potential curative option for highly selected patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC) and extensive mesenteric vascular involvement. This project aimed to develop expert consensus recommendations on indications, surgical strategies, perioperative management, and long-term care of RRCIA in patients with LAPC.
METHODS: An international multidisciplinary panel of experts in pancreatic surgery, transplant surgery, medical oncology, radiation oncology, radiology, critical care, and perioperative care was convened. A modified Delphi process was used to develop consensus recommendations. The survey comprised six domains with a total of 20 questions covering patient selection, neoadjuvant therapy, surgical strategies, perioperative management, adjuvant therapy, and follow-up. Consensus was predefined as ≥80% agreement.
RESULTS: Twenty consensus statements were developed. The quality of evidence was low for 17 statements and moderate for 3. Six recommendations were strong and 14 conditional. RRCIA was recommended only for highly selected patients at experienced high-volume centres following adequate neoadjuvant therapy and multidisciplinary evaluation. Surgical strategies should be individualized according to tumour location and vascular involvement. No definitive minimum residual bowel length was established, and preservation of well-perfused bowel and the ileocaecal valve was emphasized. Postoperative management should be tailored, including anticoagulation, nutritional support, selective implementation of enhanced recovery principles, adjuvant therapy, and structured long-term follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This consensus provides the first international framework to guide the application of RRCIA for LAPC, emphasizing its use in carefully selected patients treated at experienced centres with multidisciplinary expertise.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Transversus Abdominis Plane Block Improves Perioperative Analgesia in Transfemoral Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate, as the primary efficacy endpoint, the difference in perioperative numeric rating scale (NRS) pain scores between patients receiving a transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block and those receiving a sham block during transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI).
DESIGN: Randomized, sham-controlled, prospective clinical trial with blinding of participants, procedural operators, outcome assessors, and statistician.
SETTING: Cardiac intervention laboratory of a tertiary hospital of an institute of cardiology.
PARTICIPANTS: 18 years or older and presenting with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis and an indication for transfemoral TAVI.
INTERVENTIONS: Ultrasound-guided TAP block versus sham block.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Numeric rating scale scores were significantly higher in the sham-control group (SCG) than in the TAP block group (TAPG) at the T3 (2.17 ± 0.41 v 0.54 ± 0.40; p = 0.006) and T4 time points (4.00 ± 0.50 v 2.00 ± 0.49; p = 0.007). Total intraprocedural fentanyl consumption was reduced in the TAPG compared with the SCG (median 75 v 100 µg; p = 0.010). A greater number of patients in the SCG required rescue sedoanalgesia compared with the TAPG (73.9% v 4.2%; p < 0.001). Intraoperative unexpected patient movement scores were lower in the TAPG than the SCG (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Monitored anesthesia care combined with TAP block improves the analgesic profile and procedural stability in patients undergoing TAVI.

articles.title: Efanesoctocog alfa in mild hemophilia A.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pivotal trials of efanesoctocog alfa enrolled only people with severe hemophilia A; its use in nonsevere disease is limited to mixed-severity cohorts and a single case report of a woman. Mild disease differs: endogenous factor (F)VIII persists, and inhibitor risk is lifelong.
OBJECTIVES: To describe real-world use of efanesoctocog alfa in mild hemophilia A.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective review of consecutive individuals with mild hemophilia A, including symptomatic carriers, treated between October 2025 and June 2026. FVIII activity was measured by a one-stage assay (Actin FSL).
RESULTS: Thirteen individuals (12 men, 1 symptomatic carrier; median age, 56 years; range, 24-86) with baseline FVIII levels of 8% to 57% underwent 17 treatment episodes: 10 perioperative or procedural, 4 on-demand, and 3 prophylactic. Doses of 12 to 37 IU/kg achieved adequate hemostasis in all procedures and bleeds; 3 of 14 (2 varicose vein operations and 1 knee bleed) received a second dose. In 4 episodes, activity was 50% to 72% on days 3 to 4. Prophylaxis was administered at 26 to 40 IU/kg (median, 30) weekly or every 5 days, with trough levels of 33% to 70% (median, 61%). All injections were given on an outpatient basis. FVIII was measured in 7 of 17 episodes. No inhibitors, thrombosis, or hypersensitivity occurred.
CONCLUSION: In this first series dedicated to mild hemophilia A, efanesoctocog alfa, individualized to residual FVIII, provided adequate hemostasis at doses well below the label. A single FVIII measurement on day 3 or 4, using a product-validated assay, may replace routine monitoring. Further observations require prospective study with long-term inhibitor surveillance.
