articles.title: Temporal trends in renal replacement therapy use in adults with acute kidney injury: A severity-stratified multicentre observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Observational analyses of renal replacement therapy (RRT) use in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) are limited by the circularity between Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) AKI staging and RRT exposure.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of adults who developed AKI in 12 Queensland ICUs, Australia, from January 2015 to December 2021, with severity staged by KDIGO criteria with the RRT criterion removed. The primary outcome was the RRT utilisation proportion; secondary outcomes were the interval from ICU admission to RRT, biochemical values and cumulative fluid balance at initiation, and mortality. Trends were examined by unadjusted quasi-binomial regression and by mixed-effects logistic regression with a site random intercept, adjusted for demographics, illness severity, comorbidities, and organ support.
RESULTS: Of 89 186 ICU admissions, 31 980 with AKI were included; 3475 (10.9%) received RRT. Unadjusted RRT utilisation did not change overall (odds ratio [OR] per year 1.001; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.982 to 1.019) and decreased in Stage 3 AKI (0.954; 0.926 to 0.983). After case-mix adjustment, utilisation increased (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per year 1.041; 1.019 to 1.064; p < 0.001), including in stage 1 (1.061; 1.014 to 1.111; p = 0.011) and stage 2 (1.073; 1.031 to 1.118; p < 0.001) AKI, although stage 1 was significant in only nine of 13 sensitivity analyses. The interval to RRT shortened by 1.2 h per year (p = 0.001) and preinitiation fluid balance fell by 73 mL per year (p = 0.028). Biochemical values at initiation and mortality were stable. The trend was not consistent across sites (p < 0.001 for a site-specific slope).
CONCLUSIONS: Adjusted RRT utilisation increased at the patient level overall and in stage 2 AKI, with a less consistent increase in stage 1 AKI; however, the trend was heterogeneous across sites. This highlights the importance of case-mix adjustment and of prospective indication-level data in future observational studies.
articles.journal_full: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine

articles.title: Comparison of seven machine learning models for predicting prolonged PACU length of stay: performance evaluation and identification of key influencing factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged stays in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) significantly increase healthcare resource utilization and delay postoperative recovery. Current research on PACU prolonged stays is mostly limited to univariate analyses, lacking multidimensional, high-accuracy predictive models to support precise clinical risk stratification.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 1,996 PACU patients (May-December 2024) at a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang, China. Based on literature review and expert input, 37 candidate predictors were selected. To prevent data leakage, the dataset was randomly split into training (70%) and validation (30%) sets. All feature selection-univariate/multivariate analysis (P < 0.05), Boruta, and LASSO-was performed strictly on the training set, and the intersecting predictors were used for model building. Hyperparameters were tuned via grid search with 5-fold cross-validation on the training set. Seven machine learning algorithms including logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), LightGBM, XGBoost, and artificial neural network (ANN) were developed using R and Python, and evaluated on the independent validation set using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and Brier score. SHAP analysis was used to interpret key predictors in the best-performing model.
RESULTS: The XGBoost model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.901 (95% CI: 0.863-0.932) on the validation set and a sensitivity of 65.83% for detecting prolonged PACU stays. SHAP analysis identified surgical duration (mean SHAP value 0.19), anesthesia duration (0.08), anesthesia method (0.06), total protein (0.06), and albumin-globulin ratio (0.03) as the top five predictive factors.
CONCLUSIONS: The XGBoost model developed in this study achieved a relatively high AUC of 0.901. However, its sensitivity for detecting prolonged PACU stay was 65.83%, indicating that the model's ability to confirm prolonged PACU stay remains somewhat insufficient. Therefore, it can be used as an auxiliary screening tool in clinical rather than a definitive diagnostic tool.

articles.title: Effect of plate geometry on femoral nonunion treated with augmentative plating while retaining the intramedullary nail: a comparison of wavy and straight plates.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aseptic atrophic nonunion of the femoral shaft after intramedullary nailing is a common but difficult problem in orthopedic practice. Many surgeons turn to plate fixation with autogenous bone grafting because it can help both stabilize the bone and support healing. In this study, we looked at how wavy plates perform compared with traditional straight plates in patients with this type of nonunion.
METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed 43 patients diagnosed with aseptic atrophic nonunion of the femoral shaft who were treated with plate fixation combined with autologous iliac bone grafting between January 2017 and January 2022. Depending on the plate design selected at surgery, patients were assigned to either a straight plate group (24 cases) or a wave-shaped plate group (19 cases). The main focus was bone healing, assessed by both the time to union and the proportion of patients achieving union within 12 months. Secondary outcomes included the plate-to-cortex distance, early lateral callus formation, sub-plate cortical bone resorption, perioperative parameters, and complications. Radiographic findings and clinical outcomes were systematically compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were similar between the groups. The wave-shaped plate group had a significantly larger plate-to-cortex distance than the straight plate group (5.6 ± 1.4 mm vs. 1.8 ± 0.6 mm, P = 0.030) and a shorter mean time to union (5.3 ± 1.4 months vs. 6.9 ± 1.7 months, P = 0.010). No significant differences were observed in 12-month union rates, perioperative outcomes, or complication rates between the groups. Early lateral callus formation and sub-plate cortical resorption were also comparable.
CONCLUSION: Wave-shaped plate augmentation combined with autologous bone grafting is a feasible treatment option for aseptic atrophic femoral shaft nonunion following intramedullary nailing. Compared with conventional straight plates, wave-shaped plates created a larger plate-to-cortex distance and were associated with a shorter radiographic union time, while no significant differences were observed in the 12-month union rate, perioperative outcomes, or complication rates. Further studies incorporating functional outcomes are needed to determine whether this radiographic advantage translates into meaningful clinical benefits.
articles.journal_full: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

articles.title: Early postoperative pain trajectories in a real-world surgical cohort: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute postoperative pain remains a major challenge in perioperative medicine and is associated with delayed recovery and an increased risk of chronic postsurgical pain. Although numerous demographic, clinical, surgical, and psychosocial factors have been proposed as predictors of postoperative pain, their predictive value remains inconsistent across heterogeneous surgical populations.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 105 adult surgical patients treated at the Emergency Center of the University Clinical Center of Serbia. Pain intensity was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at admission to the postanesthesia care unit (PACU), at PACU discharge, and 24 h after surgery. Demographic, socioeconomic, clinical, surgical, anesthetic, and analgesic variables were analyzed. Exploratory analyses included univariate comparisons, logistic regression, pain reduction (ΔNRS), and correlation analyses.
RESULTS: Mean NRS pain scores decreased from 3.54 ± 1.13 at PACU admission to 1.90 ± 0.62 at 24 h after surgery (P < 0.001). Multimodal analgesia based on tramadol and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs was the most frequently administered postoperative analgesic regimen (68.6%). Clinically significant postoperative pain (NRS ≥ 3) was present in 14 of 98 patients (14.3%) with available 24-h assessments. No consistent associations were observed between 24-h pain outcomes and the demographic, socioeconomic, clinical, surgical, anesthetic, or analgesic variables examined. Given the limited number of outcome events, the exploratory regression analysis was not sufficiently powered to establish reliable independent predictors of postoperative pain.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute postoperative pain was generally mild and decreased significantly during the first postoperative day. Within this heterogeneous single-center cohort, no independent predictors of clinically significant postoperative pain could be reliably identified among the variables examined. These findings should be interpreted in the context of the limited number of outcome events, clinical heterogeneity, and the absence of several established preoperative pain-related and psychosocial predictors. Larger, adequately powered studies incorporating procedure-specific and broader biopsychosocial factors are needed to improve postoperative pain risk assessment.

articles.title: Evaluation of a structured training model for organ transplant specialist nurse trainees: a single-group pre-post study with six-month follow-up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Organ transplantation nursing demands advanced competencies in perioperative management, long-term follow-up, patient education, and interdisciplinary collaboration. However, structured training models with comprehensive outcome evaluation remain inadequately described. This study evaluated a structured training model for organ transplant specialist nurse trainees and examined factors associated with changes in self-reported nursing competence.
METHODS: In this single-group pre-post study, registered clinical nurses selected by their hospitals for advanced organ transplantation specialty training completed a 480-hour full-time program across two cohorts (2022-2023). The model comprised advanced nursing practice leadership (2 weeks/80 hours), specialist theoretical coursework (3 weeks/120 hours), clinical placement at a provincial training-base hospital (4 weeks/140 hours), and supervised practice (4 weeks/140 hours) with one-to-one mentorship and logbook-guided standardization. Self-reported nursing competence was assessed using the Chinese version of the Nurse Competence Scale (NCS) before and after training. Secondary outcomes included program completion assessment performance, teaching satisfaction (11-item questionnaire, 5-point Likert scale), and self-reported workplace activities at 6 months. Paired t tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction and exploratory Pearson correlations were used for analysis.
RESULTS: Forty-three trainees from six Chinese provinces were included in the final analysis. Mean total NCS scores increased from 72.74 ± 3.93 to 80.44 ± 2.45 (mean difference 7.70 points; 95% CI 6.87-8.53; p < 0.0001; Cohen's dz=2.86), with significant gains across all seven dimensions. The mean overall teaching satisfaction score was 4.88 ± 0.11, and 470 of 473 item-level responses (99.37%) were rated as satisfied. At 6-month follow-up, 100% reported organizing complex case discussions, 93.0% reported conducting teaching rounds and quality improvement activities, and 60.5% reported providing nursing consultations. Changes in NCS scores were inversely correlated with age (r=-0.427, p = 0.004) and clinical experience (r=-0.493, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Completion of this structured, theory-practice integrated training model was associated with higher multidimensional self-reported nursing competence and reported participation in workplace activities among organ transplant specialist nurse trainees. Because this was a single-group pre-post study, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary evidence to inform specialist nurse education, and controlled multicenter studies with objective outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Fresh frozen plasma administration during cardiopulmonary bypass was not associated with postoperative transfusion requirements after elective total aortic arch replacement: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during total aortic arch replacement (TAR) is associated with coagulopathy. We investigated whether fresh frozen plasma (FFP) administration during CPB was associated with postoperative transfusion requirements and coagulation profiles after TAR.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective TAR. Patients were categorized according to whether FFP was administered during CPB. The primary outcome was postoperative FFP transfusion from CPB separation to 12 h after intensive care unit admission. Secondary outcomes included perioperative plasma-derived product use, postoperative bleeding, re-exploration for bleeding, and serial coagulation parameters. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: Data from 156 patients were analyzed, including 111 patients in the Pre-FFP group and 45 in the Control group. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although deep hypothermic circulatory arrest duration and CPB fluid management differed between the groups. The adjusted mean difference in total post-CPB FFP transfusion units between the Pre-FFP and Control groups was - 1.54 units (95% confidence interval, - 7.51 to 4.43). No significant differences were observed in perioperative plasma-derived product use or bleeding outcomes. Although fibrinogen concentrations were higher and activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio were shorter at the end of CPB in the Pre-FFP group, these differences largely resolved after CPB.
CONCLUSION: FFP administration during CPB was associated with transient improvement in coagulation parameters but was not associated with postoperative transfusion requirements or bleeding outcomes in adult patients undergoing elective TAR. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Pain medicine in Ukraine under wartime conditions: structures, treatment availability and resource needs in the TRACE-Pain Ukraine survey.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Ukraine faced a substantial burden of chronic pain even before the full-scale invasion. Since February 2022, war-related injury, amputation, displacement and growing rehabilitation needs have increased the complexity of pain care. Meeting these needs requires coordinated pain care supported by appropriate structures and specialist expertise. However, little is known about how pain-medicine services are organized across the country, which treatments are available, and which constraints clinicians consider most urgent. The Treatment Resources, Access, Capacity, and Education for Pain Medicine in Ukraine (TRACE-Pain Ukraine) survey assessed reported service capacity and resource needs among Ukrainian health-care professionals.
METHODS: TRACE-Pain Ukraine was a non-interventional, descriptive cross-sectional online survey of health-care professionals involved in pain management. Data were collected from 27 June 2025 to 5 June 2026.
RESULTS: Of 95 submitted questionnaires, 93 were retained: 72 were completed and 21 were substantive partial responses. Respondents represented 22 of 24 oblasts (administrative regions) plus Kyiv City. Median age was 39 years [IQR 30-49], 64.5 % were female, and 48.4 % worked in physical and rehabilitation medicine or related care. Written protocols (85.1 %), pain-scale documentation (79.5 %), weekly case conferences (76.7 %), regular team meetings (70.3 %) and telemedicine (58.1 %) were frequently reported. Conversely, 56.6 % reported no formal pain-medicine structure; dedicated pain beds or a ward were reported by 12.2 %, standardized training by 32.5 % and mentoring by 20.5 %. Treatment for several complex pain conditions was more often reported as available but insufficient rather than unavailable. Devices or medications were lacking according to 52/72 respondents (72.2 %). Personnel, funding, equipment, and medications were the leading need priorities.
CONCLUSIONS: This first multi-regional survey identified a mixed pattern of established clinical practices and uneven structural capacity within a pain-medicine system in seeming transition. Documentation, interdisciplinary exchange and telemedicine were well established, as was basic pharmacological treatment. Formal structures, specialist training, multimodal capacity and material resources were not. These findings support phased service development grounded in existing strengths, with specialized care coordinated through regional referral pathways.

articles.title: Robotic-assisted prostate and kidney surgery: evolution, outcomes, and future directions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Robotic prostate and kidney surgery has moved beyond proving technical feasibility. This review examines how recent evidence is shifting the field from platform-driven surgery toward patient-, anatomy-, and information-driven selection.
RECENT FINDINGS: In radical prostatectomy, randomized trials show that intraoperative frozen-section assessment and augmented-reality guidance can modify nerve-sparing decisions and improve functional or oncological endpoints. In partial nephrectomy, three-dimensional virtual models have progressed from anatomical planning to perfusion-aware selective clamping, complication prediction, and functional forecasting, while randomized trials are testing whether these tools improve outcomes. Indications for robotic surgery are expanding selectively to salvage prostatectomy, cT2 renal tumors, redo nephron-sparing surgery, inferior vena cava thrombectomy, and kidney-sparing upper-tract surgery. Single-port systems are enabling renewed extraperitoneal, transvesical, and retroperitoneal access, with increasing attention to anesthesia, opioid use, length of stay, and same-day discharge. Randomized evidence has also moved telesurgery beyond feasibility.
SUMMARY: The next phase of robotic surgery will be defined less by platform adoption than by choosing the right platform, access, information, and perioperative pathway for the right patient.

articles.title: Prefrontal hemodynamic fluctuations and functional connectivity during propofol and sevoflurane anesthesia: A functional near-infrared spectroscopy study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measures cortical hemodynamics, yet its ability to characterize anesthesia-related functional changes remains unclear.
METHODS: This exploratory secondary analysis used prospectively collected data from 120 female patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under propofol or sevoflurane anesthesia (60 per group). Twenty-channel prefrontal fNIRS recordings covered wakefulness, induction, and maintenance. Deoxygenated hemoglobin-derived amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), functional connectivity (FC), network topology, and within- and cross-state FC similarity were assessed. Support vector machine, logistic regression, and random forest classifiers assessed discrimination between states.
RESULTS: During induction, ALFF increased by 89.8% to 202.2% with propofol and 75.2% to 242.0% with sevoflurane across five prefrontal regions (all P < 0.001). During maintenance, mean ALFF was below awake levels, with significant reductions of 20.0% to 40.1% in three regions under sevoflurane (all P ≤ 0.019). Induction-related FC changes were limited and regionally heterogeneous. Regional FC, modularity, and global efficiency showed no significant maintenance-versus-awake differences in either group. Within-state between-subject FC similarity was significantly higher during maintenance than during wakefulness only with sevoflurane (mean difference [MD], 0.110; 95% CI, 0.054 to 0.169; P < 0.001). Cross-state between-subject FC similarity was higher for awake-maintenance than awake-induction comparisons with propofol (MD, 0.072; 95% CI, 0.055 to 0.090) and sevoflurane (MD, 0.144; 95% CI, 0.126 to 0.161; both P < 0.001). Support vector machine classification of induction versus wakefulness yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.83 (95% CI, 0.75 to 0.90) for propofol and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.91) for sevoflurane; maintenance-versus-awake AUCs were 0.67 (95% CI, 0.58 to 0.75) and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.68 to 0.85).
CONCLUSIONS: Prefrontal fNIRS detected widespread induction-related hemodynamic changes, but the present connectivity measures provided limited discrimination between maintenance of anesthesia and wakefulness.

articles.title: More than a fluid: reframing the role of albumin in sepsis.
Hypotension Prediction Index-guided care in the HYT trial: hemodynamics through slicer and dicer.
Weight- and age-dependent bias in remimazolam pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models during bispectral index-guided anesthesia: a retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Schüttler pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PKPD) model for remimazolam was derived from healthy male volunteers (20-38 years; 64-99 kg). This study examined how body weight and age modify the relationship between effect-site concentration (Ce) and bispectral index (BIS) in Korean surgical patients.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed Schüttler-predicted remimazolam Ce and observed BIS from 52 adult patients under remimazolam-remifentanil total intravenous anesthesia. A linear mixed-effects model examined demographic modifiers of the Ce-BIS relationship, including Ce × weight and Ce × age interaction terms. Patients were stratified by body weight (< 60 vs. ≥ 60 kg) and age (< 40 vs. ≥ 40 years), reflecting the Schüttler development cohort boundaries. Prediction accuracy was assessed using median performance error (MDPE), and compared with the Masui, Zhou, and Eleveld models.
RESULTS: Body weight significantly modified the Ce-BIS relationship (Ce × weight interaction, P = 0.029), with lower body weight and older age each independently associated with lower observed BIS than model-predicted values. In patients weighing < 60 kg and aged ≥ 40 years, the Schüttler model showed greater negative bias (MDPE: -20.4%) than the Masui and Zhou models (MDPE: -17.5% and -18.9%, respectively), whereas the Eleveld model exhibited a qualitatively distinct, age-driven bidirectional bias pattern.
CONCLUSIONS: Body weight and age significantly modify the Ce-BIS relationship in remimazolam-based anesthesia, with negative bias observed across all four PKPD models in low-body-weight older patients. These findings warrant prospective validation in larger and more diverse cohorts and remimazolam PKPD model refinement that adequately incorporates body size and age.

articles.title: International Expert Consensus Statement on Contemporary Prevention and Management of Postoperative Delirium in Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium is among the most frequent neurocognitive complications of cardiac surgery, with reported incidence ranging from 14% to more than 50% depending on patient population and operative complexity. It is independently associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, extended intensive care unit and hospital stay, long-term cognitive decline, and increased mortality. Despite this burden, prevention and management strategies remain inconsistent across institutions worldwide.
METHODS: An international multidisciplinary expert panel applied a structured PICOT (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Timing) framework to predefined clinical questions spanning four perioperative phases: preoperative, intraoperative, postoperative and intensive care, and recovery after intensive care. Designated expert groups synthesized available evidence through structured literature reviews, and consensus recommendations were developed using a modified Delphi methodology.
RESULTS: The panel developed 14 consensus statements. Preoperatively, routine screening with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and Clinical Frailty Scale, and multicomponent optimization are recommended. Opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia is recommended, whereas perioperative dexmedetomidine in place of benzodiazepines, cerebral oximetry, processed electroencephalography-guided anesthesia depth monitoring, and optimized oxygen delivery may be considered. In intensive care, validated delirium screening paired with sedation assessment, daily awakening and breathing trials, structured multicomponent care bundles, correction of reversible precipitants, and circadian-supportive environments are central. After transfer from intensive care, continued ward screening and structured post-discharge cognitive follow-up are recommended.
CONCLUSIONS: These statements provide a framework for preventing and managing postoperative delirium after cardiac surgery and advocate a coordinated multimodal approach. Standardizing screening, prevention bundles, and long-term follow-up within routine clinical pathways is recommended as a core institutional priority.

articles.title: State of the Art Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract: Off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB) has evolved into a mature and reproducible strategy for myocardial revascularization. Although conventional on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (ONCAB) became the standard approach with the advent of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), advances in cardiac stabilization, positioning, intracoronary shunting, and anesthetic management have enabled complete multivessel revascularization on the beating heart without CPB. Clinical studies have shown that OPCAB achieves outcomes comparable to ONCAB in appropriately selected patients while reducing perioperative complications, particularly in high-risk populations. Advances in surgical expertise, institutional infrastructure, and techniques including minimally invasive and hybrid approaches continue to expand the role of OPCAB. This review highlights the evolution, evidence, indications, and future perspectives of OPCAB as an important complementary strategy in modern cardiac surgery.

articles.title: Pericapsular nerve group versus quadratus lumborum block for hip surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block and the quadratus lumborum block (QLB) are both used to provide analgesia after hip surgery, but their comparative efficacy remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing PENG and QLB.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched through March 2025 for RCTs comparing PENG and QLB in adults undergoing hip surgery. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird estimator with Knapp-Hartung adjustment) pooled standardized mean differences (SMD) for pain, mean differences in intravenous morphine milligram equivalents (MME) for opioid consumption, and risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes. Heterogeneity was quantified with I². Prespecified subgroup analyses (surgical population and QLB approach) and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Seven RCTs (554 patients; 283 PENG, 271 QLB) were included. PENG showed a non-significant trend toward lower early (~ 2 h) resting pain (SMD - 0.25; 95% CI - 0.60 to 0.09; I²=55%). No significant differences were found for resting pain at 24 h (SMD - 0.40; -1.44 to 0.64; I²=92%), pain on movement at 24 h (SMD 0.08; -0.27 to 0.43; I²=0%), or cumulative opioid consumption (mean difference - 0.50 intravenous morphine milligram equivalents; 95% CI - 5.92 to 4.93; I²=84%).
CONCLUSIONS: No clear difference between PENG and QLB was demonstrated for pain, opioid consumption, or safety after hip surgery. The available evidence is insufficient to establish superiority between the techniques, and the early-pain and motor-sparing signals favoring PENG should be regarded as uncertain. Larger standardized randomized trials are required.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level I, systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes of 1470-nm Radial Diode Laser Ablation for Pilonidal Sinus Disease: A Real-World Clinical Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pilonidal sinus disease, known as a disease of young people, is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by long-lasting wound problems and frequent recurrence after traditional surgical methods. To accelerate postoperative wound healing and thus reduce morbidity, minimally invasive laser-based techniques have been developed to selectively ablate and destroy the sinus passages while preserving surrounding tissue.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of our patients with pilonidal sinus disease who underwent intraluminal laser ablation. All procedures were performed using a Biolitec® 1470-nm diode laser system equipped with a radial emitter fiber that allows for circumferential and homogeneous laser energy delivery to the sinus wall. To minimize interoperator variability, all surgeons followed an identical operative protocol regarding tract curettage, laser energy settings, fiber withdrawal speed, and postoperative care. Following mechanical debridement and irrigation of the sinus tracts, laser energy was delivered by inserting the radial fiber into the sinus and using a controlled withdrawal technique to ablate the epithelial lining and adhere the sinus tract. Procedures were performed under sedation or regional anesthesia. Demographic data, disease status (primary or recurrent), surgery time, postoperative complications, recovery time, and recurrence were recorded. Patients were followed up in the outpatient clinic in the early postoperative period, and subsequent follow-ups were conducted via telephone. Recurrence was defined as the reappearance of symptoms during follow-up or the formation of a new sinus.
RESULTS: Seventy-four patients were included in the study. The mean age was 24.8 years, and 81% of the patients were male. A total of 83.8% of the patients had primary pilonidal sinus disease, while 16.2% had recurrent disease. The mean procedure time was 28 minutes. Complete healing was achieved in 97.2% of patients after a single Biolitec laser session. Minor postoperative complications, mostly mild infection or serous discharge, occurred in 2.7% of patients. No major complications were observed. The mean time to complete wound healing was 18 days. During a mean follow-up period of 40 months, recurrence was observed in only 2 patient; this rate is lower than that reported in other laser-based series and conventional surgery.
CONCLUSION: Intraluminal laser ablation is a safe and effective minimally invasive technique for treating both primary and recurrent pilonidal sinus disease, offering high healing rates, rapid recovery, and a low risk of recurrence. This laser method provides an alternative to routine traditional excisional surgery.

articles.title: Discordant evidence on corticosteroids in sepsis: a meta-research study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite an extensive evidence base of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews (SRs), current sepsis guidelines provide only weak recommendations for corticosteroid therapy, while available SRs report conflicting mortality conclusions. We aimed to characterize the evidence landscape of SRs evaluating corticosteroids for sepsis, including their clinical scope, underlying RCT evidence bases, mortality conclusions, and to explore potential sources of discordance.
METHODS: Meta-research study of SRs on corticosteroids in sepsis published between 2015 and 2025. Study-pool overlap was assessed using a SR×RCT inclusion matrix, Jaccard similarity (J), and hierarchical clustering. SRs and RCTs were classified according to standardized Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome (PICO) profiles. We explored discordance in short-term mortality conclusions among clinically comparable SRs and potential associations with study-pool composition, target populations, and methodological characteristics.
RESULTS: Forty-two SRs including 121 unique RCTs were identified. More than half of pairwise SR comparisons shared no RCTs, and only three pairs showed high overlap (J > 0.8). SRs addressing similar intervention and target population profiles frequently relied on different study pools. Among 38 SRs with short-term mortality meta-analyses, 15 (39%) reported benefit and 23 (61%) no evidence of effect. Discordance occurred exclusively among SRs evaluating broad, non-specific corticosteroid strategies; conclusions were consistent for hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone (benefit) and hydrocortisone, ascorbic acid, and thiamine (no evidence of effect). SRs including adult sepsis ± shock populations more frequently reported benefit than those restricted to septic shock (62% vs 22%), although this comparison was based on only 22 SRs evaluating broad, non-specific corticosteroid strategies and estimates were imprecise. No single methodological or clinical factor consistently explained discordance.
CONCLUSIONS: SRs addressing apparently similar clinical questions frequently synthesized different underlying evidence bases and reported discordant conclusions. When selecting SRs to inform clinical decisions and recommendations for sepsis management, clinicians and guideline developers should consider not only methodological quality and reported PICO, but also whether the included RCTs adequately represent the intended clinical question.

articles.title: Redefining blood pressure targets in refractory septic shock.
articles.abstract: Refractory septic shock was recently delineated by a set of clinical statements reflecting poor tissue perfusion despite adequate intravascular fluid volume and high doses of vasopressors. The concept of arterial pressure, which plays a pivotal role in the Sepsis-3 definition, was not incorporated by the panelists. The intensity of vasopressor treatment was found to be predominantly associated with mean arterial pressure. Indeed, the restoration of tissue perfusion is arguably the primary objective of resuscitation efforts. However, the loss of hemodynamic coherence-that is, the uncoupling between macrohemodynamics and microcirculation-suggests that, beyond a certain level of around 60-65 mmHg, tissue perfusion, as reflected by lactate and capillary refill time, is independent of arterial pressure in most patients. In this study, we propose a hypothesis derived from a physiological perspective, positing that the cost of increasing mean arterial pressure may increase disproportionately with rising norepinephrine requirements. In patients with refractory septic shock, the optimal level of arterial pressure should be investigated using time-limited challenge and adequate markers, such as capillary refill time and lactate. The approach to this evaluation should not be predicated on the analysis of isolated values; rather, it should be informed by a longitudinal and repeated examination of multiple markers that reflect global, regional, and local perfusion. Further research is necessary to ascertain the most effective strategy.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence tools for generating multimodal intensive care unit journey and discharge summaries: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map and synthesise existing evidence on computational summarisation technologies, including machine learning-based and natural language processing-based approaches, designed to generate multimodal (textual, visual, and audio) patient summaries of adult intensive care unit (ICU) stays.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance. Studies involving adults in any ICU setting and using artificial intelligence-enabled approaches to generate patient summaries were eligible. Searches were conducted across five major databases and grey literature sources. Two reviewers independently screened records. Data were extracted using a structured charting tool and independently verified by a second reviewer. Findings were synthesised using descriptive statistics and narrative synthesis.
RESULTS: Eleven studies met inclusion criteria. Eight generated textual summaries, three produced visual outputs, and one developed an audio interface. Ten tools were clinician-facing; only one study generated summaries for families. Approaches included large language models, rule-based natural language generation, information extraction, trajectory modelling, and speech-based systems. No study implemented a fully multimodal summarisation system. All evaluations were conducted using retrospective data, simulations, or prototypes, with no prospective testing in live clinical workflows. Five themes emerged: predominance of text-based summarisation, early feasibility of large language models with reliability limitations, predominance of clinician-facing applications, heterogeneous evaluation practices, and limited evidence of clinical implementation.
CONCLUSION: Current ICU summarisation research demonstrates technical proof-of-concept feasibility but limited clinical readiness. Progress will require rigorous evaluation, stabilisation safeguards, and multimodal, patient- and family-centred designs capable of operating within regulatory and safety-critical clinical environments.

articles.title: Hypomagnesemia during Kidney Replacement Therapy with Regional Citrate Anticoagulation: a prospective study on the differences between Continuous and Prolonged Intermittent modalities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypomagnesemia is common in critically ill patients on kidney replacement therapy (KRT) and may adversely affect outcomes. We evaluated hypomagnesemia incidence during continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH), continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration (CVVHDF), and sustained low-efficiency dialysis-filtration (SLED-f) with regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) and explored the relationship between serum magnesium and mortality.
METHODS: We prospectively studied critically ill patients requiring KRT-RCA at our centre, all of whom received magnesium-containing dialysis/replacement solutions. Linear mixed-effects models and generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to examine difference in serum magnesium and hypomagnesemia, and time-varying Cox regression to assess association with mortality.
RESULTS: Patients received CVVH (n = 21), CVVHDF (n = 21), or SLED-f (n = 36). Hypomagnesemia (s-Mg; <1.7 mg/dL) occurred in 82%, requiring supplementation in 73%. Serum magnesium concentrations were lower during continuous modalities in unadjusted analyses, but differences were largely attenuated after adjustment for baseline characteristics; only one time point showed statistical significance (CVVH, session-day 4; P = 0.047); in GEE analyses, observed differences in hypomagnesemia between groups was no longer significant after adjustment for baseline characteristics. Exploratory analyses identified a U-shaped association between serum magnesium and mortality (P = 0.032), but this was model-dependent, absent in unadjusted analysis, and based on sparse data at distribution extremes.
CONCLUSIONS: Hypomagnesemia is a common complication during KRT with RCA despite magnesium-containing solutions and supplementation. Apparent modality differences largely attenuated after adjustment for baseline characteristics. The U-shaped magnesium-mortality association requires validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Applied pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles: A case-based approach.
articles.abstract: Knowledge of pharmacology is essential when caring for critically ill patients. Critical illness introduces several pharmacokinetic changes that affect the disposition of drugs in the body. Additionally, the presence of organ failures, common in this population, as well as the addition of extracorporeal devices can affect drug concentrations and lead to therapeutic failure or drug accumulation and toxicity. All phases of pharmacokinetics (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination) can be affected. These derangements, that are dynamic throughout the course of critical illness, lead to profound pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic alterations, rendering models derived from healthy populations unreliable and making titration to objective pharmacodynamic targets and frequent reassessment, essential for achieving therapeutic success while minimizing toxicity and adverse effects. Recent innovations in technology, including artificial intelligence, present promising opportunities to guide drug dosing and predict adverse reactions based on patient characteristics. This review uses a patient case to demonstrate the importance of understanding these principles of pharmacology to optimize patient outcomes while minimizing the risk of harm from medications.

articles.title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Coma in Latin American Critical Care Units: The COMA LATAM Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the point prevalence of coma across Latin American critical care units, characterize its etiology, and explore short-term outcomes.
DESIGN: Multinational, cross-sectional point prevalence study with exploratory 14-day follow-up assessment.
SETTING: Three hundred ninety-two hospitals across 19 Latin American countries, including ICUs, intermediate care units, neurocritical care units, cardiovascular ICUs, and trauma ICUs.
PATIENTS: Adult patients (≥ 18 yr) meeting the Coma Epidemiology, Evaluation, and Therapy care survey (COME-TOGETHER) criteria on May 28, 2024. Patients under deep sedation or pharmacological coma induction were excluded unless the coma state preceded pharmacological intervention.
INTERVENTIONS: None (observational study).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 8305 critically ill patients, 1145 met coma criteria (point prevalence 13.8%), with country-specific rates ranging from 5.1% to 36.8%. Individual patient data were available for 729 patients (63.7%). Traumatic brain injury was the leading individual cause (24.8%), followed by hypoxic-anoxic brain injury (14.6%) and intracerebral hemorrhage (13.5%). When categorized by pathophysiology, vascular causes predominated (48.6%), followed by traumatic brain injury (24.8%) and other causes (26.6%). Age-stratified analysis revealed trauma predominantly affecting younger patients, while cerebrovascular causes predominated in older groups. Among patients with 14-day follow-up data (29% of cohort), mortality was 29.2%, with 67.7% of survivors recovering from coma. Only the Charlson Comorbidity Index was independently associated with implementation of life-sustaining therapy limitations (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.15-1.30; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Coma affects nearly one in seven ICU beds across Latin America, with substantial country variation and distinct age-dependent etiology patterns. The significant burden highlights the need for targeted prevention strategies and specialized neurocritical care resources throughout the region.

articles.title: Charcot-Leyden crystals drive a localized inflammatory niche around mucus plugs in Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Mucus plugging causes airflow obstruction, morbidity, and mortality in chronic respiratory diseases. Charcot-Leyden crystals (CLCs), formed from eosinophil-derived Galectin-10, are frequently observed in pathologic mucus, but their role in disease is unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To define the prevalence, inflammatory context, and functional role of CLCs in mucus plugs, using acute allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) as a model of eosinophilic muco-obstructive disease.
METHODS: Airway samples from 19 patients with acute ABPA and 61 disease controls were analyzed for CLCs and Galectin-10. Paired samples from plugged and unplugged bronchial mucosal biopsies defined the spatial relationship between CLCs and inflammation. A novel mouse model demonstrated the contribution of CLCs to airway obstruction and inflammation and enabled evaluation of CLC-directed imaging and therapy.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Airway CLCs were a sensitive and specific marker of acute ABPA. CLC-containing mucus plugs were surrounded by a localized type 2 inflammatory niche, alongside eosinophils, neutrophils and extracellular traps, whereas inflammation was minimal in unplugged airways from the same patients, or plugs lacking CLCs. In mice, CLC-containing plugs induced persistent airway obstruction and local inflammation, both reduced by a crystal-dissolving anti-Galectin-10 antibody. Galectin-10 concentrations provided a quantitative biomarker of acute ABPA, while a CLC-targeted positron emission tomography tracer enabled noninvasive visualization of crystal-rich plugs.
CONCLUSIONS: CLC-containing mucus plugs form focal inflammatory niches in acute ABPA, and experimental CLC deposition is sufficient to promote persistent airway obstruction and inflammation. These findings identify CLCs as a biomarker, imaging target, and tractable therapeutic target in eosinophilic muco-obstructive airway disease.
