Thus, we planned this study to evaluate the neurological outcome of patients undergoing craniotomy for excision of meningiomas using intraoperative fiberoptic jugular venous oximetry versus the standard care. We hypothesized that intraoperative jugular venous oximetry monitoring in these patients will improve the patient outcome.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Patients (American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I and II) aged 18 to 60 years undergoing elective craniotomy for excision of intracranial meningioma were randomized to receive either jugular venous oxygenation-based intraoperative management or standard anesthesia management. Patient demographics, intraoperative vitals, and length of hospital stay were noted. Patients' neurological status was assessed telephonically at 1 month postoperatively using extended Glasgow outcome scale (GOSE).
RESULTS: A total of 40 patients were enrolled in this study. Demographics and intraoperative variables were comparable between two groups. There were five episodes of jugular venous oxygen desaturation in three (7.5%) of the study patients. None of the patients had jugular pressure more than 6 mm Hg at any time point of surgery, irrespective of position of the patient. The hemodynamic variables were comparable between the two groups. The mean lactate oxygen index was 0.002 in Group B. Both groups had no significant difference with respect to GOSE at 1 month. We did not observe any complications with respect to procedure and technique of placement of jugular venous catheter.
CONCLUSIONS: Results of this preliminary study suggest that the intraoperative management guided by continuous jugular venous oximetry is not superior to standard management for improving neurological outcome in patients undergoing excision of intracranial meningiomas. Further research is necessary to confirm these findings and explore its complete potential.

articles.title: Opioid-free anesthesia versus opioid-based anesthesia on postoperative delirium incidence: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The use of opioids as anesthetic agents is associated with multiple adverse effects, such as delirium. Patients with postoperative delirium (POD) have a higher risk of mortality or major complications. Recently, a multimodal anesthetic technique known as opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) has been developed to minimize or eliminate the use of opioids during anesthesia, which is hypothesized to reduce the incidence of POD. This systematic review aims to compare OFA and opioid-based anesthesia (OBA) to the incidence of POD.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Literature searches were conducted electronically without time restrictions across six databases: PubMed, Cochrane Central Register for Controlled Trials, ProQuest, ScienceDirect, Springer Nature, and PMC Europe. Additional studies were obtained through electronic searches on Google. The inclusion criteria were human studies involving participants aged ≥18 years, interventions of OFA and OBA, and POD as an outcome. Study selection was performed using Rayyan QCRI, and risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) and Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I).
RESULTS: Six studies met the inclusion criteria; three randomized controlled trials (RCTs), two cohort studies, and one case-control study. Five studies demonstrated no significant difference in the incidence of POD between the OFA and OBA groups; one study reported no occurrence of POD in either group. Several factors influencing POD included advanced age, type and duration of surgery, and the pharmacological effects of anesthetic agents such as dexmedetomidine, lidocaine, midazolam, and regional analgesic agents.
CONCLUSION: OFA has not been shown to clearly reduce the incidence of POD. The occurrence of POD is multifactorial.

articles.title: Efficacy of dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant to propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia in children undergoing magnetic resonance imaging: A prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Pediatric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) requires deep sedation to ensure immobility and optimal image quality. Propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia is effective but may cause airway depression and hemodynamic instability at higher doses. Dexmedetomidine has minimal respiratory effects but may prolong sedation. This study evaluated whether a low-dose dexmedetomidine bolus combined with propofol shortens recovery time (primary outcome); improves hemodynamic stability; reduces airway events, induction time, and total propofol dose; and minimizes scan interruptions (secondary outcomes).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this prospective, randomized controlled trial, children undergoing MRI were assigned to two groups. Group D+P received 0.5 µg/kg of dexmedetomidine over 2-3 minutes plus a 1 mg/kg bolus of propofol followed by infusion; Group P received propofol alone as bolus and infusion. Propofol infusion rate was adjusted to achieve a Ramsay Sedation Scale score of 5-6. Recovery time was analyzed using t test; scan interruptions were compared using Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests.
RESULTS: Group D+P had a shorter recovery time (19.4 ± 35 vs. 31.4 ± 36.1 min; P = 0.042) and faster induction (128.9 vs. 224.6 sec; P < 0.001). The propofol infusion rate was lower in Group D + P than in Group P (76.3 ± 65.6 vs 123 ± 45.5 µg/kg/min; P < 0.001). Additional boluses were more frequent in Group P (P = 0.003). Bradycardia occurred in significantly more children in Group D + P than in Group P (P = 0.008).
CONCLUSIONS: Low-dose dexmedetomidine as an adjunct to propofol for pediatric MRI sedation reduces recovery time, propofol requirement, and airway-related complications, while enabling faster induction and fewer scan interruptions with increased risk of bradycardia.

articles.title: Utility of programmed intermittent bolus infusion modality in peripheral nerve catheters for postoperative pain management - A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Continuous peripheral nerve block catheters deliver prolonged anesthesia or analgesia during the perioperative period and have evolved into established practices. Recent advancements in regional anesthesia aim to improve patient outcomes by reducing morbidity. Despite the use of adjuvants, single injection pain management typically lasts only 16 to 24 hours. Alternatively, continuous infusion (CI) pumps may increase local anesthetic doses, raising the risk of toxicity and opioid use. The newly evaluated programmed intermittent bolus (PIB) pumps show promise for peripheral nerve blocks, yet a Cochrane Library search indicates a gap in research, with only handful of registered trials on this topic. This highlights the need for further investigation and subgroup analyses to strengthen evidence for this modality in pain management.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: In accordance with the PROSPERO registry protocol for this review, we conducted a literature search to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the PIB pumps in peripheral nerves blocks for postoperative pain management. Our primary outcomes included pain scores, consumption of local anesthetics, morphine, and rescue analgesics, as well as any encountered side effects.
RESULTS: There were 25 published randomized controlled trials, meeting the inclusion criteria, comprising 1572 patients, directly comparing PIB and CI, and explaining all the comparatives with rare complications. Despite the ever growing quest to find the ideal postoperative pain management method, there is limited literature and it is insufficient to guide clinical practice. Our study underscores the utility of PIB.
CONCLUSION: PIB proves a better analgesic mode than CI.

articles.title: Confronting-View One-Window and Two-Port Robot-Assisted Thoracic Surgery for Anatomical Lung Resection: Surgical Technique and Initial Perioperative Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the surgical technique and evaluate the perioperative outcomes of confronting-view 1-window and 2-port robot-assisted thoracic surgery (CV-1W2P RATS) compared with conventional look-up-view multiport RATS (LU-MP RATS).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 109 patients who underwent CV-1W2P RATS and compared them with 100 patients who underwent LU-MP RATS. Perioperative outcomes and postoperative pain management were evaluated.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally similar between the groups. All 101 CV-1W2P RATS procedures without conversion to thoracotomy were completed using 3 incisions without CO2 insufflation. Operative time was similar, whereas console time was significantly shorter in the CV-1W2P RATS group. Conversion to thoracotomy occurred in 8 patients (7.3%) in the CV-1W2P RATS group but in none of the LU-MP RATS group. No significant differences were observed in blood loss, postoperative complications, chest tube duration, or postoperative hospital stay. Despite less frequent use of epidural analgesia, postoperative pain scores were similar, and significantly fewer patients in the CV-1W2P RATS group required additional analgesics at the first postoperative outpatient visit.
CONCLUSION: CV-1W2P RATS is a feasible reduced-port approach; however, conversion to thoracotomy occurred more frequently than with conventional LU-MP RATS during our initial experience. This difference should be considered when introducing the approach, particularly in technically demanding cases. Its confronting-view configuration, reduced chest wall invasiveness, improved bedside assistance, and avoidance of CO2 insufflation may provide additional clinical and educational advantages.
articles.journal_full: Annals of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery : official journal of the Association of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons of Asia

articles.title: Heart transplantation in complex clinical and social contexts: expanding indications, ethical boundaries, and clinical decision-making.
articles.abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the definitive therapy for selected patients with stage D heart failure; however, current practice increasingly extends beyond traditional eligibility criteria. Progress in mechanical circulatory support, donor management, immunosuppressive therapies, and perioperative care has facilitated transplantation in patients with complex clinical profiles, including advanced age, obesity, chronic infections, prior malignancies, substance use disorders, and socioeconomic vulnerabilities. This review traces the evolution from strict contraindications to personalized risk assessment supported by multidisciplinary transplant teams and ethical oversight. The discussion encompasses clinical decision-making between HTx and left ventricular assist devices, incorporating INTERMACS profiles, end-organ function, frailty, psychosocial evaluation, donor availability, and waiting times. Emerging strategies to broaden the donor pool, such as donation after circulatory death, normothermic regional perfusion, and ex-vivo heart perfusion, are examined with respect to safety and clinical outcomes. Particular attention is paid to combined heart-kidney transplantation, management of recipients with chronic viral infections, and collaboration with cardio-oncology for patients with histories of cancer. Finally, the review addresses ethical considerations related to equity, organ allocation, and shared decision-making, as well as future directions including precision transplant medicine, artificial intelligence-based risk modeling, and evolving ethical frameworks aimed at enhancing outcomes amid persistent organ scarcity.

articles.title: Identification of Risk Factors for Nonadherence in Preoperative Patients Following Pharmacist Intervention: A Retrospective Study in Japan.
articles.abstract: Nonadherence to preoperative medication instructions can lead to surgical delays or cancellations. Some patients fail to follow medication instructions properly. This study aimed to identify risk factors for preoperative medication-related nonadherence in a Japanese cohort and to develop a practical risk scoring system. We conducted this single-center retrospective cohort study at St. Luke's International Hospital among adult patients who were scheduled for anesthesiologist-managed surgery and received preoperative medication instructions from pharmacists between June 2021 and May 2023. Nonadherence was defined as failure to follow instructions regarding the temporary discontinuation or continuation. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed using complete case data to identify independent risk factors for nonadherence. Candidate variables included age, sex, body mass index (BMI), number of regular medications, interval from pharmacist counseling to surgery, number of remaining teeth, American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status, and presence of a cohabiting partner. A risk scoring system was developed based on the regression coefficients. Of 8181 eligible patients, 6162 complete cases were analyzed. Medication-related nonadherence was observed in 350 patients. Multivariable analysis identified four independent risk factors for nonadherence: age ≥75 years (p < 0.001), an interval from pharmacist counseling to surgery of ≥30 d (p = 0.002), use of ≥5 regular medications (p = 0.013), and BMI >25 kg/m2 (p = 0.027). No significant interactions were observed between age group and process-related factors. The derived risk score showed modest discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.630. These factors may help identify patients who require reinforced preoperative medication counseling, thereby potentially supporting more targeted preoperative medication management.

articles.title: Mortality prediction at the tracheostomy decision point after liver transplantation: development and internal validation of a bedside risk score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver-transplant (LT) recipients requiring prolonged ventilation and considered for percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy (PDT) have high short-term mortality, but LT-specific tools to support prognosis-aligned communication at this decision point are lacking. We developed and internally validated a simple PDT-day model and an integer Tracheostomy Decision-Point Risk Score (TRS) to estimate 90-day mortality from the PDT decision point in LT recipients undergoing PDT.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included 83 adult LT recipients undergoing PDT between December 2010 and June 2024. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 90 days from the PDT decision point, operationalized as the day of PDT. The model estimates risk after the PDT decision point and not the causal effect of PDT. Logistic regression used routinely available PDT-day variables; internal validation used bootstrap shrinkage. Discrimination and calibration were assessed by AUC, Brier score, calibration-in-the-large, and calibration slope. Coefficients were converted to an integer TRS.
RESULTS: 90-day mortality was 62.7% (52/83). Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD; +5 points), age (+ 10 years), and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT; +5 s) measured on the PDT day were independently associated with 90-day mortality (adjusted odds ratios 2.54 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.45-4.47], 1.97 [1.16-3.36], and 1.53 [1.02-2.28], respectively; all p ≤ 0.040). Discrimination was good (AUC 0.846; bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.829 [95% CI 0.74-0.93]) with favorable calibration (calibration-in-the-large - 0.01; slope 1.02). The TRS (+ 2 points per + 5 MELD, + 2 per + 10 years, + 1 per + 5 s aPTT) retained discrimination (AUC 0.831) and stratified observed 90-day mortality: 38% (14/37) low, 72% (13/18) intermediate, and 89% (25/28) high. 90-day survival differed across bands (global log-rank p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: For LT recipients who reach the PDT decision point and undergo PDT, the TRS provides internally validated 90-day mortality estimates that may support prognosis-informed multidisciplinary deliberation and bedside risk communication. It should be used only as one component of decision-making and does not estimate the causal effects of PDT, no-PDT strategies, or PDT timing. Use in prolonged-ICU LT recipients without PDT requires separate validation.

articles.title: Intraoperative bedside lung-ultrasound use to optimize positive end-expiratory pressure for elective robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy or cystectomy: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated efficacy and safety of intraoperative individualized stepwise positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) titration guided by lung ultrasound (LUS) in reducing pulmonary atelectasis and complications in patients undergoing robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy or cystectomy (RARPC).
METHODS: This randomized trial included 88 patients undergoing elective RARPC. Patients were assigned to either standard ventilation (PEEP 4 cmH₂O; group C) or LUS-guided stepwise PEEP titration up to 12 cmH₂O (group R). Patients, outcome assessors, and the data analyst were blinded. The primary outcome was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model, estimating the between-group difference in LUS score at 2 h after surgery.
RESULTS: Group R showed significantly lower total LUS scores at 2 h after surgery (adjusted difference: -1.68, 95%CI: -2.89 to -0.47; p = 0.007) compared to group C. Likewise, significantly lower LUS scores were observed in Group R from the end of surgery onward. PEEP titration progressively reduced post-pneumoperitoneum atelectasis rates from 50% to 9.1%, at a highest PEEP level of 12 cmH₂O. Dynamic lung compliance in group R was significantly greater at Top compared with the control group (58.93 ± 3.48 vs. 49.91 ± 5.74 mL/cmH₂O; p < 0.001). Heart rate, mean arterial pressure, oxygen saturation, and end-tidal CO₂ were comparable at all time points. Both groups were comparable for intraoperative hypotension and bradycardia.
CONCLUSION: Intraoperative LUS-guided individualized PEEP optimization significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative atelectasis and improved dynamic lung compliance without compromising hemodynamic stability in patients undergoing RARPC. Lung ultrasound offers a practical, effective, and non-invasive bedside tool for optimizing ventilation in high-risk surgical settings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION AND PROTOCOL: This study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov in March 2024 (ID: NCT06307704). The trial protocol is available through the ClinicalTrials.gov registry at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06307704 .

articles.title: The effects of ephedrine, phenylephrine, and norepinephrine on pregnant human myometrial contractility: an ex vivo study✰.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The choice of vasopressor during Caesarean delivery to prevent maternal hypotension remains debated. This study aimed to determine the concentration-dependent effects of vasopressors on pregnant myometrium, with and without oxytocin.
METHODS: In this prospective ex vivo study, myometrial samples were obtained from full-term pregnant women during elective Caesarean delivery. Myometrial contractility to vasopressors was recorded in the absence/presence of oxytocin compared with controls. Concentration-response testing was done with ephedrine, phenylephrine, and norepinephrine. The primary outcome was the motility index (amplitude×frequency). Isolated primary myometrial cells were also used for calcium mobilisation assays.
RESULTS: Myometrial samples were obtained from 32 females. The mean motility index increased with ephedrine (+39.9%; 95% CI 20.6-62.5; P<0.001) and phenylephrine (+36.2%; 95% CI 19.3-55.4; P<0.001), but norepinephrine had no effect (+12.0%; 95% CI -0.7 to 26.1; P=0.066) compared with control. Similar changes in motility index were observed in the presence of oxytocin. Calcium mobilisation recordings on primary myometrial cells supported the contractility findings, with increases in intracellular calcium ions after ephedrine and phenylephrine, but not with norepinephrine compared with control.
CONCLUSIONS: Ephedrine and phenylephrine increased ex vivo human myometrial contractility, both independently and in combination with oxytocin, consistent with improving uterine tone during Caesarean delivery. Norepinephrine does not affect myometrial contractility, suggesting that it is safe to use before delivery.

articles.title: Association between early self-reported quality of recovery and postoperative complications after non-cardiac surgery: A secondary analysis of three prospective cohort studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To determine the overall postoperative outcome and success, it is important to assess the occurrence of postoperative complications as well as patients' perception of their health outcomes. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between self-reported quality of recovery and postoperative complications.
METHODS: This secondary analysis included data from three prospective observational studies evaluating quality of recovery in patients undergoing elective non-cardiac surgery. Self-reported quality of recovery was assessed using the Quality of Recovery-15 questionnaire (QoR-15), which was completed by patients preoperatively and on the first postoperative day. Postoperative complications were recorded between surgery and hospital discharge according to the Clavien-Dindo classification (CDC) of surgical complications. Binary logistic regression models were used to assess the association between self-reported quality of recovery and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: A total of 1,151 patients were included in this secondary analysis. Of these, 361 (31.4%) experienced postoperative complications. The median difference between preoperative and postoperative QoR-15 sum scores was higher in patients with postoperative complications compared to patients without complications (34 [IQR: 15-51] vs. 22 [IQR: 7-41]; p < 0.001). We found a relevant association between a greater decline in QoR-15 scores from preoperative to first postoperative day and postoperative complications after adjusting for potential confounders (OR 1.18 [95% CI: 1.14;1.23], p < 0.001). The association with no or minor complications was stronger in heterogeneous populations with various types of surgical procedures than in patients with radical prostatectomy.
CONCLUSIONS: Early self-reported quality of recovery is associated with the occurrence of postoperative complications after elective non-cardiac surgery. Whether this association may aid in identifying patients at risk of developing postoperative complications warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins overlap with the hyperinflammatory phenotype in acute respiratory failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of acute respiratory failure (ARF) identifies patients with high mortality, but its underlying pathophysiology remains incompletely understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to inflammation, oxidative stress, and cell injury in critical illness. We investigated whether plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins characterize the hyperinflammatory phenotype and whether they contribute to its association with mortality.
METHODS: We analyzed 285 emergency department patients with ARF and suspected or confirmed COVID-19. Inflammatory phenotypes were derived by latent class analysis using nine biomarkers and clinical indicators. A mitochondrial-protein score was calculated from 59 MitoCarta3.0-matched proteins, and mitochondrial clusters were derived by principal component analysis and k-means clustering. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality.
RESULTS: Latent class analysis identified 185 hypoinflammatory (65%) and 100 hyperinflammatory (35%) patients, with a significant difference in 28-day mortality (14/185, 7.6% vs. 31/100, 31.0%; p < 0.001). The mitochondrial-protein score increased with the probability of hyperinflammation (ρ=0.46, p < 0.001). Forty-three of 59 mitochondrial-associated proteins were more abundant in the hyperinflammatory phenotype, with prominent differences in apoptosis regulation, oxidative stress, and oxidative phosphorylation proteins. In a mutually adjusted model, the hyperinflammatory phenotype remained associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR]=6.40, 95%CI:3.08-13.95; p < 0.001), whereas the mitochondrial-protein score was not (OR=0.83 per SD, 95%CI:0.58-1.17; p = 0.30). Mitochondrial clusters yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of ARF is characterized by increased plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins, linking inflammation with mitochondrial biology and cellular injury. This mitochondrial signature did not account for mortality independently of inflammatory phenotype, suggesting that it represents a biological component of the hyperinflammatory state.

articles.title: Effects of pneumoperitoneum pressure on perioperative atelectasis assessed using lung ultrasonography in patients undergoing robotic-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery: A prospective, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery commonly requires prolonged pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning, which promote perioperative atelectasis and may increase complication risk. We aimed to investigate the effect of low pneumoperitoneum pressure (LPP) on atelectasis following robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, surgeon- and assessor-blind, randomised controlled trial in women undergoing elective robot-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery. Participants were randomly allocated to the LPP (12 mmHg) or standard pneumoperitoneum pressure (SPP: 15 mmHg) group. Primary outcomes were modified lung ultrasound (mLUS) scores assessed after surgery and 30 min post-extubation. Secondary outcomes included incidence of atelectasis, percentage of desaturation in the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU), lengths of PACU and hospital stay, surgeon satisfaction with the operative visual field, numeric rating scale pain score and modified clinical pulmonary infection score on postoperative day 1, and postoperative pulmonary complications 7 days postoperatively.
RESULTS: Sixty patients were enrolled (30 per group). The mLUSs were significantly lower in the LPP group versus the SPP group postoperatively (P < 0.001) and 30 min post-extubation (P < 0.001), particularly in the posterolateral lung region (P < 0.001). Compared with the SPP group, the LPP group experienced a 1.59-fold reduction in the risk of postoperative atelectasis 30 min post-extubation in the PACU (P = 0.004). Other secondary outcomes showed no significant intergroup differences.
CONCLUSIONS: A low pneumoperitoneum pressure during robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery reduced perioperative modified lung ultrasound scores and the incidence of early postoperative atelectasis. However, this imaging difference was not accompanied by significant improvements in oxygenation. Further studies powered for clinical pulmonary outcomes are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, https://www.chictr.org.cn/; ChiCTR 2400085515.

articles.title: Purinergic signaling in perioperative ischemia-reperfusion injury: Pharmacological strategies for organ protection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) remains a significant cause of postoperative organ dysfunction and mortality after cardiac, vascular, transplant, and high-risk noncardiac surgery. Despite advances in anesthetic and surgical techniques, practical strategies to prevent IRI are limited. Growing evidence indicates that purinergic signaling, mediated by extracellular ATP, ADP, adenosine, and their receptors, centrally regulates inflammation, microvascular function, and tissue recovery during perioperative ischemia and reperfusion.
METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes preclinical, translational, and clinical evidence on purinergic mechanisms in perioperative IRI across major organ systems, including the heart, lungs, kidneys, liver, intestines, and brain, emphasizing pharmacological strategies and anesthetic interactions relevant to intraoperative and early postoperative management.
RESULTS: During ischemia and early reperfusion, extracellular ATP released from injured cells activates P2 receptors, promoting inflammasome activation, endothelial dysfunction, and microcirculatory injury. Subsequent hydrolysis of ATP by ectonucleotidases CD39 and CD73 generates adenosine, which activates P1 receptors (Adora1, Adora2a, Adora2b, and Adora3) to suppress inflammation, improve perfusion, and enhance tissue protection. Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-dependent upregulation of CD73 and A2B transcriptionally amplifies this ATP-to-adenosine transition, and miRNAs post-transcriptionally modulate it. Pharmacological approaches targeting these pathways represent promising strategies for perioperative organ protection, whereas clinical evidence supporting anesthetic regimen selection for purinergic modulation remains insufficient. The efficacy of conditioning strategies, including ischemic preconditioning and remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC), remains controversial, with negative large-scale trials highlighting the translational gap between preclinical models and multimorbid surgical patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Purinergic signaling provides a unifying mechanistic framework for perioperative ischemia-reperfusion injury and represents a promising target for pharmacological organ protection. Prioritize pharmacological strategies that enhance adenosine generation, activate protective adenosine receptors, or inhibit ATP-P2X7-driven inflammation in perioperative clinical trials. Understanding how comorbidities and concomitant medications modulate purinergic pathways is essential for successful clinical translation.

articles.title: A Second Major Change in Jehovah's Witness Blood Transfusion Policy within 6 Months.
Effects of lowering inspired oxygen fraction during anesthesia emergence on immediate postoperative loss of lung aeration assessed by ultrasonography: a multicentre randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Controversy remains regarding the effect of inspired oxygen fraction (FIO2) on postoperative lung aeration. We sought to evaluate whether lowering FIO2 solely during emergence from anesthesia reduces immediate postoperative loss of lung aeration, assessed by lung ultrasonography.
METHODS: In this double-blind multicentre randomized controlled trial, we allocated 102 patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrectomy to either a low- or high-FIO2 group (FIO2 = 0.5 vs 0.8 during emergence, respectively). The primary outcome was the lung ultrasonography score (LUS) measured in the postanesthesia care unit (PACU). Secondary outcomes were the Oxygen Reserve Index™ (ORi™) after extubation, atelectasis on chest radiography taken on postoperative day (POD) 2, and oxygen desaturation events in the PACU and within the first 48 postoperative hr.
RESULTS: The median [interquartile range (IQR)] LUS did not significantly differ between the two groups (low-FIO2 group, 3 [2-5] vs high-FIO2 group, 3 [2-6]; P = 0.48). The median [IQR] ORi values after extubation were 0.42 [0.10-0.74] and 0.52 [0.30-0.83] in the low- and high-FIO2 groups, respectively (adjusted P = 0.36). The incidence of atelectasis on chest radiography on POD 2 (low-FIO2 group, 57% vs high-FIO2 group, 49%; P = 0.43; adjusted P > 0.99) and other pulmonary complication rates were not different between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Lowering the FIO2 from 0.8 to 0.5 during the anesthesia emergence period alone did not reduce immediate postoperative LUS after laparoscopic gastrectomy. Routine reduction of the FIO2 < 0.8 during emergence solely for the purpose of preserving postoperative lung aeration may have limited clinical value in a relatively low-risk patient population.
STUDY REGISTRATION: CRIS.nih.go.kr (KCT0008594); first submitted 29 June 2023.

articles.title: Postoperative pulmonary function after video-assisted thoracic surgery using epidural analgesia or oral morphine for pain management: A secondary analysis of the SEAVATS randomised trial.
Anaphylactic Shock With Bovine Serum Albumin Tissue Adhesive (BioGlue) in Cardiac Surgery: Case Series of an Under-Recognised Phenomenon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Anaphylaxis during cardiac surgery is a rare but life-threatening condition in which a severe systemic allergic reaction occurs in response to a specific allergen. BioGlue is a haemostatic agent used in cardiac surgery, composed of 45% purified bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 10% glutaraldehyde. Its use has been associated with anaphylactic shock in rare but well-described cases, typically mediated through immunoglobulin E (IgE) cross-reactivity between feline albumin (Fel d 2) and BSA. We aimed to assess the link between the use of BioGlue in cardiac surgery and anaphylactic reactions, and to identify potential measures to mitigate this risk.
METHOD: This article presents a case series of three patients who developed anaphylactic shock during cardiac surgery following application of BioGlue at a single UK centre within a period of 3 years. A structured literature review was conducted to explore the incidence, potential mechanisms, and management strategies of anaphylactic reactions associated with BioGlue.
RESULTS: All three patients developed profound vasoplegia and bronchospasm during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) shortly after BioGlue application, with markedly elevated serum tryptase. Skin-prick testing confirmed hypersensitivity to the BSA component in all cases. Feline serum albumin (Fel d 2)-specific IgE was detected in all three patients; alpha-galactose sensitisation and overt dietary pork intolerance were absent.
CONCLUSIONS: We emphasise the need for vigilance regarding anaphylactic reactions during cardiac surgery involving BioGlue. Its use should be avoided in patients with known Cat-Pork syndrome. We propose a practical mitigation strategy-saline field washout after BioGlue application-to reduce antigen recirculation via the CPB circuit.

articles.title: Operative management and outcomes of symptomatic carotid near occlusions stenosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To present the outcomes of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and to compare these outcomes with those of patients with symptomatic non-CNO carotid stenosis.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included patients who underwent CEA of the internal carotid artery between January 2011 and December 2025. Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates. The primary endpoint was perioperative stroke, defined as a stroke occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints were cranial nerve injury, cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, surgical revision, bleeding complications, reintubation, and in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: In the unmatched cohort, 1,321 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA), of whom 85 (6.4%) presented with symptomatic CNO. After propensity score matching (2:1), 255 patients were analysed, comprising 85 with symptomatic CNO and 170 matched controls with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis. Baseline and operative characteristics were well balanced. The perioperative stroke rate was similar between patients with symptomatic CNO and those with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis (1.2% vs. 2.4%). No significant differences were observed in myocardial injury (2.4% vs. 2.4%, p>0.9), cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (13% vs. 14%, p>0.9), cranial nerve injury (5.9% vs. 4.1%, p=0.5), surgical revision (7.1% vs. 5.9%, p=0.7), or postoperative bleeding (5.9% vs. 5.3%, p>0.9).
CONCLUSION: Carotid endarterectomy using the eversion technique appears feasible and can be performed with an acceptable perioperative complication rate in selected patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion. Although no statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were observed compared with patients undergoing CEA for conventional symptomatic carotid stenosis, the limited sample size and low event rates preclude conclusions about equivalence. Further studies with larger cohorts and long-term neurological follow-up are warranted to establish the clinical benefit of surgical revascularisation in this patient population.

articles.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) allows real-time assessment of the anesthetic state of the brain and offers a means of titrating anesthetic delivery in children. Randomized trials have shown that EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure, shortens emergence and recovery, and lowers the incidence of emergence delirium, yet routine use outside research settings has remained largely confined to enthusiastic clinicians and clinical trials.
AIMS: To describe the adoption of routine intraoperative raw EEG monitoring over time at a quaternary pediatric hospital, to characterize practice variation among anesthesia providers, and to identify patient and procedural factors associated with EEG use.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of anesthetic records in the electronic health record from 17 October 2024, when automated EEG capture began, to 30 June 2026, following departmental implementation of routine raw EEG monitoring. Providers were categorized by EEG use as high (> 40% of cases), moderate (20%-40%) or low (< 20%). Trend, provider-level, and procedural associations with EEG use were examined using segmented regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and clustered logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 26 168 analyzed cases, 21.7% (5674) involved intraoperative EEG monitoring, provided by 59 staff anesthesiologists, 9 senior fellows, 24 fellows, and 102 residents. EEG use rose from 17.8% of cases in October 2024 to 28.4% in June 2026. Use varied widely among staff anesthesiologists (median 18.1%, IQR 12.3%-31.3%; range 0.9%-79.5%); 59.3% (35/59) were low users, and 18.6% (11/59) were high users, with the five highest users accounting for 27.0% of all EEG-monitored cases managed by staff. Case mix explained only a small proportion of this variation (pseudo R2 = 0.064). EEG-monitored cases were more often longer, involved neuromuscular blockade, TIVA maintenance, cardiac surgery, and trainee presence.
CONCLUSIONS: Adoption of routine raw EEG monitoring increased steadily but nonlinearly following implementation. Variation in use among providers was only weakly explained by case mix, indicating that individual practice patterns, more than patient or procedural characteristics, drove uptake. Efforts to broaden EEG monitoring may benefit from targeting low-use providers and during fellowship training.

articles.title: Complex Type Split Cord Malformation: A Two-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Complex spinal dysraphism is the condition where multiple dysraphic pathologies are observed in the same patient. Complex type split cord malformation (SCM) is a compound dysraphic phenotype involving disruptions at multiple developmental stages, characterized by the co-occurrence of SCM and spina bifida aperta. This study aimed to understand the differences between complex SCMs from classical SCM cases in terms of embryological aspects, perioperative management, and follow-up.
METHODS: Patients with SCM associated with spina bifida aperta who were treated at Dicle University and Kocaeli University, Departments of Neurosurgery, between 2011 and 2025 were included in the study. Patient age (months), gender, presenting clinic, lesion localization, SCM type, number of affected vertebrae, neurological status, presence of tethered cord, presence of kyphoscoliosis, spina bifida aperta type, Chiari malformation, syringomyelia, presence of posterior fusion defect number of vertebrae with defect, hydrocephalus, accompanying intracranial pathologies, and additional anomalies were included in the study.
RESULTS: The study included 44 patients who underwent surgery for complex SCM. Of the patients, 81.8% were operated on during the neonatal period in the same session with spina bifida aperta surgery. Surgery was planned for 11.4% of patients for follow-up purposes and for 6.8% following detection of SCM on MRI performed due to gait disturbances. It was observed that 68.2% of patients were plegic/severely paretic, 22.7% had moderate paresis, and 9.1% had mild paresis/normally. Regarding the type of spina bifida aperta, 72.7% of patients had myelomeningocele, and 27.3% had myeloschisis. Type 1 SCM was detected in 79.5% of patients, type 2 SCM in 13.6%, and type 1.5 SCM in 6.8%. Additionally, 93.2% had tethered cord/thickened-fatty filum terminale, 90.9% had posterior fusion defects, 77.3% had hydrocephalus, 68.2% had kyphoscoliosis, 65.9% had Chiari malformation, 54.5% had syringomyelia, 45.5% had intracranial pathologies other than hydrocephalus, and 4.6% had lipoma.
CONCLUSION: Complex SCMs should not be viewed solely as a spinal pathology; they should be evaluated multidisciplinarily in the perioperative period in terms of anomalies accompanying spina bifida aperta. In these cases that are diagnosed at a younger age, the incidence of type 1 SCM increases, while the frequency of occurrence in the lumbar region decreases and increases in the thoracic region. Furthermore, it has been determined that additional anomalies accompanying spina bifida aperta occur more frequently with complex SCMs.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of older adults who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery for symptomatic Rathke cleft cysts.
articles.abstract: Rathke cleft cysts (RCCs) are benign cystic lesions in the sellar and suprasellar regions that are often asymptomatic but may cause symptoms due to the compression of adjacent structures. With the aging of population, the incidence of symptomatic RCCs in older adults is increasing. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics, surgical outcomes, and follow-up between older and younger adult patients systematically. A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients aged ≥ 18 years who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) for RCCs at a single center from 2011 to 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: nonelderly (18-59 years) and elderly (≥ 60 years). A total of 153 patients were analyzed, with 120 younger and 33 older adult patients. Older adults presented more frequently with dizziness and fatigue. The elderly group had a shorter operation time, whereas the other surgical outcomes were similar between the two groups. The incidences of perioperative diabetes insipidus and mortality during follow-up were significantly higher in the elderly group. The recurrence rate was also higher, but no significant difference was observed. In multivariable Fine-Gray competing risk analysis, older age (adjusted SHR: 3.99, 95% CI: 1.45-11.00, p = 0.007) and cyst location, including both suprasellar (adjusted SHR: 12.70, 95% CI: 1.39-115.00, p = 0.024) and sellar-suprasellar extension (adjusted SHR: 8.67, 95% CI: 1.09-68.70, p = 0.041; vs. sellar), were associated with recurrence, whereas preoperative hypopituitarism was not (adjusted SHR: 2.20, 95% CI: 0.76-6.36, p = 0.200). EES is safe and effective for elderly patients with symptomatic RCCs. Elderly patients often present with atypical symptoms, leading to a delayed diagnosis. RCCs seem to be more likely to recur in older patients than in younger adults; thus, more careful monitoring and longer follow-up period is needed on the older adults.

articles.title: An observational study protocol characterising pain trajectories, opioid use and predictors of chronic postsurgical pain in children with cerebral palsy undergoing orthopaedic surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Children with cerebral palsy (CP) are likely at greater risk for developing chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) due to their high prevalence of pre-existing pain and frequency of orthopaedic procedures. However, little is known about the prevalence, trajectories and risk factors of CPSP or persistent opioid use among children with CP undergoing orthopaedic surgery. Understanding CPSP and patterns of postoperative opioid use in this population is crucial to optimise perioperative pain management, inform opioid stewardship practices, improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare use and costs.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This multi-site, prospective, longitudinal study aims to recruit 450 children aged 5–17 years with CP undergoing orthopaedic surgery. Participants will complete study assessments from 1 month before surgery to 12 months postoperatively. Study measures include preoperative quantitative sensory testing; caregiver-reported and child-reported (for participants ≥8 years who are cognitively able) assessments of pain and psychosocial factors at five time points; real-time postoperative text message assessments of pain and opioid use; and postoperative gait laboratory measures of functional outcomes. Demographic and surgical, and clinical data, including medical history, inpatient postoperative pain scores and analgesic medication use, will be extracted from the electronic medical record. Analysis will (1) characterise the postoperative pain and opioid use trajectories, (2) identify predictors of CPSP and persistent opioid use and (3) examine relationships between perioperative pain severity and the functional mobility outcomes achieved via orthopaedic surgery.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Central and local Institutional Review Boards at each site have approved the study. Study results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journal publications and presentations at scientific conferences.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05764681.

articles.title: SiLaC versus PEPSiT for pediatric pilonidal sinus disease: a monocentric retrospective cohort study (PILO-LASER).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence comparing minimally invasive approaches for pediatric pilonidal sinus disease (PSD) is limited. We aimed to compare the effectiveness of Sinus Laser-Assisted Closure (SiLaC) and Pediatric Endoscopic Pilonidal Sinus Treatment (PEPSiT), with particular emphasis on wound healing time and disease recurrence rate.
METHODS: A retrospective monocentric cohort study was conducted including patients aged under 18 years treated for PSD between January 2022 and December 2025. The primary outcome was wound healing time. Secondary outcomes included recurrence rate, postoperative complications and operative time.
RESULTS: Seventy-three patients were included: 21 underwent SiLaC and 52 underwent PEPSiT. Age, sex, height, weight and body mass index did not differ significantly between groups, whereas redo surgery was more frequent in the SiLaC group (6/21 vs. 3/52; p = 0.014). Median wound healing time was significantly shorter following SiLaC than PEPSiT (15 [IQR 15-22] vs. 55.5 [IQR 24.3-113.3] days; p < 0.001; Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the location shift - 38 days, 95% CI - 55 to - 14). Among the 69 patients with available data, recurrence was observed in 3/19 (15.8%) in the SiLaC group and 12/50 (24.0%) in the PEPSiT group (Fisher's exact test, p = 0.534; odds ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.15-2.39). Operative time was slightly shorter with SiLaC (18 vs. 22 min; p = 0.046), although the 95% CI of the location shift reached zero (- 4 min, 95% CI - 8 to 0). No Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ II complication occurred. Follow-up was shorter in the SiLaC group (2 vs. 5 months; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: SiLaC was associated with significantly shorter time to clinically documented wound healing. Recurrence findings should be interpreted as short-term observations; the study does not investigate long-term recurrence rates. SiLaC's compatibility with lateral positioning and local or locoregional anesthesia may facilitate perioperative and postoperative management. Prospective studies with longer follow-up are warranted to assess long-term efficacy, recurrence, recovery, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Characteristics and co-morbidities of pediatric patients requiring cholecystectomy.
articles.abstract: Cholelithiasis in children is an increasingly recognized condition, due to the rising prevalence of risk factors and advances in diagnostic techniques. This retrospective descriptive cohort analyzed the characteristics of patients who underwent surgery for cholelithiasis in two Italian centers. From 2013 to 2023, 53 pediatric patients were retrospectively analyzed. Data collected included surgical indications, predisposing factors, and perioperative management. When preoperative ultrasound detected stones in the common bile duct, Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) was performed, followed by Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (LC) after two months. Postoperative clinical and ultrasonographic follow-up was conducted at 6 months and 1 year. The primary indication for surgery was symptomatic cholelithiasis in 38 patients (71.7%), followed by acute cholecystitis in 11 (20.7%) and persistent cholelithiasis in 4 (7.6%). Predisposing factors included hematological disorders in 14 cases (26.4%), a positive family history in 25 (47.2%), exposure to lithogenic substances in 9 (17.0%), and obesity in 9 (17.0%). ERCP was performed in 7 patients. Postoperative complications included one case of biliary fistula and one case of post-cholecystectomy syndrome. At follow-up, all patients were asymptomatic except for two who reported nonspecific abdominal pain. The most common risk factors for pediatric cholelithiasis in our cohort were a positive family history, hematological disorders, and obesity. LC remains the standard surgical treatment in children, with the primary aim of preventing complications.
articles.journal_full: La Pediatria medica e chirurgica : Medical and surgical pediatrics

articles.title: Acupuncture for Perioperative Pain Management in Cesarean Section: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Focusing on Pain Subtypes and Heterogeneity Exploration.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cesarean section (CS) is among the most common surgical procedures worldwide, yet postoperative pain management remains challenging, with opioid-related adverse effects constraining analgesic options in lactating women.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy of acupuncture and acupoint stimulation for perioperative pain management in CS, focusing on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)-classified pain subtypes and heterogeneity sources.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and CBM through January 15, 2025 (PROSPERO: CRD42023487558). Eligible studies were RCTs evaluating acupuncture for CS perioperative pain. Primary outcomes were 24-h and 48-h pain intensity and analgesic consumption. Fixed- or random-effects models were used according to the heterogeneity criteria described in the Methods. Heterogeneity was explored via meta-regression, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses. Certainty was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Forty-one RCTs (n = 4,823) were included. Acupuncture and acupoint stimulation significantly reduced 24-hour pain (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -2.63, 95% CI [-2.97, -2.28]; prediction interval [-4.80, -0.46]; I² = 94%) and 48-hour pain (MD = -2.06, 95% CI [-2.29, -1.82]; I² = 96%). Low-RoB sensitivity analysis yielded SMD = -1.42, suggesting unblinded designs inflate estimates. Combined modalities produced the largest effect (SMD = -2.75). GRADE certainty was low-to-moderate across outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Acupuncture and acupoint stimulation may reduce pain after cesarean section. Substantial heterogeneity, risk of bias and low-to-moderate certainty limit confidence in the magnitude and applicability of the pooled effects. Use as an adjunct in enhanced recovery pathways warrants evaluation in rigorously designed trials.

articles.title: Case Report: Manic Decompensation During the Second Trimester of Pregnancy Requiring Electroconvulsive Therapy.
articles.abstract: Manic episodes during pregnancy represent a significant clinical challenge due to risks for both the mother and fetus, as well as the limitations inherent to pharmacological treatment during gestation. Severe affective episodes-particularly those with manic symptoms-may lead to heightened maternal stress, impulsive behaviors, impaired self-care, and potential obstetric complications. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) constitutes a therapeutic alternative when pharmacotherapy is ineffective or contraindicated. We present the case of a 31-year-old pregnant woman with a history of an unspecified affective disorder within the bipolar spectrum, who developed an acute manic episode during the second trimester following withdrawal of lithium for conception planning. The patient required psychiatric hospitalization due to progressive psychomotor agitation, disinhibition, and insomnia. After multidisciplinary evaluation, nine ECT sessions were administered between 18 and 21 weeks of gestation, with standardized anesthetic management and close obstetric monitoring. No maternal or fetal complications were observed. The patient exhibited progressive clinical improvement, allowing stabilization and safe continuation of pregnancy. This case highlights the potential efficacy and relative safety of ECT in managing severe manic episodes during pregnancy when prompt maternal stabilization is required. It also underscores the importance of coordinated multidisciplinary care and individualized risk-benefit assessment.

articles.title: Association between prior epidural labour analgesia and increased incidence of hypotension after spinal anaesthesia for caesarean section: A retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: The administration of spinal anaesthesia after epidural labour analgesia may increase the risk of block failure or high spinal block, particularly when the intrathecal local anaesthetic dose is reduced. This retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study evaluated the feasibility of using a standard spinal dose in partients (i.e. women who are in labour) with epidural labour analgesia undergoing caesarean section. Women who underwent caesarean delivery between April 2016 and March 2020 were analysed. The primary outcome was the rate of conversion to general anaesthesia. After 161 patients had been matched in the epidural labour analgesia-to-spinal anaesthesia and spinal anaesthesia groups, general anaesthesia conversion rates were comparable (3.3% vs 2.5%, P = 0.544); all conversions resulted from block failure. However, the epidural labour analgesia-to-spinal anaesthesia group experienced significantly more frequent hypotension (55.9% vs 30.4%, P < 0.001) and required higher doses of ephedrine (mean 8.3, standard deviation 9.8 mg vs mean 5.9, standard deviation 11.1 mg, P = 0.036). Although epidural labour analgesia did not increase the rates of block failure or high spinal block when preventive strategies were utilised, it was associated with a higher incidence of hypotension and increased vasopressor requirements.

articles.title: Bioadhesive Hyaluronic Acid-Cellulose Hydrogels for Sustained BDNF Release to Mitigate Local Anesthetic Neurotoxicity and Enhance Peripheral Nerve Repair.
articles.abstract: Peripheral nerve block (PNB) is indispensable in regional anesthesia, yet local anesthetics such as lidocaine can provoke neurotoxicity, causing dorsal root ganglion injury and delayed nerve recovery. Although brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is a potent neuroregenerative cue, its clinical value is limited by rapid degradation and poor local retention. Here, we report an injectable, bioadhesive hybrid covalent/dynamic hydrogel (DAHA-POMC) constructed from hyaluronic acid and cellulose for sustained BDNF delivery and peripheral nerve repair. The hydrogel exhibited rapid in situ gelation, favorable mechanics, elastic recovery, and controllable degradation, enabling prolonged retention of bioactive BDNF. In vitro, BDNF released from the DAHA-POMC hydrogel retained neurotrophic activity, and protected lidocaine-exposed dorsal root ganglion (DRG)-derived neuronal cells by improving viability, preserving mitochondrial membrane potential, reducing apoptosis, and promoting axonal outgrowth. Transcriptomic and protein analyses supported the involvement of ERK signaling in this neuroprotective effect. In vivo, in an intraneural lidocaine-associated sciatic nerve injury (SNI) model, the BDNF-loaded hydrogel significantly outperformed free BDNF, improving nerve conduction, remyelination, and gastrocnemius muscle preservation. Collectively, this work establishes DAHA-POMC as a multifunctional neuroregenerative platform that integrates localized BDNF delivery with regenerative tissue support, offering a potential post-injury treatment strategy for focal peripheral nerve injury associated with local-anesthetic exposure.

articles.title: Modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through a perichondrial approach for postoperative analgesia after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative analgesia after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy is challenging in patients with obesity because of opioid-related respiratory risks. We evaluated the incremental analgesic effect of adding ropivacaine to a bilateral modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through a perichondrial approach.
METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial included 100 adults undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. Patients received bilateral ultrasound-guided modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through a perichondrial approach with 30 mL of 0.2% ropivacaine or placebo (30 mL of 0.9% saline) per side. Pain intensity was assessed for 24-hours using a 0-10 Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). Morphine consumption, postoperative recovery, 15-item Quality of Recovery (QoR-15) score, adverse effects, and interleukin-6 and interleukin-8 concentrations were also evaluated. Repeated outcomes were analyzed using linear or generalized linear mixed models.
RESULTS: Across 24-hours, the overall mean difference in pain at rest was -0.57-points (95% Confidence Interval [95% CI -1.21 to 0.08]; p = 0.085), with no group-by-time interaction (p = 0.836). Pain during movement was lower with ropivacaine (overall mean difference, -0.84-points; 95% CI -1.46 to -0.23; p = 0.008), without a significant group-by-time interaction (p = 0.078). Twenty-four-hour morphine consumption was 10 (7-14) versus 11 (5-19) mg (p = 0.473). The median QoR-15 score was 125 (116-132) versus 118 (110-124) (p = 0.042), whereas recovery-category distributions did not differ (p = 0.140). No overall group differences were observed for postoperative symptoms or interleukin-6 or interleukin-8.
CONCLUSION: Adding ropivacaine to bilateral modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through a perichondrial approach produced a modest reduction in pain during movement without reducing pain at rest or morphine consumption. The improvement in postoperative recovery was small.

articles.title: Intrathecal morphine with or without transversus abdominis plane block for major abdominal surgery: a retrospective exploratory cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether adding a Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block to Intrathecal Morphine (ITM) improves analgesia after open Major Abdominal Surgery (MAS) is unknown. In cesarean delivery, the combination provides no additional benefit, but MAS involves greater tissue trauma and a larger visceral pain component. We assessed the additive analgesic value of TAP block to ITM in MAS.
METHODS: In this retrospective exploratory cohort study, patients undergoing MAS at a single center who received at least one regional technique were categorized into three groups: ITM alone, TAP block alone, or both. Primary outcomes were maximum pain score and total opioid consumption during the first 24 postoperative hours. Multivariable regression adjusted for prespecified prognostic factors.
RESULTS: Of 271 patients analyzed (ITM, n = 105; TAP block, n = 122; both, n = 44), ITM was associated with significantly lower adjusted pain scores (β = -1.26; 95% CI: -2.19, -0.34; p = 0.003) and opioid consumption (β = -18.61; 95% CI: -26.76, -10.47; p < 0.001) at 0-24 hours compared with TAP block alone. Adding a TAP block to ITM was not associated with additional benefit, with no significant differences between the two groups in pain scores (β = -0.01; 95% CI: -1.14, 1.12; p = 0.98) or opioid consumption (β = 2.27; 95% CI: -7.67, 12.22; p = 0.582). These differences were most pronounced during the first 8 postoperative hours and equalized by 16-24 hours.
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing MAS, adding a TAP block to ITM was not associated with additional analgesic benefit. ITM alone was associated with significantly lower pain scores and opioid consumption compared with TAP block.

articles.title: Sensitivity to Physical Activity Predicts Daily Physical Activity Levels in People with Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether Sensitivity to Physical Activity (SPA, a measure of changes in pain responses to standardized physical tasks) predicts self-report and objective physical activity levels in individuals with chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) pain. We also examined whether SPA offers predictive value in activity levels beyond psychological factors and quantitative sensory testing (QST).
METHODS: Sixty-one participants with chronic MSK pain completed a standardized SPA lifting task, psychological questionnaires (Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, Pain Catastrophizing Scale), and QST (pressure pain thresholds, temporal summation of pain). Participants wore an accelerometer for up to nine days to objectively measure physical activity. Self-reported activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Hierarchical regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the predictive value of SPA, psychological, and QST measures on physical activity outcomes.
RESULTS: SPA significantly predicted objectively measured daily physical activity levels, explaining unique variance in both average daily steps (ΔR²=11.6%, P=0.005) and time spent performing moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (ΔR²=6.1%, P=0.030), after controlling for age and pain levels. SPA was not associated with self-reported physical activity. Neither psychological factors nor QST measures significantly predicted objective or subjective activity levels.
DISCUSSION: Lifting-based SPA emerged as a unique predictor of real-world physical activity in individuals with chronic MSK pain, outperforming traditional psychological and sensory predictors. These findings support the potential of SPA as a biopsychosocial marker for physical inactivity and the importance of objective activity monitoring in rehabilitation planning.

articles.title: Effect of PEEP on Diaphragm Is Associated with Lung Recruitability in ARDS: A Physiological Study.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
articles.journal_full: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Cardiovascular physiology of respiratory support in acute cardiac critical illness: A hemodynamic guided approach.
articles.abstract: Respiratory support is traditionally regarded as a treatment for respiratory failure. However, interventions that modify pleural pressure, transpulmonary pressure, lung volume, or the work of breathing simultaneously influence venous return, ventricular loading conditions, pulmonary vascular resistance, ventricular interdependence, myocardial oxygen demand, cardiac output, and systemic perfusion. Consequently, similar respiratory interventions may produce different haemodynamic effects according to the predominant cardiovascular physiology. This narrative review examines heart-lung interactions during respiratory support in acute cardiac critical illness and proposes a physiology-based framework organized around three predominant haemodynamic phenotypes: left ventricular congestion/afterload excess, left ventricular low-output/cardiogenic shock, and right ventricular pressure overload/failure. Acute pulmonary embolism is considered an important aetiology of the latter phenotype rather than a separate haemodynamic category. We discuss how high-flow nasal oxygen, continuous positive airway pressure, bilevel non-invasive ventilation, and invasive mechanical ventilation modify cardiovascular physiology and how their effects may be anticipated and reassessed using clinical examination, systemic perfusion, haemodynamic monitoring, focused echocardiography, and lung ultrasound. These phenotypes are dynamic and may overlap or evolve during critical illness; therefore, the proposed framework should be regarded as a conceptual bedside approach rather than a validated therapeutic algorithm. Respiratory support may consequently be considered a cardiovascular as well as a respiratory intervention, requiring repeated assessment of both respiratory benefit and haemodynamic cost.

articles.title: The SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol and Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS) for dynamic assessment of peripheral edema burden in critically ill patients: a prospective, longitudinal observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excessive fluid resuscitation may lead to pathologic fluid accumulation and increased mortality. Cumulative fluid balance (CFB) correlates poorly with outcomes. Ultrasonographic central congestion metrics (VExUS/Lung ultrasound) inherently overlook critical fluid shifts within the peripheral reservoir. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed the SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol for standardized, semi-quantitative assessment of peripheral edema burden.
METHODS: Ultrasonographic assessment was performed bilaterally across six core anatomical regions using the SUBCUT protocol on days 1, 3, and 7. Individual sites were graded semi-quantitatively using the Ultrasonographic Subcutaneous Edema Grade (USEG, 0-4), yielding the Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS, 0-48) as the cumulative sum across 12 evaluation sites. The primary endpoint was ICU mortality, evaluating the prognostic performance of Day 3 SWELS.
RESULTS: Among 111 patients analyzed (ICU mortality 23.4%; 26/111), baseline SWELS and CFB were similar between survivors and non-survivors. By Day 3, median SWELS surged in non-survivors (24 vs. 8; P < .001), yielding greater unadjusted, apparent discrimination than CFB (AUC 0.86 vs. 0.65). In competing-risk analysis, a 5-point increase in Day 3 SWELS was independently associated with ICU mortality (sHR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.22-1.86; P < .001). Incorporating Day 3 SWELS into a contemporaneous clinical base model (Age, Admission Sepsis, Day 3 SOFA) enhanced model fit and discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.043; P = .008).
CONCLUSIONS: The SUBCUT protocol provides a novel framework for assessing peripheral edema burden. At Day 3, its derivative, SWELS, demonstrates incremental prognostic association beyond contemporaneous organ dysfunction, offering an extravascular perspective for multi-compartment fluid mapping.

articles.title: Magnesium slips through the filter.
Health-care utilization, costs, and quality of life in patients with sepsis: Results from the SAGA trial in the Netherlands.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis imposes a substantial clinical and economic burden, yet detailed patient-level data on long-term healthcare costs and quality of life (QoL) is mainly based on intensive care unit (ICU) survivors and relies on model-based projections for patients treated in general wards.
AIM: To assess direct and indirect healthcare costs and QoL during the first year after community-onset sepsis.
METHODS: Data were obtained from a cluster-randomized trial of patients hospitalized with sepsis of urological, abdominal or unknown origin in the Netherlands. Mean direct hospitalization costs were collected from hospital data. Additional healthcare utilization and productivity losses were obtained through structured questionnaires in a subset of patients followed for 12 months. We used inverse probability weighting to adjust for differences between the subset and full cohort. QALYs were estimated using the EQ-5D-5L at months 0 (then-test), 2, 6, and 12, and the SF-36 was administered at 12 months.
RESULTS: Among 472 patients, 91 (19%) required ICU admission. Mean direct hospitalization costs were €8858 (95% CI: 7988-9855) per patient: €6697 (95% CI: 6185-7251) for general ward-admitted patients and €18,155 (95% CI: 14,856-22,342) for ICU-admitted patients. Over 12 months, mean total costs per patient were €30,889 (95% CI: 22,485-43,105): €25,839 (95% CI: 19,089-35,845) for general ward-admitted patients and €41,769 (95% CI: 23,132-48,943) for ICU-admitted patients. The weighted mean QALY during follow-up was 0.62 (95% CI: 0.51-0.74) compared with 0.65 (95% CI: 0.54-0.75) before sepsis. SF-36 at 12 months showed the greatest limitations in general health, physical role functioning, and energy/fatigue.
CONCLUSION: Sepsis is followed by substantial healthcare and societal costs during the first year after admission, with a significant burden among patient treated in general wards. By providing Dutch patient-level cost and QoL data across ICU and non-ICU settings, this study enables improved economic evaluations and better-informed health policy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: European Union Clinical Trials Register (2021-001,840-83). Count = 296.

articles.title: Preoperative Serum Biomarkers Improve Prediction of Poor Postoperative Outcome After Cardiopulmonary Bypass Compared With Clinical Variables in Neonates.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Neonates undergoing surgery for congenital heart disease (CHD) are at risk for poor postoperative outcomes after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), including death, prolonged ICU stay, and ICU readmission. Current prognostic models rely predominantly on nonmodifiable clinical factors.
OBJECTIVES: To utilize machine learning methods to compare the predictive utility of preoperative blood biomarkers vs. clinical features alone for ICU-30, a validated composite outcome after neonatal CPB that includes postoperative 30-day morbidity and mortality.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prospective observational single-center cohort study of consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days undergoing CPB for CHD.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Plasma and clinical data were collected from consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days immediately before CPB. Thirty-seven biomarkers were measured by individual or multiplex enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and tested for association with ICU-30, defined as 1) mortality within 30 days of CPB, 2) ICU stay longer than 30 days, or 3) ICU readmission within 30 days. Predictive performance of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and random forest (RF) models was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). For XGBoost, the top 20 features were identified based on model importance (gain).
RESULTS: Biomarkers were available for 144 neonates. Most were male (51%), White (64%), and non-Hispanic (75%). Most operations were Society of Thoracic Surgeons-European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery (STAT) category 3 (32%) or STAT category 5 (29%). ICU-30 occurred in 29 neonates (20%). Using combined clinical and biomarker data, XGBoost demonstrated moderate discrimination for ICU-30 (AUROC, 0.74), outperformed RF (AUROC, 0.72), and LASSO (AUROC, 0.70). Biomarkers alone performed better (AUROC, 0.72) than clinical data alone (AUROC, 0.67) with XGBoost. The top two features in the combined XGBoost model were neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) and trefoil factor 3 (TFF3). Using Shapley additive explanation to assess both predictive impact and directionality, the most influential features were NGAL, a disintegrin and metalloproteinase with a thrombospondin type 1 motif, member 13 (ADAMTS13), and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among neonates with CHD requiring CPB, multibiomarker models improved prediction of poor postoperative outcome compared with clinical variables alone. The most informative model features included markers of renal injury/perfusion and gastrointestinal epithelial injury (NGAL and TFF3), as well as vascular injury and inflammation (ADAMTS13 and Ang-2). These findings support further investigation of biomarker-informed risk stratification and may provide insight into pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying adverse postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: How ICU Teams Can Engage With Healthcare Leaders to Transform the Practice of Critical Care Medicine Through ICU Liberation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The ICU liberation ABCDEF bundle is a quality improvement (QI) tool designed to optimize pain, sedation, and delirium management in critically ill patients, to facilitate ventilator weaning and early mobility in patients, and to increase patient and family engagement in care. Increasing bundle performance is associated with improved ICU patient outcomes and reduced healthcare costs. Support for bundle implementation and sustainability efforts by healthcare system leaders is the strongest determinant of bundle performance. This narrative review outlines strategies that ICU teams can use to secure the necessary executive support for their bundle implementation and sustainability efforts to improve their bundle performance.
DATA SOURCES: Medline and PubMed databases. Search terms included critical care, ICU liberation, ABCDEF bundle, ICU outcomes, QI, implementation, patient safety, healthcare leadership, and administrative harm.
STUDY SELECTION: Peer-reviewed clinical trials, systematic reviews, observational studies, and narrative reviews (English only, from January 1990 to June 2025) focusing on the clinical and economic impacts of the ICU liberation ABCDEF bundle and the role of healthcare leadership in improving bundle performance.
DATA EXTRACTION: Data were narratively aggregated without new statistical meta-analyses.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Leadership strategies that support bundle performance include: executive sponsors engaging with ICU teams, developing an executive pitch, making a compelling business case for bundle implementation, and aligning the bundle with healthcare system strategic initiatives. Healthcare leaders should prioritize patient safety, teamwork, and family engagement in the ICU and provide the necessary information technology and QI resources to support data-driven bundle performance efforts.
CONCLUSIONS: The ICU liberation ABCDEF bundle offers a synergistic, patient-centered framework to improve ICU patient care and outcomes and reduce healthcare costs for all ICU patients. Executive support for the bundle significantly improves bundle performance by ICU teams. ICU teams must partner with healthcare executives to get the necessary resources for their bundle implementation efforts.

articles.title: Stakeholders' Perceptions About Intraoperative Communication and Hand-Offs During Liver Transplant.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: After multidisciplinary discussion of a complication during orthotopic liver transplant at our institution, we sought to evaluate stakeholders' perceptions of cross-disciplinary communication and management of intraoperative hand-offs.
METHODS: Semistructured interviews were performed with operating room (OR) personnel who participate in liver transplants at our hospital (surgical technologists, anesthesiology, and surgery). Interview transcripts were coded using inductive and deductive analysis.
RESULTS: Participants identified role-specific critical time periods which mandated complete concentration and varying strategies to minimize interruptions during these times. Participants described several team characteristics and individual behaviors which influence safety, including paying attention, assisting others, documenting relevant information (such as time of organ out of ice and time of reperfusion), minimizing interruptions, cross-disciplinary communication, team member familiarity, and the microculture within the transplant OR. We identified role-specific variation in optimal timing of intraoperative hand-offs during liver transplant; however, participants were unanimous that hand-offs were inappropriate during warm ischemia and reperfusion as well as any periods of patient instability. Anesthesiology and surgery interviewees agreed that cross-disciplinary communication leading up to warm ischemia and reperfusion is critical to patient safety during this high-risk period.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings have informed a quality improvement project to optimize intraoperative communication during liver transplants at our institution.

articles.title: Robot-assisted pyelo-ureteral reconstruction for ureteral stricture in kidney transplant recipients: functional outcomes and perioperative morbidity from a bicentric cohort.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In kidney transplantation, urinary complications are the most common (occurring in 4-10% of cases), with ureteral strictures (US) and vesicoureteral reflux being the most prevalent. Initial management often involves emergency urinary diversions, which serve as long-term palliative solutions. Reconstruction via pyeloplasty or pyelo-native ureteral anastomosis is the gold standard technique following failure of endoscopic treatment. Whilst open surgery remains the standard approach, robot-assisted laparoscopy may reduce parietal trauma in these immunocompromised patients and optimise preservation of peri-ureteral tissues. However, data on this approach remain limited. The aim of our study was to evaluate the functional outcomes in intention to treat of this technique.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, two-centre study was conducted, including kidney transplant recipients who underwent urinary anastomosis reconstruction (pyelo-native ureteral anastomosis, uretero-ureteral anastomosis or uretero-vesicostomy) via robot-assisted laparoscopy between March 2018 and January 2026. The primary outcome measure was the absence of upper urinary diversion (endoureteral stent or nephrostomy) at one year, analysed in intention to treat. Secondary outcome measures included anatomical restoration, changes in serum creatinine levels and postoperative morbidity according to the Clavien-Dindo classification.
RESULTS: Twenty-four patients were included (mean age 54 years). Two procedures were terminated intraoperatively due to a complete pelvic retraction in the context of chronic graft rejection. Technical feasibility was 91.6% (22/24). Overall treatment success, defined as freedom from urinary diversion at one year in intention to treat, was 66.7% (14/21), and functional success among evaluable reconstructed patients was 77.8% (14/18).
