The eye-opening time, orientation recovery time, and time to discharge from the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) in the sufentanil group were longer than those in the alfentanil group (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Compared with sufentanil induction, alfentanil administration in laparoscopic colorectal surgery for elderly patients can more effectively reduce hemodynamic fluctuations, decrease the use of intraoperative active drugs, and ensure rapid awakening without increasing postoperative adverse reactions - that is, it provides a higher level of comfort.

articles.title: Pediatric Dermatologic Conditions.
articles.abstract: Pediatric skin conditions of the lower extremity present a diagnostic and management challenge, and this article offers the practitioner a systematic framework. It opens with practical guidance on performing cutaneous procedures in children-engaging the parent, minimizing pain and anxiety through topical anesthesia and distraction, and setting postoperative limits for optimal scar outcomes. It then surveys environmentally induced disorders, bites and stings, genodermatoses including the palmoplantar keratodermas, and bacterial, viral, and fungal infections. Eczematous conditions, psoriasis, nevi, pediatric melanoma, and nail disorders are each reviewed with attention to lower extremity presentation, common misdiagnoses, and current management strategies.
articles.journal_full: Clinics in podiatric medicine and surgery

articles.title: Transfusion practices among children admitted to a South African PICU following cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood products may be required in patients undergoing cardiac surgery; however, there is a paucity of data on blood transfusion guidelines in the perioperative and postoperative cardiac surgery period.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the prevalence of blood product transfusion, factors associated with transfusion and outcomes in patients who received blood products following cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This was a prospective, single-centre observational study that consecutively recruited 126 children aged <18 years admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) following cardiac surgery between July 2017 and January 2018. Demographic, intraoperative and postoperative blood product transfusion data were extracted from patient records, entered into a standardised case record form and analysed using Statistica version 13 (StatSoft Inc, USA). Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.
RESULTS: Of the recruited children, 53% received blood products, with 30.9% receiving cryoprecipitate, 22.2% receiving packed red blood cells, 18.3% receiving albumin, 15.9% receiving fresh frozen plasma and 15.1% receiving platelet concentrates. Factors associated with the use of blood products included previous cardiac surgery, younger age, lower weight and prolonged coagulation parameters (p<0.05). Receiving blood products was associated with worse outcomes: a standardised mortality ratio of 3.1 v. 0 (p<0.0001), median (IQR) PICU length of stay of 5 (3 - 11) v. 2 (2 - 5) days (p<0.0001), and duration of mechanical ventilation of 47 (22 - 132) v. 20 (6 - 27) hours (p<0.0001).
CONCLUSION: There is a high prevalence of blood product use in children in the PICU following cardiac surgery, and this is associated with worse outcomes.
CONTRIBUTION OF THE STUDY: This is the first South African study to describe the use of all major blood product types, not only red blood cells, and their indications in children following paediatric cardiac surgery. It demonstrates a markedly different transfusion pattern from that reported in North American PICUs, with cryoprecipitate, rather than red blood cells, being the most frequently used product. Blood product use was common and was independently associated with worse outcomes, including longer PICU stays, prolonged ventilation and higher standardised mortality. These findings highlight the need for locally developed, evidence-based transfusion protocols to support blood product stewardship, particularly in resource-constrained settings that depend on voluntary blood donation.
articles.journal_full: The Southern African journal of critical care : the official journal of the Critical Care Society

articles.title: Lighting the Way: Joseph Cichon, Inaugural Emery N. Brown Award Recipient.
Surgery for Nonthymomatous Myasthenia Gravis.
articles.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by fluctuating muscle weakness due to impaired neuromuscular transmission, most commonly mediated by antibodies against the acetylcholine receptor. The thymus plays a central role in disease pathogenesis, and complete thymectomy including all thymic and mediastinal adipose tissue has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with nonthymomatous, antiacetylcholine receptor antibody positive generalized MG. Minimally invasive approaches, including video-assisted and robotic-assisted thymectomy, offer remission rates comparable to open surgery with reduced perioperative morbidity. Careful patient selection and perioperative disease optimization remain essential.

articles.title: Elevated electrical stimulation thresholds for sciatic nerve block in individuals with diabetic complications: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus is associated with peripheral nerve structural alterations, potentially affecting nerve excitability. Electrical stimulation threshold is a key parameter for nerve localization during sciatic nerve block. This meta-analysis investigates the impact of diabetes mellitus and its complications on this threshold.
METHODS: We systematically searched multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Database, from their inception to November 10, 2025, for studies comparing electrical stimulation thresholds during sciatic nerve block between diabetic and non-diabetic subjects. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the Newcastle‑Ottawa Scale (NOS). Data were pooled using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses were conducted by alternating effect models and sequentially excluding individual studies. Subgroup analyses were performed to explore potential sources of heterogeneity. In addition, trial sequential analysis (TSA) was applied to determine whether the sample size was sufficient and to assess statistical power. The quality of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.
RESULTS: Six studies involving 486 participants were included, all of which were of high quality according to the NOS. The pooled analysis demonstrated a significantly higher stimulation threshold in diabetic participants compared to controls (mean difference [MD] = 0.57 mA, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.22-0.91, P = 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 94%). Sensitivity analyses, including alternating effect models and sequential exclusion of individual studies, confirmed the robustness of these findings. Subgroup analysis identified the presence of diabetic complications (peripheral neuropathy or diabetic foot) as a significant source of heterogeneity (P = 0.02), while geographic region and puncture site were not associated with heterogeneity (P > 0.05). TSA indicated that the evidence was robust, with sufficient statistical power to support the conclusion. The result was supported by low evidence.
CONCLUSION: Diabetic complications, particularly peripheral neuropathy or diabetic foot, are associated with elevated electrical stimulation thresholds for sciatic nerve block. This suggests that procedural parameters may need adjustment in this patient subgroup to ensure accurate nerve localization.

articles.title: Bacteriological profiling and antimicrobial resistance of combat-related infections: analysis of war wounds from Ukraine during 2024-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combat-related wound infections in the Russo-Ukrainian war pose high morbidity due to the prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) organisms. The aim of the study was to characterize pathogen distribution, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dynamics, and risk factors (evacuation and sampling timing) with the intent to develop a prognostic model for resistance in wounded military personnel.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 203 patients with ballistic injuries treated at a Role 3 military hospital (Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine) was performed. Microbiological sampling yielded 685 unique strains. Isolates were categorized by year (2024 vs. 2025), sampling timing (≤ 48 h vs. > 48 h), and evacuation interval (< 72 h vs. ≥ 72 h). Susceptibility testing followed EUCAST v.14-15. Bacteriological profiling was made for Multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, Extensively Drug-Resistant (XDR), and Pan-drug-Resistant (PDR) microbes. Data was managed in WHONET Microbiology Laboratory Database Software (2025); statistical analyses used R and AMR packages. A supervised machine-learning workflow using a standard Random Forest algorithm was implemented to predict phenotypic resistance risk, with model performance evaluated by ROC-AUC analysis.
RESULTS: Gram-negative bacteria predominated, led by A. baumannii, K. pneumoniae, E. coli, and E. cloacae. Overall resistance rate was 51.2%. True patient-level carbapenem resistance was high in K. pneumoniae (imipenem 83.1%) and A. baumannii (imipenem 91.5%); colistin retained activity. Patient-corrected MDR prevalence significantly escalated from 72.9% in 2024 to 82.3% in 2025 (p = 0.022), confirming a deepening ecological resistance reservoir. Polymicrobial infections were common (93.6% of episodes), often including MDR/XDR pathogens. Resistance was highest in the early-evacuation/early-sampling (Groups 1, 73.6% MDR) and late-evacuation/late-sampling (Groups 4, 97.1% MDR) groups. Random Forest predicted resistance with an overall AUC = 0.718, demonstrating reliable performance specifically within high-volume cohorts (Groups 1 and 4).
CONCLUSIONS: Combat wounds demonstrate a severe burden of resistant Gram-negative pathogens with stationary chronological resistance plateaus linked to evacuation and sampling timelines. The rapid colonization kinetics observed during early transit continuum indicate that the institutional reservoir is pervasive across the evacuation network. The machine-learning model provides reliable automated risk stratification for high-volume echelons to optimize empirical selection, while early clinical management must prioritize aggressive surgical debridement and source control over premature antimicrobial escalation.

articles.title: Patient knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding postoperative patient-controlled analgesia: a cross-sectional study using structural equation modelling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postoperative pain management is crucial for recovery, and Patient-Controlled Analgesia (PCA) provides an important self-administration method for pain relief. However, inadequate understanding can hinder its optimal use. Therefore, this study aimed to explore patients' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding postoperative PCA.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among postoperative patients using a self-designed KAP questionnaire through a non-random, non-probability convenience sampling method at one hospital from September 12, 2023 to December 25, 2023. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analysis was conducted to examine the relationship between knowledge, attitude, and practice.
RESULTS: The study enrolled 451 participants, averaging 48.76 ± 15.87 years in age, with 42.35% utilizing intravenous PCA. The knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 9.10 ± 3.87 (out of 24), 19.02 ± 3.96 (out of 30), and 29.95 ± 7.24 (out of 50), respectively. SEM revealed a direct positive influence of knowledge on practice (β = 0.538, P = 0.012) and a direct negative influence of knowledge on attitude (β = -0.355, P = 0.009), with no significant direct effect of attitude on practice.
CONCLUSION: Patients demonstrated insufficient knowledge, negative attitudes, and suboptimal practices regarding postoperative PCA. The negative knowledge-attitude correlation may be attributed to a phenomenon of blind optimism or the bliss of ignorance, where patients with lower knowledge exhibit more favorable, albeit ungrounded, attitudes toward PCA. Additionally, the failure of attitudes to influence practice highlights that favorable beliefs alone cannot drive behavioral change without skill-building and systemic support. Despite single-center and convenience sampling limitations, these findings underscore the need for nuanced interventions addressing both psychological complexities and practical barriers to PCA use.

articles.title: MRI-derived lumbosacral cerebrospinal fluid volume influences both the extent and persistence of spinal anesthesia: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Considerable interindividual variability exists in the spread and duration of spinal anesthesia despite standardized anesthetic techniques. Lumbosacral cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) volume has been proposed as an important anatomical determinant of neuraxial block characteristics. However, its influence on clinically relevant outcomes beyond peak sensory block level remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between MRI-derived lumbosacral CSF volume and spinal anesthesia characteristics in patients undergoing elective lower extremity orthopedic surgery.
METHODS: Thirty-nine patients undergoing elective lower extremity orthopedic surgery under spinal anesthesia were prospectively evaluated. Lumbosacral CSF volume was measured using semi-automated segmentation of three-dimensional T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) datasets. Correlations between CSF volume and spinal block characteristics were assessed using Pearson or Spearman correlation analyses, as appropriate. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of peak sensory block level.
RESULTS: The mean lumbosacral CSF volume was 12.60 ± 5.16 cm³. Lower CSF volumes were significantly associated with higher peak sensory block levels (ρ = -0.475, p = 0.002), longer sensory block duration (ρ = -0.455, p = 0.006), longer motor block duration (ρ = -0.445, p = 0.007), prolonged two-segment regression time (ρ = -0.343, p = 0.015), and higher sensory block levels at 5 min (ρ = -0.483, p = 0.004). Height demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with CSF volume (ρ = 0.529, p < 0.01). In multivariable regression analysis, lumbosacral CSF volume was identified as the only independent predictor of peak sensory block level (β = -0.563, p < 0.001), explaining 31.7% of the observed variability (R² = 0.317).
CONCLUSION: MRI-derived lumbosacral CSF volume influences both the extent and persistence of spinal anesthesia. Lower CSF volumes were associated with greater cephalad sensory spread, prolonged sensory and motor blockade, and delayed regression. Furthermore, lumbosacral CSF volume emerged as the only independent predictor of peak sensory block level in multivariable analysis. These findings suggest that lumbosacral CSF volume is an important anatomical determinant of spinal anesthesia behavior and may contribute to future individualized neuraxial anesthetic planning.

articles.title: Tailored strategies for vitamin C, D, iron, and carnitine in critical illness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Micronutrients are essential cofactors for metabolic, immune, and cellular processes. Low plasma concentrations are frequent in ICU patients but poorly reflect tissue stores. Inflammation drives redistribution and utilisation, while disease, reduced intake, impaired absorption, dilution, and increased losses may contribute to true deficiency. Plasma values, therefore, cannot distinguish redistribution from deficiency, making individualised requirement estimation difficult. This narrative review focuses on four micronutrients of recent high interest, aiming to address some missing links in critical illness.
MAIN BODY: Current guidelines recommend routine provision of basal micronutrient requirements for all ICU patients, with additional monitoring and increased doses reserved for high-risk groups with losses. Plasma measurements, often the only available tool, should be interpreted alongside inflammatory markers, clinical context, and risk factors. Large RCTs of vitamin C have mainly yielded neutral or negative results, which may reflect unguided supplementation across heterogeneous populations without accounting for timing, duration, dosing strategies, and biochemical formulation variability; alternatively, vitamin C may simply be ineffective as an early intervention in critical illness. Available evidence from ICU vitamin D trials indicates signals of outcome benefit, but the evidence is heterogeneous and trial sizes are limited, preventing firm ICU-specific recommendations. Ongoing large trials are expected to clarify effects of high-dose strategies. Iron status spans a narrow therapeutic window: iron deficiency and anaemia are highly prevalent during and after ICU, yet iron overload and ferroptosis-related toxicity also contribute to organ dysfunction. Targeted, hepcidin-guided intravenous (I.V.) iron therapy appears promising to safely correct deficiency. Both carnitine deficiency and high blood levels are associated with worse outcomes in ICU patients. Risk factors for alterations in carnitine concentrations include CRRT, renal and hepatic dysfunction, valproate use, inflammation, and wound losses. Supplementation should be evaluated in a stepwise approach to detect potentially excessive levels in a dose-finding RCT.
CONCLUSION: New biomarkers and analytical approaches are needed to differentiate redistribution from deficiency, capturing dynamic changes over time. Future approaches should move beyond plasma measurements toward cellular and functional biomarkers that better reflect stores and biological activity. Given current limitations, testing should be selective to where results are expected to alter management, include CRP, and timing guided by underlying risk. Research should prioritise precision strategies with better biomarkers and longitudinal sampling to account for dynamic risk, needs, losses, and responses.

articles.title: Perioperative transient myoclonic state with asterixis in an elderly patient: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transient myoclonic state with asterixis (TMA) is characterized by repetitive, short-lived myoclonus without impaired consciousness disturbance. Herein, we report a case of an elderly man who developed TMA perioperatively.
CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his 80 s who was independent in activities of daily living underwent lumbar laminectomy under general anesthesia. Post-operatively, he emerged from anesthesia without any issues including neurological symptoms. On the night of postoperative day (POD) 1, he remained conscious, but developed acute dysarthria, finger tremor, and involuntary tremulous movements involving the face, neck, tongue, and bilateral upper extremities. Routine laboratory investigations and brain magnetic resonance imaging showed no abnormalities. He was diagnosed with TMA and responded well to oral clonazepam.
CONCLUSIONS: TMA should be recognized in the differential diagnosis of acute onset involuntary movements, particularly in patients after general anesthesia. Increased awareness of this condition is important to avoid misdiagnosis and unnecessary interventions and ensure appropriate management.

articles.title: Advancing evidence quality and reproducibility in endoscopic transorbital approach in neurosurgery research: a systematic review and reporting guideline for enhanced comparability.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the quality of studies reporting clinical and surgical outcomes of meningiomas and trigeminal schwannomas treated with the endoscopic transorbital approach (ETOA), and to develop a Reporting Guideline to enhance reproducibility, data pooling and comparability.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science up to July 2025. We included studies reporting patients with meningiomas or trigeminal schwannomas that were treated with ETOA. Reporting quality was assessed across nine domains: (1) patient baseline characteristics; (2) imaging methods and tumor features; (3) definitions of pivotal concepts; (4) neurosurgical/interventional team characteristics; (5) anesthetic protocol; (6) surgical procedure details; (7) clinical and procedural outcomes, including adverse events; (8) retreatment details; and (9) funding and conflicts of interest. Additionally, baseline characteristics of the included studies were extracted to contextualize our analysis.
RESULTS: Thirteen observational studies comprising 310 patients (81.6% meningiomas, 18.4% trigeminal schwannomas) were included. Critical appraisal revealed consistent shortcomings across all nine domains, highlighting major gaps in the current literature. The main gaps included the lack of reporting previous comorbidities, tumor classification, clear definitions of perioperative complications, morbidity, and mortality, as well as anesthesia related details. Additional gaps included limited reporting on symptom duration, elective versus emergency status, intraoperative and postoperative complications - particularly hemorrhage, mortality, and its underlying causes. Based on these findings, we developed the Endoscopic Transorbital Approach Reporting Guideline, comprising 70 items across the nine domains, designed to standardize reporting of surgical and clinical outcomes.
CONCLUSION: This systematic review revealed substantial methodological and reporting deficiencies, which undermine the reliability of current evidence and constrain the advancement of knowledge in this field. The proposed Reporting Guideline provides a structured framework to address these shortcomings and to improve transparency, reproducibility, and comparability in future research, ultimately strengthening the evidence base and improving patient care.

articles.title: Association of preoperative sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use with postoperative delirium and long-term cognitive decline in older adults: a target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium is an important postoperative neurocognitive complication associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes, particularly in older adults with type 2 diabetes. Current perioperative guidelines recommend withholding sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors 3-4 days before surgery to prevent euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis. We emulated a target trial to investigate whether recent preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with clinically coded postoperative delirium and subsequent cognitive diagnostic outcomes.
METHODS: Using the TriNetX global health research network, we identified adults aged ≥ 60 years with type 2 diabetes undergoing major operative procedures between January 2016 and December 2025. Applying a new-user design and 1:1 propensity score matching, we compared patients with recent preoperative prescriptions for SGLT2 inhibitors within 90 days preoperatively with matched non-users. The primary outcome was clinically coded postoperative delirium within 7 days. Secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality and long-term coded cognitive diagnostic outcomes.
RESULTS: The matched cohort included 126,190 patients (63,095 per group). SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a lower risk of clinically coded postoperative delirium compared with non-use (3.98% vs. 4.53%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.83-0.92; P < .001). Exploratory surgical-category analyses suggested that the association was more pronounced in cardiovascular and respiratory procedures than in several other surgical categories, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Long-term follow-up (> 5 years) revealed lower risks of subsequent coded delirium and coded cognitive diagnostic outcomes among SGLT2 inhibitor users. Findings were consistent across several sensitivity analyses and were supported by negative control analyses, although residual confounding cannot be excluded.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower risks of postoperative delirium and long-term cognitive outcomes in older adults with type 2 diabetes undergoing surgery. These findings identify a clinically important perioperative neurocognitive signal in a population increasingly exposed to SGLT2 inhibitors. Because residual confounding, exposure misclassification, and outcome underascertainment cannot be excluded, prospective studies with adjudicated exposure, standardized delirium assessment, and perioperative safety monitoring are needed.

articles.title: Association between perioperative blood transfusion and 30-day complications in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery: a cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Perioperative blood transfusion (PBT) is a common intervention in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. However, its association with postoperative complications remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PBT and 30-day complications in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted using the clinical database of a tertiary referral center for elderly patients (≥ 60 years) who underwent hip fracture surgery between December 1, 2021, and December 22, 2022. The primary outcome was the incidence of 30-day composite complications, including both major and minor complications following surgery. Multivariate logistic regression was used to assess the association between PBT and outcomes, and the adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals were calculated.
RESULTS: Of the 1,156 included patients (64.8% female; median age 76 years), the 30-day composite complications rates were 36.6% (260 patients) in the PBT group and 23.6% (105 patients) in the non-transfusion group (P < 0.001). In multivariate models, an increased risk of 30-day composite complications in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery was significantly associated with PBT (preoperative only: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.946; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.519-5.716; intraoperative or postoperative only: aOR, 2.499; 95% CI, 1.421-4.394; preoperative and intraoperative or postoperative: aOR, 2.436; 95% CI, 1.324-4.483) compared to patients without transfusions.
CONCLUSION: Among elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, PBT is observed to be associated with an increased risk of 30-day composite complications, and the timing of preoperative transfusion may represent a period of heightened risk.

articles.title: Admission body mass index categories and short-term mortality in critically ill adults: a retrospective cohort study using Asian-oriented cut points.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Admission body mass index (BMI) is routinely available in intensive care, but BMI-mortality associations are difficult to interpret because BMI may reflect adiposity, nutritional reserve, sarcopenia, fluid status, illness severity, and selection processes. We evaluated admission BMI category in relation to in-hospital mortality and intensive care unit (ICU) mortality in critically ill adults using Asian-oriented BMI cut points.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adult ICU admissions from 2018 to 2020. BMI was categorized using Asian-oriented cut points as < 18.5, 18.5-23.9, 24.0-26.9, and > = 27.0 kg/m². The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; ICU mortality was secondary. Multivariable logistic regression with patient-level cluster-robust standard errors adjusted for age, sex, APACHE II score, ICU type, admission source, and selected comorbidities. A conceptual directed acyclic graph was added to clarify the assumed covariate structure and to guide interpretation of the adjusted associations.
RESULTS: Among 16,692 ICU admissions, BMI was available for 11,923/16,692 (71.4%). Adjusted analyses included 11,450/11,923 admissions (96.0%) for in-hospital mortality and 11,379/11,923 admissions (95.4%) for ICU mortality. In-hospital mortality was 22.8% (314/1,376), 15.8% (747/4,729), 12.5% (352/2,806), and 9.4% (283/3,012) across increasing BMI categories. Compared with normal BMI, adjusted odds ratios for in-hospital mortality were 1.31 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.62; p = 0.011) for underweight, 0.79 (95% CI 0.66-0.95; p = 0.012) for overweight, and 0.61 (95% CI 0.50-0.74; p < 0.001) for obesity. Obesity was also associated with lower ICU mortality (adjusted odds ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.58-0.90; p = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: Admission BMI category was associated with short-term mortality in this cohort. The findings should be interpreted as adjusted associations rather than evidence that higher BMI is causally protective. The substantial proportion of missing BMI data, uncertainty around anthropometric measurement, and residual confounding limit causal interpretation.

articles.title: Risk factors and a perioperative prediction model for postreperfusion syndrome in donation after circulatory death liver transplantation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postreperfusion syndrome (PRS) is a common and clinically important complication during liver transplantation. It is characterized by marked hemodynamic instability after graft reperfusion and has been associated with adverse perioperative outcomes. However, perioperative factors associated with PRS in donation after circulatory death (DCD) liver transplantation remain incompletely defined, and clinically applicable prediction tools are limited. This study aimed to identify perioperative factors associated with PRS, develop an internally validated prediction model, and explore the relationship between PRS and postoperative outcomes.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult recipients who underwent orthotopic liver transplantation using DCD grafts at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University between January 2016 and May 2025. PRS was defined as a decrease in mean arterial pressure of at least 30% from the prereperfusion baseline within 5 min after reperfusion, lasting for at least 1 min. Prespecified donor-, recipient-, and intraoperative variables were screened, and a limited number of clinically plausible candidate predictors were entered into multivariable logistic regression to reduce the risk of overfitting. A nomogram was constructed from the final model. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap internal validation. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression were used to explore the association between PRS and long-term outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 430 eligible recipients, 82 developed PRS, yielding an incidence of 19.1%. Multivariable analysis identified donor age ≥ 40 years (OR 3.54, 95% CI 1.65-7.59; P = 0.001), donor ALT ≥ 200 U/L (OR 3.96, 95% CI 1.66-9.46; P = 0.002), hepatic encephalopathy (OR 3.90, 95% CI 1.48-10.27; P = 0.006), severe thrombocytopenia (≤ 30 × 109/L) (OR 3.34, 95% CI 1.34-8.37; P = 0.010), and higher prereperfusion norepinephrine infusion rate (OR 1.12 per 0.1 µg/kg/min increase, 95% CI 1.01-1.24; P = 0.031) as independent factors associated with PRS. The model showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.736, 95% CI 0.668-0.804) and reasonable calibration; the optimism-corrected C-index after bootstrap validation was 0.64. Patients with PRS had greater intraoperative blood loss and transfusion requirements, higher postoperative NT-proBNP, serum creatinine, and bilirubin levels, longer ICU stay and mechanical ventilation duration, and higher rates of early allograft dysfunction and acute kidney injury (all P < 0.05). PRS was also associated with higher mortality in the overall cohort (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.08-2.23; P = 0.02). In subgroup analyses, this association was more evident in recipients with non-malignant liver disease than in those with hepatocellular carcinoma.
CONCLUSIONS: In DCD liver transplantation, older donor age, elevated donor ALT, hepatic encephalopathy, severe thrombocytopenia, and greater prereperfusion norepinephrine requirement were independently associated with PRS. The proposed model may serve as an internally developed perioperative risk-stratification tool, although further external validation is needed. PRS was associated with worse perioperative outcomes, and its relationship with long-term survival appeared to vary across recipient subgroups.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction model of transition from acute kidney injury to acute kidney disease after liver transplantation: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to acute kidney disease (AKD) is a frequent sequela after liver transplantation (LT), associated with increased short-term mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and increased likelihood of progression to chronic kidney disease. Early identification of high-risk patients remains a critical unmet need. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based model for early prediction of AKI-to-AKD transition after LT.
METHODS: Patients who underwent LT and developed postoperative AKI between January 2019 and December 2022 were enrolled as the development cohort (n = 359), randomly allocated into a training set and an internal validation set. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated to construct prediction models. All models were subsequently assessed in a temporal validation cohort in the same medical center (n = 104 from January 2024 to December 2025). The Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. An online risk calculator was developed based on the final model.
RESULTS: The incidence of postoperative AKD in the training set was 57.1%. AKD progression was associated with 8 predictors: postoperative day 7 blood urea nitrogen (BUN), preoperative serum creatinine (Scr), postoperative day 7 sodium, calcineurin inhibitor overexposure, imipenem/cilastatin use, amphotericin B use, sex, and cefoperazone/sulbactam use. The logistic regression model demonstrated the best overall performance, with an AUC of 0.805 in the internal validation cohort and 0.809 in the temporal validation cohort, with good calibration. SHAP analysis indicated that postoperative BUN, preoperative Scr, and postoperative sodium were the most influential predictors. Decision curve analysis demonstrated net clinical benefit.
CONCLUSION: This study developed and temporally validated an interpretable predictive model for AKI-to-AKD transition after LT, which can facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and guide individualized nephroprotective strategies.

articles.title: Quality of postoperative recovery in patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection as affected by transversus abdominis plane block combined with moderate neuromuscular blockade: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery quality in laparoscopic surgery may benefit from deep neuromuscular blockade, whereas the effects of combining transversus abdominis plane block (TAPB) with moderate neuromuscular blockade in this regard remain unreported. This work investigated whether moderate neuromuscular blockade differs from deep neuromuscular blockade in terms of postoperative recovery quality in patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery with routine TAPB, to provide evidence-based support for optimizing perioperative neuromuscular blockade strategies.
METHODS: 110 patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery were randomized to moderate (train-of-four count 1-2) or deep (post-tetanic count 1-2) neuromuscular block, with both groups undergoing TAPB. The primary outcome was recovery quality assessed by the Quality of Recovery-40 (QoR-40) on postoperative day 1 (POD1).
RESULTS: No statistically significant between-group differences in mean POD1 QoR-40 scores were found (172.18 ± 6.78 vs. 172.51 ± 6.89; 95% CI - 2.91 to 2.26; P = 0.802), with no significant differences across the scale's five subdomains.
CONCLUSIONS: During TAPB application for laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection, no clinically meaningful differences in postoperative recovery quality were identified between moderate and deep neuromuscular blockade.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500103278, registered 27 May 2025.

articles.title: Back to bedside: reflections on how we diagnose neuropathic pain.
Comparison of gasping breaths induced by three commonly used volatile anesthetics in mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies showed that administration of inhaled 2-MAC sevoflurane induces gasping in mice by activating a persistent sodium current in the brainstem, an effect blocked by riluzole. However, whether other commonly used volatile anesthetics elicit a similar gasping response in mice has not previously been investigated. This study compared respiratory responses to high doses of three volatile anesthetics.
METHODS: Seven spontaneously breathing adult mice each inhaled one of three anesthetics (sevoflurane, isoflurane, and desflurane) on separate days, and eventually inhaled all three anesthetics. Each anesthetic concentration was increased from 1 MAC to inhaled 2-MAC, while breathing patterns and suprahyoid muscle electromyographic activity (EMGSH) were measured. The effects of riluzole (18 mg/kg, i.p.) on gasping were also tested in five additional mice anesthetized with desflurane and/or isoflurane.
RESULTS: All three inhaled anesthetics altered the respiratory pattern from eupnea in 1 MAC to gasping in inhaled 2-MAC in seven mice. However, the time course of ventilation and EMGSH responses to volatile anesthetics at inhaled 2-MAC differed significantly among the three agents: desflurane had the strongest inhibitory effect on inspiratory and EMGSH activities, isoflurane had the weakest inhibitory effects and promoted stable gasping, and sevoflurane showed an intermediate effect. In addition, riluzole administration eliminated isoflurane- and desflurane-induced gasping in five mice.
CONCLUSION: All three anesthetics produced a similar gasping response at inhaled 2-MAC; however, the response's time course and the mechanism by which stable gasping was maintained depend heavily on the volatile anesthetic used.

articles.title: Perioperative factors associated with postoperative continuation of mechanical ventilation after initial burn surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Early surgical intervention, including debridement and grafting, is crucial in acute burn injury management. Although early extubation in operating rooms (ORs) reduces intensive care unit length of stay and ventilator-associated complications, extubation feasibility following initial burn surgery remains uncertain. We investigated perioperative factors associated with postoperative continuation of mechanical ventilation (MV) after initial burn surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed patients with burns who underwent acute-phase debridement between 2018 and 2024. Patients requiring postoperative MV were compared with those extubated in ORs. Factors independently associated with postoperative MV were identified using multivariate logistic regression analysis.
RESULTS: Among 418 patients, 75 required postoperative MV. Age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.03, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.00-1.06), percentage of total body surface area (%TBSA) burned (aOR = 1.08, 95% CI 1.03-1.12), preoperative intubation (aOR = 11.8, 95% CI 3.02-46.4), intraoperative fluid administration volume (ml/kg) (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and intraoperative maximum vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) (aOR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.10-1.26) were independently associated with postoperative MV continuation. This association between the intraoperative maximum VIS and postoperative MV continuation was maintained in the sensitivity analysis excluding preoperatively intubated patients (aOR = 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.25).
CONCLUSION: Age, %TBSA burned, preoperative intubation, intraoperative fluid administration volume, and maximum intraoperative VIS were independently associated with postoperative continuation of MV after initial burn surgery. Maximum intraoperative VIS may provide additional information regarding the hemodynamic component of perioperative severity by quantifying the intensity of vasoactive and inotropic support required during surgery.

articles.title: Professionalism and leadership in obstetric anesthesia: from ethical practice to teamwork.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To examine how professionalism and leadership support safe, respectful obstetric anesthesia and clarify the contribution and limitations of the proposed Integrated Professionalism-Leadership Framework for Obstetric Anesthesia (IPL-OA).
RECENT FINDINGS: Professionalism increasingly encompasses organizational responsibilities alongside individual conduct. Obstetric anesthesia guidance emphasizes maternal autonomy, response to pain, and continuity of care. Teamwork and simulation literature supports communication and coordination, although evidence directly linking leadership interventions to improved maternal outcomes remains limited. Consensus recommendations, observational associations, and intervention findings, therefore, require different interpretations. IPL-OA connects six domains across clinician, team, unit, and institutional levels. Its proposed contribution is a specialty-specific mapping of ethical commitments to observable actions, enabling resources, accountable owners, and candidate measures. An illustrative pathway for inadequate neuraxial anesthesia during cesarean delivery demonstrates this mapping without presenting patient data or observed improvement.
SUMMARY: IPL-OA is an unvalidated implementation proposal that complements existing competency, high reliability, and clinical frameworks. Its evaluation should establish feasibility and measurement reliability before testing added benefit over existing care. Patient experience, equity, workforce conditions, and unintended effects should accompany clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Validation of weight-based formulae for estimating paediatric epidural depth.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Accurate prediction of epidural depth in children enhances procedural success and safety in regional anaesthesia. Multiple weight-based formulae exist, yet comparative validation using both actual procedural and imaging data is limited. We aimed to evaluate and identify the most reliable formulae for estimating lumbar and thoracic epidural depth in paediatric patients using retrospective needle depth and prospective ultrasound measurements.
METHODS: Seven published formulae were applied to a retrospective cohort (n = 140) with recorded needle depth at 'loss of resistance' and a prospective cohort (n = 70) with ultrasound-measured posterior dura depth. Performance was assessed using goodness-of-fit statistics adjusted for age, mean absolute error (MAE), the proportions of estimates within ±0.5 cm and ±1.0 cm of the measured depth, and Bland-Altman agreement analyses.
RESULTS: For lumbar epidurals, Hasan's formula (Depth = 0.8 + 0.05 × weight in kg) demonstrated the best fit across both measurement methods, yielding a MAE of 0.16-0.26 cm, with 88.7%-95.7% of predictions within ±0.5 cm and up to 98.6% within ±1.0 cm. For thoracic epidurals, Wong's formula (Depth = 1.06 + 0.067 × weight in kg) showed the strongest correlation, with a MAE of 0.21-0.33 cm and up to 92.9% of estimates within ±0.5 cm.
CONCLUSION: These two formulae provide bedside estimates of dura depth in paediatric patients with clinically acceptable accuracy and may support pre-procedural planning, although their clinical impact on complication rates and procedure time requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Electroencephalography-derived spectral edge frequency 95 targets in toddlers under propofol anaesthesia✰.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proprietary processed EEG indices are less accurate in young children. We evaluated spectral edge frequency 95 (SEF95), a nonproprietary EEG index representing the frequency below which 95% of total EEG power resides, to establish target thresholds for varying anaesthetic depths during propofol anaesthesia in toddlers. Secondary objectives were to assess the relationship between SEF95 and plasma propofol concentration, and to evaluate airway reactivity during laryngoscopy.
METHODS: In this prospective study of toddlers aged 13 to 24 months, Dixon's up-and-down method and centred isotonic regression were used to determine the SEF95 targets for 50% (ED50) and 90% (ED90) probability of nonresponse to three clinical stimuli: pacifier placement (assessing consciousness), electrical nerve stimulation (nociception), and laryngoscopy (intubation readiness). Linear mixed-effects regression was used to analyse the association between plasma propofol concentration and SEF95.
RESULTS: Among 51 toddlers, SEF95 ED50 and ED90 targets (Hz) were 21.8 (90% CI 20.8-23.4) and 20.3 (19.1-20.7) Hz for pacifier placement, 12.0 (10.8-18.3) and 10.4 (8.7-11.3) Hz for electrical stimulation, and 10.3 (4.6-11.8) and 4.4 (1.5-5.4) Hz for laryngoscopy. Each 1 Hz increase in SEF95 corresponded to a 0.21 μg ml-1 decrease in plasma propofol (r=0.46, P<0.001), as described by the equation: plasma propofol concentration (μg ml-1)=5.80-0.21×SEF95 (Hz).
CONCLUSIONS: This study defined EEG SEF95 targets for loss of consciousness, response to noxious stimuli, and intubation readiness in toddlers aged 13 to 24 months. When combined with existing infant data, these age-specific SEF95 targets can optimise propofol titration and dosing accuracy during EEG-guided propofol anaesthesia in patients aged <2 yr.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05701748. Registered 17 January 2023; PI: Ian Yuan.

articles.title: Sugammadex versus neostigmine in adults aged 60 years and older undergoing surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of postoperative recovery and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncertainty remains regarding the clinical advantages of sugammadex over neostigmine in older adults, particularly for recovery efficiency and postoperative outcomes.
AIM: To compare the effects of sugammadex versus neostigmine on postoperative recovery and clinical outcomes in adults aged 60 years and older undergoing surgery.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis included eight randomized controlled trials. The primary outcome was postoperative residual neuromuscular blockade (PRNB). Secondary outcomes included post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, time to extubation, hypoxemia, pneumonia, and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). Effect measures were risk ratio and mean difference.
RESULTS: A total of 851 participants were included, and 50.2% received sugammadex. Sugammadex was associated with a lower risk of PRNB (RR 0.34 [95% CI: 0.18; 0.64]; p < 0.001; I² = 54%), with moderate between-study heterogeneity; however, the 95% prediction interval (0.11; 1.03) included the null value. Sugammadex significantly reduced PACU length of stay (MD -8.84 [95% CI: -12.18; -5.51], p < 0.001, I2 = 0%), hospital length of stay (MD -1.12 [95% CI: -2.01; -0.24], p < 0.01, I2 = 16%), and hypoxemia (RR = 0.61 [95% CI: 0.38; 0.97]; p = 0.04, I2 = 0%). No statistically significant differences were observed for the remaining outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Sugammadex was associated with a lower risk of PRNB and shorter PACU stays compared with neostigmine. Although the primary analyses suggested reductions in hypoxemia and hospital length of stay, these associations were not statistically significant after the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. INTERNATIONAL PROSPECTIVE REGISTER OF SYSTEMATIC REVIEWS (PROSPERO): CRD420261376045.

articles.title: Empiric Antifungal Therapy in Critically Ill Patients Undergoing Surgery for Severe Intra-Abdominal Infection: a Large Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-abdominal candidiasis is frequent in critically ill surgical patients and is associated with high mortality. Whether empiric antifungal therapy improves outcomes after surgery for intra-abdominal infection (IAI) in critically ill patients remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center data warehouse-based cohort study of 1,061 adults admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) after surgery for IAI between 2018 and 2024. Patients who received systemic antifungal therapy within 24 hours after surgery were compared with those who did not. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were day-5 renal dysfunction, assessed by the renal SOFA component and the creatinine-based KDIGO stage, and the need for surgical reintervention. Adjusted analyses used propensity-score overlap weighting. Prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses used a Peritonitis Score ≥3, the identification of at least one organism in peritoneal samples, and a yeast-positive peritoneal sample.
RESULTS: Empiric antifungal therapy was initiated in 46.0% of patients. Peritoneal sampling was available in 957 patients (90.2%); 21.4% had no organism identified and 25.2% had a yeast-positive sample. In adjusted analyses, empiric therapy was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality (OR 1.53, 95% CI 0.83-2.78), lower day-5 renal SOFA score, lower KDIGO stage, or fewer reinterventions. Findings were consistent in patients with Peritonitis Score ≥3, with at least one identified organism, and with a yeast-positive sample. ICU and hospital stays were longer in treated patients after weighting.
CONCLUSIONS: Empiric antifungal therapy initiated within 24 hours after surgery for severe IAI was not associated with improved short-term outcomes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NA.

articles.title: Monitoring of Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS) During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in the ICU: the MAVERIC pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous congestion is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of organ dysfunction during acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Although the Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) score is a promising bedside marker of systemic venous congestion, its dynamic evolution during CRRT remains unknown. We aimed to describe serial changes in VExUS during CRRT and explore their association with ultrafiltration intensity and fluid balance.
METHODS: MAVERIC was a prospective single-centre observational pilot study including adults undergoing CRRT for acute kidney injury. VExUS was assessed before CRRT initiation and after 24 and 48 hours. The primary objective was to describe temporal changes in VExUS using an alluvial plot. Patients were classified into three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution. Associations with net ultrafiltration (NUF) and cumulative fluid balance were explored.
RESULTS: Forty-seven patients were included. Overall, VExUS grades decreased significantly during the first 48 hours of CRRT (p = 0.0048). Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were identified: persistently low congestion (45%, n = 21), resolving congestion (32%, n = 15), and persistent or worsening congestion (23%, n = 11). Patients with resolving congestion had the highest NUF rates (1.35 [0.85-1.66] mL/kg/h) and the most negative cumulative fluid balance (-36.7 [-74.6 to -21.1] mL/kg), with significant differences across groups (p = 0.003 and p < 0.001, respectively). Patients with persistent or worsening congestion had lower NUF rates.
CONCLUSIONS: Serial VExUS assessment provides dynamic information on systemic venous congestion during CRRT. Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were associated with differences in net ultrafiltration and fluid balance. Serial VExUS monitoring may help identify patients with persistent or worsening congestion, raising the hypothesis that it could inform reassessment of decongestion strategies. Whether integrating serial VExUS assessment into individualised decongestive strategies improves renal outcomes should be evaluated in prospective interventional studies.

articles.title: Accuracy and Precision of Acceleromyography and Electromyography at the Adductor Pollicis Muscle in Restricted Thumb Movement Positions: An Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative neuromuscular monitoring commonly uses acceleromyography (AMG) or electromyography (EMG). Acceleromyography requires unrestricted thumb movement, whereas EMG is independent of thumb motion. We compared the accuracy and precision of AMG and EMG responses after patients' arms were immobilized during routine surgical positioning.
METHODS: Patients undergoing general anaesthesia without neuromuscular block were enrolled. EMG and AMG monitors were placed on contralateral arms, and both arms were tucked under surgical drapes. The monitors simultaneously recorded train-of-four ratio (TOFR) after ulnar nerve stimulation every minute. Accuracy was defined as TOFR variability from the expected baseline value (1.00), and precision as consistency of repeated measurements, quantified by the coefficient of repeatability (CR). Failed measurements were defined as the absence of valid quantitative TOFR values, displayed as "0" or "?". AMG TOFR values were normalized to patient-specific baseline TOFR measurements for secondary analyses.
RESULTS: Forty patients provided 3,733 TOFR measurements (1,879 EMG and 1,854 AMG). EMG was more accurate than AMG (mean EMG-AMG difference in absolute deviation from 1.0, -0.108; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.134 to -0.083; p < 0.001) and more precise, with a smaller CR (0.10 vs. 0.35; p < 0.001), including compared with normalized AMG (CR, 0.35). Device failure rate was lower with EMG than AMG (3.6% vs. 27.7%; p = 0.0003). Failures increased over time, particularly for AMG after approximately 45 minutes.
CONCLUSION: EMG provided more accurate and precise TOFR measurements than AMG, including normalized AMG, with fewer failures, supporting EMG-based monitoring when upper extremity mobility is restricted.
REGISTRATION: Clinical trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Database (Registration Number: NCT06805032, Principal investigator: J.R.R., date of registration January 28, 2025).

articles.title: Calm in Crisis: Lessons from My First Intraoperative Emergency.
Perioperative Right Heart Failure in Cardiac Surgery: Reply.
Rethinking the Responsible Adult Requirement after Ambulatory Anesthesia: Toward Risk-stratified Discharge.
articles.abstract: For decades, ambulatory anesthesia pathways have commonly required a "responsible adult" before discharge after sedation or anesthesia. In practice, this requirement may function as a binary eligibility criterion based on a patient's social circumstances. However, the empirical evidence evaluating discharge without an escort remains limited and derives largely from observational studies. This Focal Point argues that carefully selected low-risk patients should be studied within structured alternative discharge pathways that preserve safe transportation, communication, observation, and rescue capacity. Such pathways should not permit self-driving or unrestricted solo discharge. The aim is to determine whether postanesthesia safeguards can be matched more precisely to patient, anesthetic, procedural, recovery, transport, and postdischarge risk while preserving conventional adult support for patients whose clinical circumstances warrant it.

articles.title: I Told You So! Scientists Who Were Ridiculed, Exiled, and Imprisoned for Being Right.
Perioperative Right Heart Failure in Cardiac Surgery: Comment.
Advanced Heterotopic Pregnancy with Invasive Extrauterine Placentation.
Value of Magnetic Resonance Imaging before Cesarean Delivery in Klippel-Feil Syndrome.
Trends in Women Entering Anesthesiology and Other High-compensation Specialties Relative to the U.S. Doctor of Medicine Graduate Pipeline, 2010 to 2024.
Tegileridine versus Sufentanil for Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting after Gynecological Laparoscopic Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind Superiority Trial.
Evaluating the analgesic effectiveness of erector spinae plane block for patients undergoing cardiac surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Sex, Smoking Status, and Long-Term Outcomes After Lung Cancer Resection: An STS General Thoracic Surgery Database Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of lung cancer in women is increasing, yet the effect of smoking history on survival remains uncertain.
METHODS: Adults who underwent resection for non-small cell lung cancer (2015-2024), from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons database, were grouped by sex and smoking status. Outcomes were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and Cox models.
RESULTS: In total, 145,103 patients were identified (current or former smoker women: 65,650 [45.2%]; current or former smoker men: 55,912 [38.5%]; never-smoker women: 16,902 [11.7%]; never-smoker men: 6,639 [4.6%]. Median age was 69 years. Never-smoker women were more likely to be Asian, have clinical stage I disease, and have adenocarcinoma; they also had the lowest rates of 30-day mortality and major morbidity. Current or former smoker men had the highest complications rates. These findings persisted after risk adjustment. Longitudinal mortality data were available for 59,756 patients (57%). Five-year survival was 79% for never-smoker women, 70% for never-smoker men, 71% for current or former smoker women, and 58% for current or former smoker men. Risk-adjusted survival was longer in women versus men and in never-smokers versus current or former smokers for both sexes. Compared with never-smoker women, all-cause mortality risk was higher in current or former smoker women (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]=1.18 [95% confidence interval {CI},1.11-1.26]), never-smoker men (aHR=1.44[95% CI,1.30-1.60]), and current or former smoker men (aHR=1.71 [95% CI,1.59-1.84]).
CONCLUSIONS: Never-smoker women had the lowest perioperative risk and superior long-term survival, highlighting sex and smoking status as independent determinants of outcomes after lung cancer resection.

articles.title: Vagus nerve stimulation in a patient with bilateral cochlear implants: potential device interactions and clinical considerations.
articles.abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is one of the standard treatments for drug-resistant epilepsy, and cochlear implants (CIs) are one of the standard treatments for profound sensorineural hearing loss. However, case reports combining both CIs and VNS devices are extremely rare, and there is limited knowledge regarding interference between these devices and their safety. We report the case of a 13-year-old boy with drug-resistant epilepsy associated with congenital cytomegalovirus infection, who had previously undergone bilateral cochlear implantation. He presented with multiple seizure types and multifocal epileptogenic discharges on long-term video-electroencephalography. Despite polytherapy, the seizures persisted and VNS was introduced. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, with no device interference between the CIs and VNS. This case demonstrates that patients with bilateral CIs can safely undergo VNS implantation with appropriate perioperative management and postoperative follow-up.

articles.title: Influence of cerebrospinal fluid dynamics on aseptic bone flap resorption: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aseptic bone flap resorption (ABFR) remains a common complication after autologous cranioplasty following decompressive craniectomy (DC), with reported prevalences varying widely-often reported between 10% and 30%-likely due to inconsistent follow-up. Data on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics in pathogenesis of ABFR are scarce. Aim of the present study was therefore to identify potential risk factors, with a particular focus on CSF drainage procedures.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent DC followed by autologous cranioplasty from 2015 to 2022. We collected demographics, clinical details, perioperative variables, and CSF interventions. Univariate and multivariate analyses identified associations, with subgroup focus on patients completing structured follow-up.
RESULTS: ABFR was diagnosed in 39/259 patients (15.1%), resulting in 38/101 (37.6%) in the 6-months follow-up cohort. Changes in CSF dynamics such as preoperative lumbar CSF drainage (p = 0.035) were identified as a risk factor, whereas ventriculoperitoneal shunt pressure adjustment was not associated with an increased risk of ABFR. After differentiation of the direction of adjustment, pressure reduction was not associated with ABFR. Especially preoperative lumbar CSF drainage remains an independent risk factor (p = 0.023) in multivariate analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Without structured imaging follow-up, ABFR rates are likely underestimated. CSF dynamic alterations beyond shunt presence alone may represent a relevant risk factor for ABFR. Our findings emphasize that primary alloplastic cranioplasty could be considered in at least a subgroup of patients.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

articles.title: Surgical hyperlactataemia during resection of an intraventricular meningioma.
articles.abstract: We present the first documented case of intraoperative hyperlactataemia during a minimally invasive resection of an intraventricular meningioma. The phenomenon remains unstudied, which creates a significant gap in both neurosurgical knowledge and patient management during perioperative periods. This will therefore help neurosurgeons and anaesthesiologists to recognise intraoperative metabolic problems, which will lead to further research and the development of better methods to handle such situations.
articles.journal_full: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England

articles.title: Does gabapentin affect the incidence of postoperative delirium in a dose dependent pattern?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway for Colorectal Surgery (CRS) emphasizes opioid-sparing analgesia to reduce ileus and length of stay (LOS). Our hospital adopted gabapentin as part of postoperative analgesia for CRS. We evaluated the association between perioperative gabapentin use and postoperative delirium (POD).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,165 encounters of patients ≥65 years undergoing elective CRS between 04/2015-06/2023. Encounters requiring critical care, LOS>3 months, or readmissions were excluded. Delirium was identified using chart review, ICD codes and/or new antipsychotic use. Multivariate logistic regression compared delirium rates among three groups: No Gabapentin (NG), low dose (LG) and high dose (HG). Models adjusted for age, race, ethnicity, gender, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), etc. Subgroup analyses investigated delirium by age, gender, CCI.
RESULTS: 1,027 individuals were studied: 20.5% NG, 70.8% LG, and 8.7% HG. NG Individuals were older (75.5±7.2) than LG (74.2±6.7) or HG (72.7±6.6), while CCI (6.6±3.8) was similar across groups. The NG group had more patients with dementia (NG 14.2% vs LG 9.5%, p=0.05 vs HG 11.2%). A higher incidence of POD was noted in NG (34.6%) when compared with LG (25.3%, 1.74(1.22-2.47), adj. p=0.002) as well as HG (23.6%, p=0.06). Prior gabapentin exposure did not significantly impact the incidence of postoperative delirium (OR 1.33 (0.86-2.05)) when the cohort was compared based on prior gabapentin exposure.
CONCLUSION: The use of low dose gabapentin postoperatively is associated with lower incidence of delirium compared to absence of gabapentin. However, the absence of gabapentin in our study is a reflection of baseline vulnerability for delirium. Prior exposure to gabapentin had no influence on incident POD. Future prospective trials are required to address the factors to be considered when determining the optimal dosing of gabapentin in older surgical adults.

articles.title: The effect of two different interventions applied during the transfer of children to the operating room for circumcision on fear, anxiety, comfort and pain levels: Randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of an animal-assisted intervention and kaleidoscope on the fear, anxiety, comfort, and pain levels of children while transferring them to the operating room for circumcision surgery.
METHODS: This randomised controlled trial with pretest-posttest design included 96 children aged 7-10 years who were scheduled for circumcision surgery at the urology and paediatric surgery departments of a State Hospital and met the inclusion criteria (animal-assisted intervention group = 31, kaleidoscope group = 32, control group = 33). The interventions were administered while transferring them to the operating room. Data were collected using five tools: a Child Information Form, the Children's Fear Scale, the Children's Anxiety Meter-State, the Comfort Behaviors Checklist, and the Wong Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance, dependent samples t-test, and Bonferroni post-hoc test.
RESULTS: The posttest mean scores of CFS, CAMS, and FACES were significantly lower in the animal-assisted intervention and kaleidoscope groups than in the control group, while posttest CBC mean scores were significantly higher (p < 0.05). Both interventions alleviated their fear, anxiety, and pain and improved their comfort during the transfer. The animal-assisted intervention was more effective than the kaleidoscope intervention.
CONCLUSIONS: These interventions should be integrated into standard nursing practice for paediatric surgery, particularly during operating room transfer.
IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Integrating AAI and kaleidoscope interventions into paediatric perioperative nursing care may promote child-friendly practices and improve children's surgical experiences.

articles.title: Beyond Factor Levels: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Outcome and Bleeding Risk in Congenital Factor VII Deficiency.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCongenital factor VII (FVII) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive bleeding disorder with highly variable clinical expression. Pregnancy management is difficult because FVII activity may rise during gestation in heterozygous women, yet bleeding phenotype and peripartum outcomes correlate poorly with factor level.ObjectiveTo summarize published pregnancies in women with congenital FVII deficiency, clarify how FVII activity, bleeding history, delivery mode, hemostatic prophylaxis, and obstetric factors relate to maternal and neonatal outcomes, and review the reported efficacy and safety of available treatment options.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review with descriptive synthesis of published pregnancy cases. PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched from database inception, covering publications available through May 2026. Case reports and case series describing pregnancy outcomes in women with confirmed or presumed congenital FVII deficiency were included. Data were extracted on demographics, genotype or zygosity where reported, FVII activity, bleeding history, delivery mode, anesthesia, prophylaxis, estimated blood loss, thrombotic events, and neonatal outcomes.Bleeding outcomes were standardized using the contemporary ACOG definition of primary PPH, while other clinically significant obstetric bleeding was recorded separately using intervention-based criteria.ResultsForty-five pregnancies from 30 published reports (1992-2026) across 17 countries were identified. Delivery was vaginal in 23 cases and by cesarean section in 20 cases; one case involved medical termination and one did not specify the delivery mode. Severe deficiency (FVII <10%) was present in 27 cases. Among the published cases with evaluable prophylaxis status, hemostatic prophylaxis was administered in 32 of 44 pregnancies (73%). Five of 45 published pregnancies (11%) met contemporary criteria for primary PPH. Five additional cases had other clinically significant primary or peripartum bleeding requiring therapeutic intervention but did not meet contemporary PPH criteria. One source-reported PPH case could not be classified because blood-loss volume and hypovolemia were insufficiently reported. Secondary PPH and clinically significant antepartum hemorrhage occurred in one case each. Most bleeding episodes with a documented etiology were attributable to obstetric or surgical causes, including uterine atony, genital tract laceration, or placental abruption with disseminated intravascular coagulation. However, one recent undiagnosed case developed refractory postpartum hemorrhage after common obstetric causes were excluded, underscoring that coagulopathy may still be contributory.These proportions are descriptive of the published cases and should not be interpreted as population-based estimates of incidence or risk.Four pregnancies were complicated by either confirmed primary PPH or other clinically significant peripartum bleeding despite prophylactic rFVIIa, whereas several pregnancies in women with severe deficiency were managed without prophylaxis and without hemorrhage. These descriptive findings cannot establish prophylactic effectiveness because treatment indications, obstetric risk, and dosing varied across reports.Thrombotic events or thrombotic history were reported in two women. No neonatal hemorrhage was reported among 43 live births.ConclusionsFVII activity alone appears to be an unreliable predictor of peripartum bleeding in the published cases. Management should be individualized according to bleeding phenotype, third-trimester FVII activity, obstetric risk, delivery route, anesthesia requirements, and thrombotic risk. Delivery planning should include timely access to tranexamic acid and appropriate factor replacement when clinically indicated. Postpartum VTE prophylaxis should be individualized according to bleeding stability, thrombotic risk factors, delivery route, and exposure to rFVIIa. Current evidence is insufficient to support routine prophylactic rFVIIa, although it may be considered on a case-by-case basis when the perceived bleeding risk is high. These conclusions are based on heterogeneous case reports and small case series and should be interpreted accordingly.
articles.journal_full: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis

articles.title: Implementation of a spinal-induced hypotension management bundle for elective cesarean delivery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Spinal-induced hypotension (SIH) remains the most common complication associated with spinal anesthesia for cesarean delivery and may compromise maternal hemodynamic stability and uteroplacental perfusion. Evidence supports prophylactic vasopressor therapy, serotonin receptor antagonists, and optimized fluid management; however, these strategies are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. This quality improvement (QI) project evaluated the effect of a standardized SIH management bundle (SIHMB) on maternal hemodynamic outcomes.
METHODS: A prospective QI initiative was conducted in the obstetric operating suites of an academic medical center with a Level II trauma facility. Adult parturients undergoing elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia were included. The intervention bundle consisted of intravenous ondansetron 8 mg administered 5 to 10 minutes prior to spinal anesthesia, crystalloid co-loading with 1 L of fluid during spinal placement, and prophylactic phenylephrine infusion initiated at 0.5 mcg/kg per minute. Data were collected during 12-week preimplementation and postimplementation periods. Primary outcomes included incidence and severity of hypotension. Secondary outcomes included rescue vasopressor use, antiemetic administration, and bundle adherence. This QI project was reported in accordance with the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines for reporting QI initiatives.
RESULTS: A total of 242 patients were included (103 preimplementation, 139 postimplementation). Implementation of the SIHMB significantly reduced the incidence of hypotension from 46% to 32% (P = .024). Mean lowest systolic and diastolic blood pressures increased significantly following implementation. Rescue vasopressor administration decreased from 72% to 49% (P < .001). Utilization of prophylactic phenylephrine infusion increased from 32% to 62%.
CONCLUSION: Implementation of a standardized hemodynamic management bundle significantly improved maternal hemodynamic stability during cesarean delivery. Standardizing prophylactic strategies for SIH may enhance obstetric anesthesia safety and reduce reliance on reactive vasopressor therapy.

articles.title: Maximum dose recommendations for local anesthetics: a scoping review.
Baseline frailty severity and survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive mechanical ventilation in patients with sepsis: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty has been associated with adverse outcomes during mechanical ventilation (MV). We evaluated the association between frailty severity, assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), and survival to intensive care unit (ICU) discharge without ongoing invasive MV.
METHODS: We analyzed adults with sepsis enrolled in the prospective, multicenter Korean Sepsis Alliance registry between September 2019 and December 2023 who received invasive MV on ICU day 1. Patients with CFS 9 were excluded. The primary outcome was survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive MV. Frailty was defined as CFS 5-8 versus CFS 1-4 and was examined across increasing CFS severity using categorical and restricted cubic spline analyses. Mixed-effects logistic regression with a participating-center random intercept was adjusted for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, ICU day 1 Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, and infection site.
RESULTS: Among 2,204 patients, 1,458 (66.2%) had CFS 5-8. The primary outcome was achieved by 1,120 patients (50.8%); crude rates were 52.9% in patients with CFS 1-4 and 49.7% in those with CFS 5-8 (P = 0.152). Frailty was associated with lower adjusted odds of the primary outcome (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.73; 95% CI 0.59-0.90). Compared with CFS 1-4, the estimate for CFS 5 was close to the null (OR, 1.08; 95% CI 0.78-1.49), while the odds were lower for CFS 6, 7, and 8 (ORs, 0.68, 0.73, and 0.59, respectively; global P < 0.001). In spline analysis, the adjusted probability of the primary outcome decreased from 58.6% at CFS 1 to 43.3% at CFS 8 (P overall < 0.001; P for nonlinearity = 0.55). In pairwise analyses of ICU discharge status, frailty was associated with higher odds of survival with ongoing invasive MV versus survival without ongoing invasive MV (adjusted OR, 1.94; 95% CI 1.26-2.98); the corresponding estimate for ICU death versus survival without ongoing invasive MV was 1.22 (95% CI 0.97-1.53).
CONCLUSIONS: Among invasively ventilated patients with sepsis, baseline frailty was associated with lower adjusted odds of survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive MV. These findings support considering frailty severity when discussing recovery and care needs, but do not establish a treatment threshold or a causal effect of frailty.

articles.title: From evidence to bedside: A decade of critical care pharmacotherapy and implications for ICU training.
articles.abstract: Pharmacotherapy management is integral to the care of critically ill patients, yet decisions are frequently made in dynamic and uncertain conditions. Over the last decade, a series of large trials and shifts in understanding have reshaped how therapies are selected and applied in the intensive care unit (ICU), often challenging long-standing practices and refining established treatment strategies. This review examines influential studies and paradigm shifts across four major areas of ICU pharmacotherapy: respiratory failure and acute respiratory distress syndrome, infectious disease and antimicrobial therapy, hemodynamic management in sepsis and septic shock, and sedation and delirium. We highlight how emerging evidence led to pharmacotherapeutic evolution within each domain and identify common patterns across these domains supporting a movement toward individualized, context-dependent care and more deliberate use of pharmacologic therapies. For trainees, the last decade provides important lessons regarding application of pharmacotherapy in the ICU, including the need to integrate evidence interpretation with clinical judgement.

articles.title: Capillary refill time at the admission of trauma patients: A prospective, observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The early identification of tissue perfusion is a significant challenge in the management of severe trauma cases. Capillary refill time (CRT) is a simple clinical marker of peripheral perfusion. The objective of this study was to ascertain the correlation between CRT and serum lactate levels in patients with severe trauma.
METHODS: A prospective, single-center observational study was conducted in a 20-bed intensive care unit (ICU) of a level 1 trauma center between April 2025 and January 2026. Adult patients who were directly admitted to the ICU from the scene of the accident for severe trauma, as defined by an injury severity score above 15, were included in the study. The CRT and serum lactate were measured on admission to the ICU. The primary endpoint was the association between admission serum lactate and admission CRT ≥ 3 s (abnormal CRT). Secondary analyses included the correlation between CRT and serum lactate at admission and the association between CRT and duration of vasopressor exposure during the first 3 days. Multivariate linear regression was performed on logarithmically transformed serum lactate, adjusted for age, core body temperature, prehospital weight-adjusted fluid administration, prehospital use of norepinephrine and prehospital timing.
RESULTS: Of 627 patients screened, 196 were included in the analysis. The admission CRT was 2.4 [1.7-3.1] s with serum lactate level at 2.1 [1.3-3.4] mmol/L. Admission serum lactate did not differ significantly between the patients with abnormal CRT and those with normal CRT (2.6 [1.4-4.6] versus 1.9 [1.3-3.1] mmol/L; p = 0.07) while CRT and serum lactate levels were correlated (r = 0.33; p < 0.01). In multivariate analysis, continuous analysis of CRT was independently associated with serum lactate levels with a 15% increase in serum lactate per additional sec of CRT (95% CI 1.06-1.25; p < 0.01). Among patients with serum lactate >2 mmol/L, abnormal CRT was associated with longer vasopressor exposure at day 3 and increased ICU mortality.
